CPT Tutorial

title: CPT Resources
text:
Click here for the CPT Request Form once you have completed the CPT Tutorial.

**CPT FAQs:**

What are the requirements to do CPT?

In order to do CPT, the following requirements must be met:
1)  The practical training must be an integral part of an established curriculum AND
2)  The internship or job must be directly related to the student's major area of
study AND
3)  The practical training cannot be authorized solely for the purpose of employment
AND
4)  The internship, practicum, or practical training must be a graduation requirement
for all students in that major

Can I have two employers?

Yes, but you will have to complete two separate CPT applications. During spring and
fall semesters, you are still limited to part-time CPT (a total of 20 hours or less per week).  During the summer term, you can work
full-time (21 hours or more per week).

title: CPT Resources
text:
I’ve heard some schools allow “Day-1 CPT.” Does WSU do that?

Immigration regulations state that F-1 students are eligible for CPT after completing
one academic year of study in the U.S. The only exception allowing students to participate
sooner is for graduate programs that mandate immediate participation in an activity
requiring CPT authorization.

title: CPT Resources
text:
Inquiries about “Day-1 CPT” are usually received from students searching for a way
to extend their full-time employment authorization as they approach the end of their
OPT.  This cannot normally be achieved because WSU policy limits CPT to 20 hours per
week while classes are in session and because the student must engage in a full course
of study while approved for CPT.  A good general principle of CPT is to approach it
primarily from the curriculum perspective and secondarily from the employment perspective. 
The school curriculum and not the desire for employment should be the primary focus
during CPT.

I’ve heard of other schools allowing full-time CPT every semester.  Can I have full-time
CPT during fall or spring terms?

USCIS has general CPT rules, but every school has different CPT policies. At WSU,
CPT during fall and spring semesters is generally limited to 20 hours per week.

title: CPT Resources
text:
What if I’m doing an unpaid internship? Do I still need CPT?

Yes, USCIS has said that even unpaid internships require CPT authorization.

Does CPT take away from my OPT?

Part-time CPT and fewer than 12 months of full-time CPT should not affect OPT eligibility. 
Only if a student participates in a full year (365 days) of full-time CPT would OPT
eligibility be affected.

Can I do CPT related to my minor?

Immigration regulations require CPT to be related to your major field of study. CPT
cannot be authorized for a position related to your minor.

How long does it take to get CPT authorization?

CPT approval from start to finish will depend on how long it takes you to get the
required signatures on the CPT form, enroll in appropriate CPT course, and OIE processing
times.

I heard that every student gets to do a certain amount of full-time CPT. Is that true?

title: CPT Resources
text:
At WSU, full-time CPT is typically only authorized during summer terms and over the
winter break, though some exceptions may exist for academic reasons.  Guaranteeing
a certain amount of full-time CPT may be the policy at some schools, but not at WSU.

I want to do full-time CPT in my final term because I only have one class to take.
Can I do that?

The number of hours you are allowed to work is not based on your course load. At WSU,
CPT during fall and spring semesters is generally limited to 20 hours per week.

How early can I request a CPT form?

While students cannot begin participating in CPT until they meet the one academic
year eligibility requirement, they can start the process of obtaining a CPT application
in advance.

title: Immigration Status Violations
text:
# Immigration Status Violations

# Immigration Status Violations

Violating your immigration status (also commonly called "going out-of-status") while
in the U.S. can have serious, long-lasting, and expensive consequences for a student.

**Termination of SEVIS Records**
There are several reasons why an International Student Advisor might be required to
terminate your SEVIS record.  These reasons include:

- Failure to enroll in a full course of study by the SEVIS registration deadline
- Dropping below a full course of study or withdrawing from all of your classes before
receiving authorization from ISS
- Enrolling in too many online classes
- Being expelled or suspended
- Working without authorization
- Failing to report OPT employment
- Accruing more than 90 days of unemployment while on OPT
- Failing to report to ISS after initially arriving in the U.S.

title: Immigration Status Violations
text:
**Consequences of Being Terminated in SEVIS**
If you are terminated in SEVIS, you:

title: Immigration Status Violations
text:
- Cannot work.  If you are currently employed on campus, you must quit your job.
- Cannot do Curricular Practical Training (CPT)
- Cannot do Optional Practical Training (OPT)
- Cannot get a driver's license (or renew a driver's license) or obtain a Social Security
Card
- May not be accepted for transfer by another school
- Can be subject to arrest or deportation
- Can accrue illegal presence in the U.S.  If you have more than 180 days of unlawful
presence in the U.S., you can be barred from re-entry for 3 years.  If you have more
than one year of unlawful presence in the U.S., you can be barred for 10 years.
- Must immediately leave the U.S. unless you apply for reinstatement.  There isn't a
30 or 60-day grace period to leave the U.S. after your SEVIS record is terminated.
- May spend a lot of time and money to get back into status without any guarantee of
success.  Students typically only have two options to get back into status:  1) Travel
outside the United States and re-enter with a new I-20 and new SEVIS ID, or 2) Apply
for reinstatement through USCIS, which can often take longer than one year for adjudication.
 Both of these options have risks and are not guaranteed to work.

title: Immigration Status Violations
text: If you have questions or concerns about your immigration status, please contact International Student Services for assistance.

title: Tips for Evaluating Positions
text:
# Tips for Evaluating Positions

##

# Tips and Guidelines for Evaluating Positions

Along with the student provided information, a determination may be made following
the NACE guidelines:

title: Tips for Evaluating Positions
text:
1. The experience must be an extension of the classroom: a learning experience that provides
for applying the knowledge gained in the classroom. It must not be simply to advance
the operations of the employer or be the work that a regular employee would routinely
perform.
2. The skills or knowledge learned must be transferable to other employment settings.
3. The experience has a defined beginning and end, and a job description with desired
qualifications.
4. There are clearly defined learning objectives/goals related to the professional goals
of the student’s academic coursework.
5. There is supervision by a professional with expertise and educational and/or professional
background in the field of the experience. \*\*\* The supervisor or mentor must have
more knowledge in the field than student.
6. There is routine feedback by the experienced supervisor.
7. There are resources, equipment, and facilities provided by the host employer that
support learning objectives/goals and a designated work area.

title: Tips for Evaluating Positions
text:
The student internship position may be denied if the employer criteria below are in
question:

title: Tips for Evaluating Positions
text:
1. Employer requirement of significant personal funding by student to either obtain position
or acquire training for a position
2. Employer requirement that a student provide personal information such as bank account
and social security numbers during the application process
3. The posting is for a “pay to play” type of position, i.e., the applicant provides
payment to a company to obtain a position with the guarantee of future income
4. A simple search suggests the email address associated with the posting is not associated
with the actual business one site that can help with this is:   www.scam-detector.com/job-scams
5. The employer does not provide a business address but merely provides personal contact
information
6. Failure to follow Federal EEO compliance guidelines
7. Use of non-specific email address as contact (i.e., “@hotmail” or “@gmail”)
8. Submission of unclear and/or questionable job duties
9. Offer of no salary unless student recruits others to participate (pyramid)
10. Use of private residence as an office or student work site
11. Receipt of complaints relevant to the program by students, alumni and/or staff

title: Tips for Evaluating Positions
text:
\*Information provided in part by the National Association of Colleges and Employers,
11.15.2021

title: Duration of Status FAQs
text:
# Duration of Status FAQs

#

# Duration of Status FAQs

What is Duration of Status? What is changing?

Historically, whenever students and exchange visitors entered the U.S., a Duration
of Status (or "D/S")  admission allowed them to remain in the U.S. indefinitely as
long as they were pursuing a full course of study.  **Due to a new federal rule, this will change for all students who enter the U.S. on
or after September 15.**  Any student who enters the U.S. on or after September 15 will be subject to the
new rule regardless of how many years they may have studied in the U.S. previously.

How will students who are already in the U.S. be affected when the new rule takes
effect?

title: Duration of Status FAQs
text:
- Students who are currently in the U.S. (and do not travel abroad) will not be significantly
affected when the new rule takes effect on September 15. Current students will be
allowed to remain in the U.S. until the Program End Date listed on their I-20 or up
to 4 years, whichever is shorter.
- Students will not be required to file an Extension of Stay (EOS) when applying for
OPT or STEM OPT for the first six months after the rule takes effect.
- Students who complete a program after September 15 will not be allowed to pursue another
program of study at the same or lower educational level. Students may only go up the
educational ladder (e.g. bachelor's to master's).

What happens if a student enters the U.S. after the new rule takes effect on September
15?

title: Duration of Status FAQs
text:
- Students will be given a fixed "Admit Until Date" (AUD) on their I-94 at their port-of-entry
in the U.S. Students will be admitted for the length of their program as listed on
their I-20 (up to a maximum of 4 years plus a 30-day grace period).
- If a student is in a program that typically requires longer than 4 years, the student
will be required to either 1) File an Extension of Stay (EOS) in order to complete
the program or 2) Leave the U.S. and re-enter to receive a new AUD.
- Students who submit a timely filed Extension of Stay may continue to work for up to
240 days. After 240 days, all employment must cease until the EOS has been adjudicated
by USCIS.
- The grace period to leave the U.S. after finishing a program will decrease from 60
days to 30 days.
- Students may only begin a new program at a higher educational level.
- Graduate students will not be allowed to change majors or transfer to another school.
- Undergraduate and Intensive English students will not be allowed to change majors
or educational objectives during their first academic year of study.  After the federal
rule takes effect, students must understand that they will be required to study in
the major or program listed on their I-20 for one academic year  before any program
or major changes can be made.
- Undergraduate and Intensive English students must complete their first academic year
of study at the school that initially issued their I-20. Transfers within the first
academic year will not be permitted.
- Students in English language will be limited to a maximum of 24 months.
- Students filing for OPT or STEM OPT during the first six months after the rule becomes
effective will not be immediately required to simultaenously file an Extension of
Stay (EOS).
- If a student stays in the U.S. beyond the specified Admit Until Date (AUD) listed
on their I-94, they will begin accruing unlawful presence in the U.S. A foreign national
who has been unlawfully present for more than 180 days but less than one year may
receive a 3-year bar on departure.  Those unlawfully present for one year or more
are barred from reentry for ten years.  Any person who is subject to a reentry bar
is also ineligible to apply for a visa, enter the U.S. for any purpose, or adjust
their immigration status to permanent residence unless they are granted a waiver of
inadmissibility or another form of relief.

# Packing List for International Students

## What to Pack as an International Student

***IMPORTANT: Please check with your airlines about the checked baggage weight limit
and carry on size allowed.***

**CHECKED BAGGAGE**

**Clothes (quantity depends on laundry habits)**

- Short sleeves, long sleeves, T-shirts
- Shorts, skirts, pants (slacks, khakis), jeans
- Sweaters, light jackets, blazers, coats, down coats
- Suits, dress shirts/pants (1-2 sets)
- Cultural costumes (1-2 sets)
- Sportswear, swimsuit
- Pajamas, underwear
- Socks
- Warm hat, scarf, gloves
- Sneakers, casual shoes, sandals, flip flops
- Dress shoes

**Bedding**

- Comforter/blanket/throw
- Pillow (optional)
- Sheets, pillowcases

**Bathroom/Personal Care**

title: Packing List for International Students
text:
- Bath towels, hand towels
- Comb, nail clippers, toothbrush,  small toothpaste, dental floss
- Traveler-size shampoo, conditioner, shower soap
- Skincare products, cosmetics

**Daily Necessities**

- Eyeglasses/contact lenses (with spare ones), sunglasses
- Contact lens solution
- Personal medicines
- A bowl, plate, one set of silverware, a cup/glass
- A few hangers

**Food**

- Snacks, cookies/crackers
- Dried condiments/spices, tea  (meat products not allowed)

**School Supplies**

- Schoolbag/backpack or tote bag
- Pencil case
- Ball pen, mechanical pencils, lead refills, highlighters

**Other**

- Cultural products, souvenirs

CARRY-ON

**Important Documents**

title: Packing List for International Students
text:
- Passport
- Itinerary
- Boarding pass
- I-20 and all admission documents
- High school transcripts, graduation certificate
- University transcripts, graduation certificate (transfer students or graduate students)
- Other academic credentials and application materials

**Cash**

- USD$1,000-1,500; keep $100-200 in wallet, have $10s & $20s; keep $50/$100 bills separately

**Electronics**

- Cell phone, charger and cable
- Laptop/tablet, charger and cable
- Converter/adapter
- Portable charger/power bank
- Headphone/earphone
- USB flash drive

**Other**

title: Packing List for International Students
text:
- Pens (1-2 for filling out forms)
- Small notepad (keeps school address, important contact information, etc.)
- Snacks/cookies (meat products not allowed)
- Chewing gum (bad breath after long flight; reduces earaches on airplane)
- Hand/body lotion (aircraft cabin is dry)
- Eye-drops (eyes dry after long flight)
- Slippers/flip flops (some people have swollen feet during a flight; convenient to
take off at security checkpoints)
- A pair of socks (it may be cold on the plane)
- Light sweater/jacket (it may be cold on the plane or in transit airport)
- One set of underwear and changing clothes in case of flight delay or checked luggage
delay/lost
- Personal medicines as needed

title: Faculty Biography
text:
# Faculty Biography

## Intensive English Faculty Biographies

---

**Andrew Bowman, Director of Intensive English**
Prior to becoming the Director of the program in 2023, Mr. Andrew Bowman has been
IELC’s Learning Laboratory Coordinator since 1996. Originally an ESOL instructor in
Paraguay, Mr. Bowman began developing language-learning software in the early nineties
and eventually returned to Wichita where he was born and raised. A graduate of the
University of Kansas, Mr. Bowman also has Master’s Degree from Rutgers University.
Having lived abroad he knows the challenges international students face when starting
a new life while trying to learning a new language.

title: Faculty Biography
text:
**Aimee Leisy, ESL Specialist**Ms. Aimee Leisy has a B.A. in History and Spanish from Bethel College in North Newton,
Kansas, and a Master’s Degree in Literacy, Culture, and Language Education from the
University of Indiana at Bloomington. She has taught at the Intensive English Language
Center for over 15 years. Her other teaching experience includes teaching English
to middle school students in Texas and to adults in both Kansas and Texas. She taught
English at private language schools in both New Zealand and Mexico and at Instituto
Tecnológico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, a well-known Mexican University.
Ms. Leisy speaks French, Italian, and fluent Spanish, having lived in Mexico for five
years. As a language learner herself, she enjoys finding effective and engaging ways
to help students improve their English proficiency.

title: Faculty Biography
text:
**Barbara Mazza Silhan, ESL Specialist**
Mrs. Barbara Mazza Silhan has been teaching at the Intensive English Language Center
since 1983. Mrs. Silhan studied at Oklahoma State University for six years where she
received a bachelor's degree in history and a master's in teaching English as a Second
Language. Mrs. Silhan really enjoys her job because of her love of being in the classroom
and working with the students. She has always been fascinated with other countries
and their cultures, and believes that she learns as much from the students as they
learn from her.

title: Faculty Biography
text:
**Marsha Webb, ESL Specialist**
Twenty-six years of teaching in a variety of settings (middle school, high school,
community college, and 29 years at the Intensive English Language Center) has Mrs.
Marsha Webb smiling about how lucky she is. Her love of teaching English combines
an avid interest in reading, discussion, world cultures, and young people. Also, with
five children of her own she is at home with university-age students and tends to
"mother" them as well. Her educational background includes an Associate of Arts degree,
a BSE from Emporia State University, a MEd from Wichita State University, and a TESOL
Teaching Certificate. With a striving for natural communication, varying methods of
teaching, and a focus on informality, learning in her classroom is intentionally fun!

title: Faculty Biography
text:
**Rima Haidar-Duncan,** **Instructor**
Rima Haidar-Duncan grew up in Beirut, Lebanon and travelled extensively in Europe.
She went to American Evangelical school for girls (A.E.S.G) which was called later
B.E.S.G. Rima is polylingual and lived in the Greek cypress for a period of time during
the devastating war in Lebanon. At that time she travelled to Europe specifically
Germany and France, then she came back to Lebanon to finish her Bachelor’s degree
in Beirut specializing in teaching English Literature and languages. In 1985, She
left to the United States to pursue her higher Education and received her Master’s
in Public Relations with special attention to corporate management from Boston University.
She worked for several years as a freelance researcher for Kuwait University under
the supervision of Dr. Behbehani. She has worked for several years as an archivist
in Assafir, a prominent Newspaper in Beirut. Rima has taught at Butler County Community
College for almost 19 years. She loves to cook Mediteranean food.

title: About Intensive English Language Center
text:
# About Intensive English Language Center

English is one of the most widely spoken languages in business and science today and
English is often required in many jobs around the world. Your education or career
will benefit from the quality English instruction offered by the Intensive English
Language Center at Wichita State University.

The Intensive English Language Center is a well-respected program for teaching English
as a Second Language (ESL). The Intensive English Language Center, or IELC, was founded
in 1976 and has educated more than 7000 students from over 100 countries around the
world.

## About the Program

title: About Intensive English Language Center
text:
- English testing upon arrival
- Seven levels (beginning through advanced levels)
- Each level takes approximately 8 weeks to complete
- 25 hours of instruction per week (5 hours each weekday)
- Students may study as little as 8 weeks or longer than one year -- whatever is needed
to achieve their needed level of proficiency
- Classes include:
- Reading
- Writing
- Speaking and Listening
- Structure (English grammar)
- Learning Laboratory -- a laboratory utilizing computers and other audio-visual aids. Students use specialized
ESL software, receive individualized attention, and are given customized Internet
assignments.
- Weekly conversation practice with conversation partners
- Essay and research paper preparation
- If there is sufficient interest and as staff availability allows, elective classes
in TOEFL Preparation and Pronunciation are available.

title: About Intensive English Language Center
text:
You must be at least 17 years old in order to apply to the Intensive English Language
Center. We are proud to be the first step in a successful career! Apply today and
find out why so many students have chosen to study at the Intensive English Language
Center at Wichita State University!

title: Mission Statement
text:
# Mission Statement

## Mission and Objective

The Intensive English Language Center (IELC) serves non-native English-speaking students
who do not meet WSU's English language proficiency requirements. It is an intensive,
pre-academic language and cultural immersion program. Approximately fifty language
classes are taught daily at seven different levels of instruction.

title: Mission Statement
text:
Three kinds of testing are conducted at the IELC. New students are tested for internal
level placement decisions in the language program. Secondly, university-wide proficiency
testing is provided to determine non-native speakers' readiness to begin academic
programs when the required language proficiency scores are not available. Thirdly,
the Test of Spoken English is administered to prospective Graduate Teaching Assistants
to assess their readiness to receive teaching appointments. Use of this test and score
requirements are stipulated by WSU and the Kansas Board of Regents.

title: Mission Statement
text:
Beyond its core instructional component, IELC sees its mission as a full-service program
encompassing social, cultural, and academic orientation programs, and a variety of
student services including: airport pickups, housing coordination, social and cultural
activities, personal and academic advising, and immigration counseling.

Faculty and administrators of the IELC also serve the university and community-at-large
through university committee work, consultations with community-based ESL programs,
and informal advising of WSU graduate students pursuing studies in English as a Second
Language. IELC also serves occasionally as a laboratory for institutional research.

## "That's My Story"

Aimee Leisy, Associate Teaching Professor of Intensive English, created the public
speaking event called “That’s My Story,” in 2017 to raise the voices of bilingual

and cultural diversity on campus.

We welcome you to come hear the stories of Intensive English students each year during
International Education Week in November!

title: Intensive English with Part-Time Graduate Study
text:
# Intensive English with Part-Time Graduate Study

##

## Intensive English with One Graduate Class

Graduate applicants who are admissible to a graduate degree program but have not yet
met Wichita State University's English requirement can begin taking one  graduate-level
class while improving their English language skills at Wichita State University's
Intensive English Language Center. Because an academic I-20 cannot be issued before
the English proficiency requirement is met, this option allows graduate students without
an acceptable English score for full graduate admission to receive an I-20 for English
language study instead.

**Students who are admissible to a graduate program may enroll in 3 Intensive English
classes and 1 graduate-level class if:**

title: Intensive English with Part-Time Graduate Study
text:
1. Student completes an application for admission with required materials to the Intensive English Language Center.
2. Student meets one of the part-time graduate/Intensive English requirements from the
table below.
- English Test results must be issued within the last 2 years for consideration.

| English Test | Required Score to Take One Graduate Class |
| --- | --- |
| TOEFL (iBT) | 69-78 |
| IELTS | 6.0 |
| PTE Academic | 50-57 |
| Duolingo English Test | 110-114 |

title: Intensive English with Part-Time Graduate Study
text:
**IMPORTANT NOTE:** Graduate students must still fulfill the English requirement established by their
graduate program in order to begin full-time graduate study. Graduate students completing the Intensive English program at Wichita State may meet the Graduate
School's English proficiency requirement by achieving a cumulative GPA of 3.00 in
levels 1 through 6, and a grade of B-plus or higher in level 7.  However, some programs
have higher requirements for English proficiency.

text:
# U.S. Educational System

## Your Education at Wichita State University

University Calendar

General Education Classes

Credit Hours

Grading System

Probation and Dismissal

Repeated Classes

## University Calendar

Wichita State University operates on the semester system. The University calendar
is as follows:

- Spring Semester (16 weeks) -- mid-January to mid-May
- Break or vacation time -- mid-May to late-May
- Summer Session (8 weeks)\* -- about June 1 to July 31
- Break or vacation time -- August 1 to mid-August
- Fall Semester (16 weeks) -- mid-August to mid-December
- Break or vacation time -- mid-December to mid-January

**\*Note**: Summer Session enrollment is not required unless it is your first term of enrollment.
Students who study during the optional Summer Session may graduate faster.

Top

## General Education Classes

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
One of the unique features of the American educational system is the requirement that
students must take classes in areas not related to their major. We feel that a broad
education is more beneficial in your professional and private lives than an education
that is strictly focused in one area of study. Students often find that, after taking
various General Education classes, they have an aptitude or interest in an area of
study that they would never have considered before. With the help of your advisor
at WSU, all students must take classes in:

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
| Skills | Requirements |
| --- | --- |
| **Basic Skills** | ***Required:*** English Composition I and II, Public Speaking, and College Algebra or higher |
| **Fine Arts** | ***Choose from:*** Art History, Dance, Musicology-Composition, or Theatre |
| **Humanities** | ***Choose from:*** Communication, English, History, Linguistics, Modern and Classical Languages, Philosophy, Religion, and Women's Studies |
| **Social and Behavioral Sciences** | ***Choose from:*** Anthropology, Criminal Justice, Economics, Entrepreneurship, Ethnic Studies, Geography, Political Science, Psychology, and Sociology |
| **Mathematics and Natural Sciences** | ***Choose from:*** Biology, Biological Anthropology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Geology, Mathematics/Statistics, Physics, and Public Health Sciences |

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
As a reminder, you do not need to select these classes now. You will meet with an
advisor after your arrive in Wichita for assistance in selecting your classes.

Top

## Credit Hours

Many students ask, "What is a credit hour?" A credit hour represents the number of
hours that you spend in one class each week during a semester. Most classes at the
University are 3 credit hours. This means that you will attend class 3 hours each
week for that particular class. Credit hours are important because:

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
1. the number of credit hours you study each semester determines how much you pay for
tuition (currently US$554.54 per credit hour). The total cost of tuition for each
semester is calculated as follows: Credit Hours X $554.54 = total cost of tuition.
The cost of housing, meals, books, and medical insurance are extra. Estimates for
these expenses can be found on our website or our application form.
2. the number of credit hours you study each semester will determine how long it will
take you to graduate from Wichita State. Most majors require that you complete 124
credit hours in order to graduate (although some majors, such as engineering and health
professions, require more). For more information on the number of credit hours required
to graduate for your major, please check out: www.wichita.edu/registrar and click on the link for "Catalog". Undergraduate International students are required
by law to study a minimum of 12 credit hours per semester. Students who enroll in
12 credit hours or more for the fall or spring semester (6 credit hours for the summer)
are considered to be studying "full-time." Credit hours from any withdrawn classes
are not used when determining a student's full-time enrollment status. This means
you may not be able to legally drop below 12 credit hours -- even if you are doing
poorly in a class. Many international students, however, study 15 or more credit hours
each semester. In order to graduate in 4 years, students must complete 15 to 16 credit
hours each semester (or take classes during the summer).
3. credit hours determine your classification as a student. Students are classified as
follows:
**Freshmen** - have less than 30 credit hours (normally 1st year students)
**Sophomores** - have 30 to 59 credit hours (normally 2nd year students)
**Juniors** - have 60 to 89 credit hours (normally 3rd year students)
**Seniors** - have 90 credit hours or more (normally 4th year students)
4. credit hours represent the weight used in calculating the average of your grades.
For example, a 5 credit hour class will have more of an impact on your overall grade
point average than a 1 credit hour class.

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
Top

## Grading System

Wichita State University uses the following system for grading:

| Letter grade | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | 4.0 | Excellent Achievement |
| A- | 3.7 | |
| B+ | 3.3 | |
| B | 3.0 | Very Good Achievement |
| B- | 2.7 | |
| C+ | 2.3 | |
| C | 2.0 | Average Achievement |
| C- | 1.7 | |
| D+ | 1.3 | |
| D | 1.0 | Below Average Achievement |
| D- | 0.7 | |
| F | 0.0 | Failing |

Your grade point average (often called a "GPA" in the U.S.) is determined by dividing
your Total Grade Points for a semester by the number of Credit Hours you attempted.
An example is as follows:

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
| **Total** | 14 | | 40.5 | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Class Name | Credit Hours | Grade | Grade Points | Calculation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Calculus - I | 5 | B+ = 3.3 | 16.5 | (5 credit hours X a grade of 3.3 = 16.5) |
| Psychology | 3 | A = 4.0 | 12 | (3 credit hours X a grade of 4.0 = 12) |
| Public Speaking | 3 | C- = 1.7 | 5.1 | (3 credit hours X a grade of 1.7 = 5.1) |
| Geography | 3 | C+ = 2.3 | 6.9 | (3 credit hours X a grade of 2.3 = 6.9) |

**SEMESTER GPA = 2.89** (40.5 grade points divided by 14 credit hours = GPA of 2.89)

The term "GPA" is a general term and can actually refer to many different kinds of
GPA's -- depending on the use. Students at Wichita State University may have the following
GPA's:

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
1. **Transfer GPA** - the grade point average for all classes you studied at another college/university
2. **Semester GPA** - the grade point average you earned in one particular semester at Wichita State
(as in the above example)
3. **WSU GPA** - the grade point average for all of the semesters you have studied at Wichita State
4. **Cumulative GPA** - refers to the combined GPA for all classes taken at other colleges/universities
AND all classes taken at WSU

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
Why is your GPA important? First and foremost, your GPA is a reflection of your achievement
at the University. Your GPA is also used in deciding if you might qualify for a scholarship,
special honors at graduation, and your eligibility to graduate or continue your study
at Wichita State. Some employers may use your GPA in deciding if you would be a good
candidate for a job. For this reason, it is important that you try to obtain the highest
GPA possible each semester.

Top

## Probation and Dismissal

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
You must perform satisfactorily in your classes in order to be allowed to continue
your studies at Wichita State University. Each Faculty (a Faculty is often called
a "College" in the U.S.) at WSU has its own GPA requirement that is used to measure
a student's satisfactory performance and his/her eligibility to graduate. Students
must obtain the following Semester GPA, WSU GPA, **and** Cumulative GPA in order to be able to continue their studies at WSU and graduate:

| College or School | Minimum GPA |
| --- | --- |
| W. Frank Barton School of Business | 2.25 GPA |
| College of Education | 2.50 GPA |
| College of Engineering | 2.00 GPA |
| College of Fine Arts | 2.00 GPA |
| College of Health Professions | 2.00 GPA |
| College of Liberal Arts and Sciences | 2.00 GPA |

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
Students who have a GPA below what is required by their Faculty/College cannot graduate
or receive a diploma. Students who do not obtain the GPA required by their Faculty/College
will be first placed on "probation" and given the opportunity to improve their performance
before being dismissed (expelled) from the University. Students who are placed on
probation will be given one semester to improve their GPA. Students who perform unsatisfactorily
during the semester during which they are on probation will be dismissed from the
University.

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
Students are placed on probation at the end of any semester in which they have obtained
a Semester GPA, Cumulative GPA, or WSU GPA below what is required by their Faculty/College
(see the above GPA requirements). Probation is removed when a student's Semester GPA,
Cumulative GPA, **and** WSU GPA reaches the requirement for their Faculty/College. Students will remain on
probation if they earn the minimum Semester GPA required by their Faculty/College
during their probation semester but their WSU GPA or Cumulative GPA remains below
the minimum. In short, it is best for all students to obtain the GPA required by their
Faculty/College during each semester of enrollment at WSU in order to avoid being
placed on probation and risk being dismissed from the University.

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
If you are placed on probation by your Faculty/College, you will be allowed to study
a maximum of 12 credit hours during your probation semester. During the semester you
are on probation, it is **very** important that you obtain the highest GPA you can. If, at the end of your probation
semester, your Semester GPA, Cumulative GPA, **and** WSU GPA meet or exceed the requirement by your Faculty/College, you will be removed
from probation. You will remain on probation if you earn the minimum Semester GPA
required by your Faculty/College during your probation semester but your WSU GPA or
Cumulative GPA remains below the minimum. **Important Warning:** If you fail to meet the minimum Semester GPA required by your Faculty/College during
the semester you are on probation, you will be dismissed (expelled) from the University.

Top

## Repeated Classes

title: U.S. Educational System
text:
The University's repeat policy allows students to have a total of 5 repeated classes.
If you have already repeated classes at another school, those repeats will count toward
the 5 you are allowed. After 5 repeated classes, all grades are averaged into your
Cumulative GPA.

For other important information about the policies and procedures at Wichita State
University, please check out https://www.wichita.edu/registrar and click on the link for "Catalog".

title: The Kansas Aviation Museum by Dhruv
text:
# The Kansas Aviation Museum by Dhruv

## A Must Visit Destination

**by Dhruv** (India) Aerospace Engineering | *Mar 25, 2025*

### Discover Wichita's Aviation Heritage

Wichita is proudly the Air Capital of the World, and the Kansas Aviation Museum is
the ultimate example of this rich heritage. The museum fills the historic Wichita
Municipal Airport Terminal Building, an art-deco treasure constructed during the 1930s
with its control tower finished in 1941. Standing in the atrium where legends like
Fred Astaire used to stand while waiting for flights, or going up to the tower to
glimpse panoramic views of Wichita, roots visitors in an important era in aviation
history.

title: The Kansas Aviation Museum by Dhruv
text:
The museum contains an impressive collection of over a dozen civilian and military
aircraft displayed on the outdoor ramp. Mentioned are the Boeing B-52D Stratofortress,
a monstrous bomber that has a 185-foot wingspan, and the Boeing KC-135E Stratotanker,
an important air refueling aircraft. Personal aircraft such as a Cessna Citation,
a Beechcraft Queen Air, and a Learjet Model 23 formerly owned by Bill Lear also illustrate
the diversity in the form and function of flight.

Within, the museum displays six full-scale aircraft and a collection of exhibits that
trace the histories of local aircraft manufacturers, with special areas on Beechcraft
and Cessna. Special exhibits such as the Rip Gooch Black Aviators Exhibit and Women
of Aviation showcase the contributions made by diverse groups to the industry

### Hands-On, Interactive Experiences

title: The Kansas Aviation Museum by Dhruv
text:
One of the best things about the museum is its interactive exhibits. The flight simulators
allow you to experience what it feels like to pilot an airplane, and it is an excellent
and learning experience for all. The piston engine model of work also allows you to
get up close and personal with how internal combustion engines operate, solidifying
engineering concepts in a fun way.

### Why Visit During Spring Break?

The Kansas Aviation Museum can be found at 3350 George Washington Boulevard, Wichita,
KS 67210. It is open daily except Thursday from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Admission is
$10 per adult, $8 for seniors, and $6 for kids, with multiple daily specials available.
Be sure to visit the museum's website for the latest hours and event information.​

title: The Kansas Aviation Museum by Dhruv
text:
Spring Break provides the perfect opportunity to discover Wichita's aviation history.
As an engineering student, a history enthusiast, or someone with a general fascination
with the miracles of flight, the Kansas Aviation Museum offers a learning experience
and an inspiration that is sure not to be missed. Don't miss the opportunity to see
this excellent museum and become part of the thrilling aviation world.

So if you find yourself in Wichita this Spring Break, make sure to head to the Kansas
Aviation Museum—a place where history, technology, and adventure come together!

title: Bridging Cultures by Harshit
text:
# Bridging Cultures by Harshit

## Celebrating Tradition and Finding Home Abroad

**by Harshit** (India) Product Design & Manufacturing Engineering | *Nov 22, 2024*

### Bridging Cultures: Celebrating Tradition and Finding Home Abroad!

As an international student at Wichita State University, one of the most beautiful
parts of my journey has been the opportunity to celebrate my cultural traditions while
also embracing a sense of belonging in a new environment. This semester, I had the
privilege to participate in a series of vibrant and heartwarming events organized
both on campus and around Wichita. From Ganesh Puja to Navratri Puja, India Nite,
Diwali Night, and Garba Night, each occasion was a celebration of culture, community,
and joy.

title: Bridging Cultures by Harshit
text:
These events were made possible through the incredible efforts of student organizations
like ISA (Indian Student Association) and AHINSA, who worked tirelessly to recreate
the spirit of our traditional festivals thousands of miles from home. Their dedication
and enthusiasm turned these gatherings into unforgettable experiences, bringing together
not just students from India but also those from diverse backgrounds eager to learn
about and celebrate Indian culture.

### Finding a Home Away From Home

title: Bridging Cultures by Harshit
text:
For me, attending these events was more than just a way to celebrate my traditions—it
was a way to feel connected and find a sense of home in a foreign land. At Garba Night,
I danced to the rhythmic beats of traditional music, surrounded by friends and fellow
students who felt like family. During Diwali Night, the sparkling lights and festivities
transported me straight back to my childhood memories of celebrating with loved ones
back in India. These moments were a reminder that no matter where we are, we carry
our culture with us, and it has the power to bring people together.

### A Chance to Share and Learn

title: Bridging Cultures by Harshit
text:
One of the most rewarding aspects of these celebrations was the opportunity to share
our rich traditions with the broader Wichita State community. From explaining the
significance of Ganesh Puja to introducing friends to the joy of Garba, these events
allowed us to act as cultural ambassadors while also learning about others' experiences
and perspectives. It’s amazing how these gatherings create a bridge between cultures,
fostering mutual respect and understanding.

### Why Wichita State is Special

title: Bridging Cultures by Harshit
text:
Wichita State University truly stands out for its inclusive and supportive environment.
The campus not only provides a space for academic growth but also encourages students
to celebrate their identities and cultures. Events like these make it clear that Wichita
State isn’t just a university—it’s a global community where traditions are honored,
differences are celebrated, and everyone finds their place.

### Your Turn to Join the Celebration!

title: Bridging Cultures by Harshit
text:
If you’re an incoming student or someone considering Wichita State, know that these
cultural celebrations are just one of the many ways you can make your time here memorable.
It’s more than just attending events; it’s about building lifelong friendships, creating
cherished memories, and finding your home away from home. So, the next time you hear
about a Diwali Night or a Navratri Puja, don’t miss the chance to be part of something
special. Who knows? You might just find yourself dancing the night away at Garba or
lighting up the room with a Diya next time. I hope to see you there!

This journey has been truly enriching, and I can’t wait to create more memories at
future celebrations. If I can find joy, connection, and belonging here, so can you.
What are you waiting for? Join us and experience it for yourself!

# The Shocker Success Center by Don

## Fall 2024 Wichita State's New Building

**by Don** (Zimbabwe) Aerospace Engineering | *Oct 28, 2024*

If you didn’t know as of Fall 2024 Wichita State has a new **Shocker Success Center**!!! What is the Shocker Success Center you might ask? Allow me to enlighten you on
our newly beloved student building!!

title: The Shocker Success Center by Don
text:
As stated, the Shocker Success Center “brings together dozens of student support functions
in a single, welcoming space conveniently located in the heart of campus”. As we all
know, our lovely campus has many amazing resources, but they weren’t all located in
the same vicinity. To make student resources more accessible than ever we decided
to bring most of the student support to the heart of campus in the same building!
Talking about convenience, it feels like a convenience store for success. This wonderful
glass facade building has three floors and a lower level. We will explore all the
services provided on each floor including my favorite(lower level).

### First Floor:

title: The Shocker Success Center by Don
text:
- **OneStop Student Services (LOCATION: Suite 104)** A great place to start our building tour is stopping by the OneStop Student Services.
This service is the first service you will see when entering the building. If you
are not sure where to go, this is best the place to start. OneStop advisors can assist
you with building semester schedules, setting up degree plans, reviewing financial
aid, understanding bills, and setting up payment plans. There are many processes and
steps required when going through college and OneStop is there to help you navigate
through your college journey.
- **Student Accommodations and Testing✍️ (LOCATION: Suite 118)** The Office of Student Accommodations & Testing sets the standards and determines the
reasonable accommodations that may meet the needs of students with disabilities while
coordinating various testing and proctored examination services to all Shockers. OSAT
is dedicated to supporting students to allow them to perform at their highest academic
potential.

title: The Shocker Success Center by Don
text: ### Second Floor:

title: The Shocker Success Center by Don
text:
- **Math Lab ✖️➗(LOCATION: Suite 207)** If you want to be one of the few students who love mathematics because you understand
it and are the best of friends, you should stop by the math lab. The Math Lab is a
free tutoring service for Wichita State students. The lab is staffed by graduate students
and exceptional undergraduate students studying mathematics or mathematics-related
disciplines. In addition, numerous mathematics faculty members volunteer time in the
lab.
- **Physics Help Desk🧑‍🔬 (LOCATION: Suite 207)** Did you know if the Sun were made of bananas, it would be just as hot? If you want
to have a better grasp of physics you should stop by The Physics Help Room. It offers
free, walk-in tutoring for introductory physics courses to students enrolled in any
degree program. Staffed by undergraduate physics majors, GTA’s, and volunteer faculty,
we are committed to your success with homework help, exam prep, and cool physics demos.
- **Writing Center✍️ (LOCATION: Suite 207)** The Wichita State University Writing Center is a writing resource available to students
who need assistance at all stages of writing — including brainstorming, topic development,
revisions, development of critical reading leading to more enhanced writing, and grammatical
exercises. Located inside the Shocker Learning Center.
- **Student Success 🙌🏾(LOCATION: Suite 218)** The goal of the Office of Student Success is to help students transition to Shocker
life and develop skills and processes to help them achieve their personal and academic
goals. Student Success comprises three areas: **First-Year Programs**(orientation and transition programs, Clash of the Colleges, Syllabus Party); **Academic Success Programs** (tutoring and supplemental instruction); and **Success Coaching**.
- **TRIO Disability Support Services📚 (LOCATION: Suite 223)** TRIO Disability Support Services assists first-generation and limited-income undergraduate
students who have learning, physical, and psychological disabilities. Among the services
provided are academic support and tutoring, access to adaptive computer equipment,
and other services that enable our students to persist and graduate from Wichita State
University.

title: The Shocker Success Center by Don
text: ### Third Floor:

title: The Shocker Success Center by Don
text:
- **Adult Learning📓(LOCATION: Suite 302)** Adult Learning is committed to supporting adult learners, ensuring that they have
access to the resources and support they need to succeed.
- **Student Outreach and Support (SOS) (LOCATION: Suite 304)** The Office of Student Outreach and (SOS) Support provides case management and basic
needs to facilitate outreach, intervention, and follow-up care for students experiencing
crisis or distress that impacts their social, personal, or academic well-being. SOS
is dedicated to being a resource for students by fostering an environment centered
on advocacy, offering holistic support, and building intentional connections to campus
and community resources.
- **TRIO Student Support Services 📚(LOCATION: Suite 307)** TRIO Student Support Services provides academic support services that help first-generation,
limited-income students, and students with disabilities to persist and graduate from
college.
- **Tech Help Desk 💻(LOCATION: Suite 320)** The Tech Help office is designed to meet the growing tech needs of students. Staff
will help students with diagnostics and troubleshooting on personal devices, issues
with internet access, software and app training, email issues, learning remotely,
as well as support for Blackboard and other university applications. Additionally,
Tech Help provides loaner Chromebooks for students.
- **Hispanic-Serving Initiatives (LOCATION: Suite 309)** The Office of Hispanic-Serving Initiatives leads the way in helping Hispanic students
succeed through academic support, applied learning, First-Year Experience programs,
and advising.
- **Military and Veterans Services (LOCATION: Suite 318)** The Military and Veterans Services office assists military members, veterans, and
their dependents in understanding, applying for, and utilizing their education benefits.
This office is responsible for certifying the enrollment and changes in enrollment
of eligible students to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Regional Office in
St. Louis.

title: The Shocker Success Center by Don
text: ### Lower Level:

title: The Shocker Success Center by Don
text:
- **International Education 🌍(LOCATION: Suite 003)** The Office of International Education manages the recruitment and admission of international
undergraduates and intensive English students, as well as supporting international
students once they’re on campus. The office also manages the regulatory concerns for

Items available may include suits, dress pants, professional shirts or blouses, professional

# Airshow by Dhruv

## An Experience Beyond the Classroom

**by Dhruv** (India) Aerospace Engineering | *Oct 14, 2024*

### A Thrilling Day at the Frontiers in Flight Airshow!

This August, I had the pleasure of attending the Frontiers in Flight airshow at McConnell
Air Force Base in Wichita. Whether you’re a longtime aviation enthusiast or someone
who just enjoys a good show, this event was an absolute must-see. And even though
I'm a huge fan of airplanes and engineering, I believe anyone could appreciate the
atmosphere and excitement that filled the day.

title: Airshow by Dhruv
text:
You don’t have to be an aviation expert to enjoy the airshow. The roar of jet engines
and the sight of planes flying in tight formations at high speeds is exciting for
everyone. The highlight for me was seeing the F-35 Lightning II in action. Even if
you’re not familiar with the technical aspects, watching this sleek aircraft perform
rapid climbs and sharp turns was exhilarating. The sheer power and agility of these
machines is something that transcends background knowledge—when you see it in person,
you’ll feel the thrill.

title: Airshow by Dhruv
text:
Another crowd favorite was the U.S. Navy Blue Angels, known for their stunning precision
and coordination. Their performances left everyone, regardless of their aviation knowledge,
with their jaws on the floor. You didn’t need to understand the science behind flying
to appreciate how closely these planes were moving together—it was simply an awe-inspiring
moment that captivated the entire crowd.

title: Airshow by Dhruv
text:
For me, personally, getting up close to iconic aircraft was a dream come true. I got
to see the F-16 Fighting Falcon and my personal favorite, the F-22 Raptor, up close—and
even got a picture with both! These aircraft, known for their speed and maneuverability,
are more than just feats of engineering marvel—they are a symbol of the advancements
in technology. If you ever get the chance to attend, even if you’re not deeply into
planes, seeing these up close is an experience you won’t forget. It’s hard not to
be impressed by their sleek design and sheer size.

title: Airshow by Dhruv
text:
One of the best things about the airshow is that it’s not just for hardcore aviation
fans. There was something for everyone, from food stalls with local eats to family
zones where kids could play and explore. The static displays—where planes like the
KC-46A Pegasus were parked on the ground for people to walk around and explore—offered
a hands-on experience that made the day enjoyable for attendees of all ages.

title: Airshow by Dhruv
text:
If you’re considering Wichita as a destination for your studies, events like this
show just how much the city has to offer outside of academics. The airshow isn’t just
about planes—it’s about community, culture, and stepping out of your routine to experience
something different. Whether you’re studying engineering, business, or anything in
between, living in Wichita provides you with opportunities to immerse yourself in
unique experiences like this. And with Wichita State University being a key part of
the city, there are always ways to balance the academic workload with local events
and activities.

title: Airshow by Dhruv
text:
Attending the **Frontiers in Flight** airshow was a great reminder that life as a student isn’t just about hitting the books—it’s
about engaging with the local community and making the most of your time outside the
classroom. Whether or not you’re into aviation, events like this offer a chance to
unwind and take in something new. If you do end up coming to Wichita for your studies,
keep an eye out for these kinds of events—they might just become a highlight of your
experience here, as they did for me.

# Certificates Strengthen Your Degree by Ivanka

## Advancing Your Educational Path

**by Ivanka** (South Africa) Biological Sciences | *Oct 8, 2024*

Hey Everyone!🫂

At Wichita State University, I have had the opportunity to pursue both a Biology degree
and a Health Science certificate concurrently. I strongly advise looking into the
certificate programs that many universities, including our own, offer to anyone who
is thinking about how to maximize their time in college.✨🙂‍↕️

### Certificate Programs: What Are They?

A set of concentrated courses called certificate programs help students to become
experts in a particular field irrespective to their major. They can be an excellent
way to delve deeper into a subject you're passionate about or that fits with your
career aspirations, and they usually take less time than a complete degree.📜

### My Journey: Biology and Health Science🧬

title: Certificates Strengthen Your Degree by Ivanka
text:
While pursuing my biology degree, I came to the idea that I wanted to add health science
expertise to my degree . I decided to pursue a Health Science certificate as a result,
which I can finish in addition to my major coursework! This combination makes perfect
sense to me since, as someone who is interested in both biology as a discipline and
its practical uses in healthcare, this degree allows me to learn more about the health
industry without having to postpone my studies.🩺

### How Do I Get Started?

title: Certificates Strengthen Your Degree by Ivanka
text:
Speak with your academic advisor on campus if you have any questions concerning certificate
programs. They can advise you on how to find a certificate program that best suits
your interests and how to incorporate one into your existing academic schedule. Spend
some time figuring out the various certificate programs to discover which ones pique
your interest and fit with your professional objectives.📌

I hope this was helpful and informative! Thanks for reading!🫶🏾

## Maria Luiza's Top 5 Restaurants

Hello, y'all! Since Spring Break was last week and I had some free time to enjoy the
weather outside, hang out with friends, and go out to eat at my favorite places, I
decided to share with you my top 5 restaurants in Wichita.

title: Top Restaurants in ICT by Maria Luiza
text:
1. **Kobe Steakhouse:** Stylish and chef-driven, Kobe Steakhouse of Japan serves surf ‘n’ turf grilled tableside.
With a blend of Japanese flavors, this spot offers a unique dining experience. My
favorite dish at Kobe is a duo combination with Sirloin and Salmon. My favorite part
of the dish is without a doubt their fried rice. Although this restaurant can be pricy,
its food and service are worth every dollar! 🥩🍤
2. **Chicken N Pickle:** A chef-driven eatery and bar with pickleball courts, shaded beer gardens, and backyard
games. Their wood-grilled and fried chicken sandwiches are standout items. You should
definitely visit Chicken N Pickle to enjoy good food, great friends, and outdoor fun!
🍗🥒
3. **Nortons Brewing Company:** Nortons is all about soulful beer. Located in downtown Wichita, they serve responsibly
sourced food made from fresh, quality ingredients. Enjoy their unique brews, great
food, and outdoor patio. 🍻🍔
4. **El Agave:** A delightful Mexican restaurant with two convenient locations. Their authentic Tex-Mex
cuisine includes mouthwatering burritos, tacos, chilaquiles, and breakfast options.
Don’t miss out on their fresh seafood dishes like fried tilapia, salmon, and spicy
shrimp. Pair your meal with a margarita and savor the flavors at El Agave! 🌮🍹
5. **Wasabi:** A haven for sushi lovers! Wasabi offers a delectable selection of inventive rolls
and Japanese mains. Whether you’re at Wasabi Hinkaku or Wasabi East, expect quality

of the Spring season—an emblem of rejuvenation and vitality. Organized by the Indian
Student Association, previously known as ISA, "Vasanth" blossoms annually during the
Spring semester, typically unfurling its colors between the first two weeks of April,
following the Spring break.

text:
Vasanth is much more than a mere event; it's a vibrant celebration of Indian culture
that weaves together a tapestry of performances and experiences designed to enchant
and inspire. The event kicks off with a warm introduction, shedding light on the invaluable
role of ISA in supporting student growth academically and providing assistance with
campus resources.

title: Learn about Indian Culture by Dhruv
text:
Imagine breathtaking dances, steeped in centuries-old traditions like the graceful
movements of Bharatanatyam, which mesmerize with their intricate footwork and emotive
storytelling. Picture soul-stirring songs resonating with tales of love and longing,
their melodies echoing through the hall and touching the hearts of all who listen.

# Hooked on Spring by Aakriti

## Beginner's Guide to Fishing in Kansas

**by Aakriti** (Nepal) Aerospace Engineering | *Mar 30, 2025*

### SPRING IS BACK!!!

Spring is here, and summer is near! If you're looking for some exciting things to
do during this season, **fishing** might be one of the many options you should try.

I started fishing last summer, and I absolutely love it. It might feel a little tricky
at first, especially as a beginner, but don’t worry—I’ve got some tips to help you
get started! Here are a few common questions answered if you’re ready to give it a
try:

### Where to go fishing?

Kansas offers a diverse array of fishing opportunities across its lakes, reservoirs,
rivers, and ponds. Some popular fishing locations to consider are:

1. Horseshoe Lake
2. K-96 fishing lake park
3. KDOT east lake
4. Chisholm North Lake
5. Santa Fe Lake

title: Hooked on Spring by Aakriti
text:
### Things to purchase before fishing:

As a new fisher person, you may have a hard time reading out so many blogs and yet
miss on some things to consider before you move for your fishing trip. Here are some
ideas I would like to list:

title: Hooked on Spring by Aakriti
text:
1. Fishing License
2. Fishing rod and reel
3. Bait - live or artificial
4. Hooks- to catch fish
5. Bobbers- to help detect bites and keep bait at desired depth
6. Sinkers or weights- for bait to go down to catch prey
7. Scissors, knife
8. Cooler/ bucket - to store the fish caught
9. Chair or stool - optional, but if you are planning to fish longer, I would recommend
foldable chair
10. Trash bag - collect your trash always
11. Personal Care- Hat, sunglasses, sunscreen, band aid, water, snacks, full clothes sometimes
if the area has tall grass around. Sun protection t-shirts have always come in handy
for me.
12. Fishing gloves - this is especially for someone who doesn’t like holding fish or bait
with bare hands.

### More about FISHING LICENSE

Fishing License is pretty easy to get. If you are planning to get a fishing license
for and from Kansas, follow either of these steps:

title: Hooked on Spring by Aakriti
text:
1. Online Purchase: It is one of the easiest purchase processes. Visit  https://gooutdoorskansas.com/  through the Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks'  online portal . Purchase, save in email and you can print a copy for yourself.
2. Phone Purchase: You can also acquire licenses by calling the toll-free number: 1-833-587-2164.
This service operates daily from 6 AM to 9 PM.

text:
# International Student Spotlight - Don Boyd

## From Zimbabwe to Wichita State University: Don's Journey of Growth

Read about Don's journey as an international student pursuing aerospace engineering.
He reflects on his decision to study at WSU, his campus involvements, the challenges
he has faced and the lessons he has learned along the way. Continue reading to learn
more about Don's remarkable journey of growth!

> "The wonderful thing about Wichita State is that there are so many communities that
> are caring and will open their arms for anyone."

**Why did you choose Wichita State University?**

title: International Student Spotlight - Don Boyd
text:
I chose Wichita State University because of its affordability, friendly environment,
and learning experience. Wichita State University, compared to other institutions,
has amazing but affordable institution fees. On top of that, there are many scholarships
for you to apply for! Besides good professors, there are lots of opportunities that
expose you to hands-on learning experiences. When you are not working on exciting
projects, you have the chance to apply your knowledge from on-campus jobs! This helps
you to stand out and showcase your skills in the job market after graduating.

**Why did you choose your major?**

title: International Student Spotlight - Don Boyd
text:
I chose aerospace engineering to continue to help connect families, friends, and people
to each other from all over the world. Being able to video call someone is great but
nothing will beat the feeling of being present with someone in the same space. This
is why I chose aerospace.

**Your involvements, internships, and jobs you have been in or had during your time
here.**

title: International Student Spotlight - Don Boyd
text:
I had the privilege to take hold of most opportunities WSU offered. I was part of
the rocket club and became an outreach chair member during my freshman year. I am
a part of the National Society of Black Engineers (NSBE) and was a chair member for
two years. I was part of the Student Activities Council (SAC), Cultural Ambassadors
Program (CAP), and many more! There are so many clubs and activities for everyone,
and if you think there isn’t, you can start your own! Besides on-campus involvement,
I have had 3 wonderful working experiences from GoCreate, which is an incredible maker
space, as well as the Crash Lab and Emerging Technologies, which are part of the National
Institute for Aviation Research (NIAR). These experiences have shaped my skill levels
in various aspects.

**What you have learned/gained from being in those involvements and opportunities?**

title: International Student Spotlight - Don Boyd
text:
Being exposed to these opportunities has shown me that there is more to college than
just education. Education is definitely needed, but being able to apply that knowledge
is even more valuable. I gained leadership skills by being in club executive positions.
I learned how to manage time and direct members while working, and these are necessary
skills that are difficult to learn in a class environment. If there is any opportunity
presented to you, run to it as fast as you can.

**Your favorite memory here on campus?**

My favorite memory is honestly the friends I have made along the way and the journey
we experienced together all the way till graduation. You look back and realize how
all the late-night study nights, projects, outings, and hangouts were what made you
enjoy college even more.

**Your advice for prospective students.**

title: International Student Spotlight - Don Boyd
text:
My advice is to make use of all the opportunities Wichita State University has to
offer! This makes you experience the best college years of your life. Go for that
event, try out a research program, run for club president, you never know until you
try it. As you go through the years, don't forget one important thing: to always have
fun.

**Any challenges you faced being an international student, and how you overcame them?**

The challenge I faced at the beginning was homesickness. It is exciting to travel
and be in a new environment on your own, but you might end up missing your family
back home. The way I overcame this was by having a great community of friends, as
well as having weekly calls with family. The wonderful thing about Wichita State is
that there are so many communities that are caring and will open their arms for anyone.

**Your plans after graduation.**

title: International Student Spotlight - Don Boyd
text:
My plans after graduation are to work in the aviation industry and maybe do a master's.

**One word to describe your time here at Wichita State.**

Growth

text:
# J-1 Medical Insurance (UnitedHealthcare)

## Medical Insurance Requirements for Exchange Visitors with Insurance from UnitedHealthcare

The U.S. Department of State requires all Exchange Visitors and their accompanying
spouse and children to maintain medical insurance which meets all of the requirements
below for the entire length of their program:

### Minimum Coverage Requirements

title: J-1 Medical Insurance (UnitedHealthcare)
text:
- Medical Benefits of at least $100,000 per accident or illness **AND**
- Repatriation of Remains in the amount of $25,000 **AND**
- Expenses associated with the medical evacuation of the exchange visitor to his or
her home country in the amount of $50,000 **AND**
- A deductible not to exceed $500 per accident or illness **AND**
- Any policy, plan, or contract secured to fill the above requirements must, at a minimum,
be:
- Underwritten by an insurance corporation having an A.M. Best rating of "A-" or above;
a McGraw Hill Financial/Standard & Poor's Claims paying Ability rating of "A-" or
above; a Weiss Research, Inc. rating of "B+" or above; a Fitch Ratings, Inc. rating
of "A-" or above; or a Moody's Investor Services rating of "A3" or above; OR
- Backed by the full faith and credit of the government of the exchange visitor's home
country.

title: J-1 Medical Insurance (UnitedHealthcare)
text:
**Important:** To satisfy regulatory requirements, the medical insurance policy must meet ALL of
the above requirements for the Exchange Visitor, their spouse, and any children who
might accompany the visitor to the U.S. Medical insurance must be maintained for their
ENTIRE STAY in the U.S. It is a serious violation of the law if the Exchange Visitor
and all dependents are not covered by medical insurance. **We will not issue a DS-2019 until you complete the purchase of UnitedHealthcare insurance
for you and all family members who will accompany you to the U.S.**

UnitedHealthcare is our preferred provider for insurance. Insurance through UnitedHealthcare
is quick and easy to purchase, meets all of the above requirements, and is affordable.

### Length Of Coverage Requirement

title: J-1 Medical Insurance (UnitedHealthcare)
text:
UnitedHealthcare offers insurance with a Policy Year from August 1 through July 31
of the following year. The following are two examples of how coverage works with UnitedHealthcare:

title: J-1 Medical Insurance (UnitedHealthcare)
text:
1. **Example 1:** In this example, you plan to be in Wichita for two months from March 1 through April
30. You should purchase insurance for the entire two months that you will be in Wichita.
2. **Example 2:** In this example, you plan to be in Wichita for eight months from May 1 through December
31. Because UnitedHealthcare's Policy Year ends on July 31, you must purchase insurance
for two different periods of time:
- **May 1 through July 31** – Purchase this coverage first. You will not be able to purchase insurance for the
remainder of your program until UnitedHealthcare releases its new rates for the next
Policy Year.
- **August 1 through December 31** – You will need to purchase this coverage as soon as UnitedHealthcare releases its
rates for the next Policy Year.

### Cost Information

The cost for insurance from UnitedHealthcare is:

title: J-1 Medical Insurance (UnitedHealthcare)

How to Apply for Undergraduate Admission

# Financial Aid for International Students

## Financial Aid for International Students

---

- ### Global Select Scholarships -- 36% Tuition Discount!!

#### Intensive English Book Scholarship

- Award is distributed to students enrolled full or part time in Wichita State University's
Intensive English Language Program and covers the cost of an eligible student's books.
- Awards are eligible for renewal only once.
- Award eligibility:
- Meet and maintain a minimum 3.0 GPA
- Be in the second session or higher in the on-campus Intensive English Language Program
- Not a recipient of the Global Select Scholarship

#### Undergraduate Scholarships After Attending Wichita State

title: Financial Aid for International Students
text:
- US$700,000 in scholarships awarded to international students each year
- Must attend WSU for 1 year before applying for scholarships
- Scholarships not awarded before the student arrives in Wichita
- Scholarships awarded based upon good grades at Wichita State.
- No scholarships based upon financial need.
- Scholarships are usually US$500 to US$2,500 per year
- Scholarships are not guaranteed.
- You can also find available scholarships under Scholarships for Current Students

#### Working on Campus

- May work up to 20 hours per week on campus.
- Off-campus employment is not allowed by law except for Cooperative Education .
- May work in offices, cook in the cafeteria, assist in cleaning offices, etc
- Can earn about US$500 per month by working 20 hours per week
- Employment is not guaranteed.

#### Tuition Payment Plan

title: Financial Aid for International Students
text:
- Not required to pay all tuition in one large payment. May pay tuition in smaller installments.
- US$30 administrative fee. No interest is charged.
- Cannot apply until after arriving in Wichita
- Payment schedule:
**Fall Semester:** First payment due in August after selecting classes then September 15, October 15,
and November 15.
**Spring Semester:** First payment due in January after selecting classes then February 15, March 15,
and April 15.
**Summer Session:** First payment due in June after selecting classes then July 15
- How much is each payment? Cannot be calculated until student arrives and selects classes.
- Housing expenses are not included in Tuition Payment Plan.

#### Low Cost-of-Living

title: Financial Aid for International Students
text:
- Very low cost-of-living
- Cost-of-living in Wichita is less than half of New York or San Francisco
- The average cost of an apartment in Wichita is US$718 per month. Average apartment
cost in New York is over US$3,000 per month. National average is US$1,100 per month.
- View University Cost Comparisons

title: Global Select Scholarships
text:
**IMPORTANT NOTE:**  International Students (see below for definition) who qualify for Global Select
receive a substantial tuition discount equivalent to 150% of the tuition rate students
from Kansas pay. Like a traditional scholarship, Global Select reduces the amount
the students pay each semester. With Global Select, you will receive a discount for
every credit hour you enroll in AND you are not required to be enrolled full time
in order to qualify for the discount. As such, for many students, Global Select is
a better discount option than a traditional scholarship. Traditional scholarships
typically require a student to be enrolled full time and are usually for a fixed award
amount. This means that your scholarship award is the same regardless of the number
of credit hours you enroll in. Global Select is different. Please note that Global
Select provides a discount on tuition only (not fees).

title: Global Select Scholarships
text:
**Global Select is a merit-based scholarship and is not awarded based on financial need.**

How to Apply

- Answer one scholarship question on our application for admission. Students must
Apply for Admission in order to be considered for a scholarship. It's quick and easy!
- Automatically awarded to eligible students at the time of admission.
- Automatically renews until the end of your program

Eligibility Requirements (New Students)

title: Global Select Scholarships
text:
- Available for incoming International Students (freshman, transfer, and graduate).
- An “International Student” is defined, for purposes of this program only, as anyone
who is in a non-immigrant visa status.  This includes H1-B visa holders.  Anyone who
is not a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, refugee, or asylee is classified as an
International Student.
- If a student's immigration status changes after admission and the student is no longer
classified as an International Student, Global Select will be rescinded.
- Grades earned in systems other than American-style 4.0 grading scale will be converted
to this scale as part of the application evaluation process once all needed application
materials are received.
- **Undergraduate Applicants**
GPA of 3.0 (out of 4.0) or its international equivalent. The Office of International
Education will determine the student's eligibility for a scholarship.  Please note
that Global Select scholarships are awarded based upon your grades.  SAT and ACT scores
are not used to determine your eligibility for a scholarship.
- **Graduate Applicants**
GPA of 3.3 (out of 4.0) or its international equivalent. The Graduate School will
determine the student's eligibility for a scholarship.
- **Students who Graduate from Wichita State**
GPA of 3.3 or higher regardless of education level
- Only awarded at the time of admission.
- Only awarded with admission to a degree program.
- Discount only available for academic classes (effective Fall 2024).

title: Global Select Scholarships
text:
Eligibility of Current & Returning Students

- Transfer from Wichita State to another institution voids the Global Select Scholarship
award. If a student later returns to Wichita State, they will no longer be eligible
for a Global Select Scholarship and will be charged the regular nonresident rate for
tuition.
- Continuing students who were not eligible for Global Select at the time of admission
will not be reconsidered regardless of their performance at Wichita State, unless
the student graduates from Wichita State and pursues admission to a higher level program
at Wichita State.
- Global Select may be rescinded if the CGPA on a student's final transcript used at
the time of admission drops below the minimum CGPA requirement.

Eligibility of Students with Other Tuition Discount Rates

title: Global Select Scholarships
text:
- Global Select does not apply if student receives resident or other discount tuition
rates including: graduate assistantships, legacy tuition waivers, online programs
(including the hybrid MBA program), Intensive English Language Program (effective
Fall 2024), tuition waivers through Comité Paraguay Kansas (CPK), or WSU employees
and their dependents.
- Global Select does not apply to programs that charge a fixed fee regardless of residency
status, such as Executive MBA, Accelerated Baccalaureate Nursing Program, and WSU/K-State
Nursing Program.

title: Transfer Credit for International Students
text:
- Syllabi are detailed descriptions of the classes that you studied, the amount of time
that you spent in lectures or laboratories, and more. Example of a Syllabus
- If syllabi are needed, the Office of International Education will inform you. You
should then send the syllabi as soon as possible.
- All syllabi must be in English.
- Each syllabus must match the course name on your transcript and cover the same dates
in which you attended the course. For example, the syllabus for College English I
must cover topics for Fall 2019 - the same term in which you took the class. You cannot
submit a syllabus for College English I that was taught in Fall 2017 or any other
term than when you took the course.
- Each syllabus should be in a PDF format and not sent all within one PDF.  Each course
should be separate.
- Student may translate syllabi if an English version is not offered by the school.
