title: Transfer Credit for International Students
text: **STEP 4 -- Submit Official Transcripts**

title: Transfer Credit for International Students
text:
- Unofficial transcripts are used to determine admission, however official transcripts
are needed to perform a degree audit. It is in your best interest to provide transcripts
**now** rather than to wait until you arrive at WSU.
- To be official, transcripts must be originals OR photocopies (in English) bearing
the original stamp, or seal of the school, and original signature of your school’s
official, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or another government
authority. If the school is unwilling to attest a copy in English, please provide
an officially-attested copy in the original language, accompanied by an English translation
that is attested by the official translator that does the translation. **Please visit www.wichita.edu/CountryRequirements to review the specific official transcript requirements for each country where you
took your coursework and to review our transcript retention policy.**
- Please send your transcripts to:
Office of International Education
Wichita State University
1845 Fairmount Street
Wichita, Kansas 67260-0122 USA

title: Transfer Credit for International Students
text: **STEP 5 -- Determination of Equivalencies**

title: Transfer Credit for International Students
text:
- We will send your syllabi to the WSU department which offers a comparable class.
- **This evaluation process can sometimes take 2 months or longer to complete.**
- If a review of your syllabi indicates you have taken the equivalent of our English
Composition course(s), you must sit for the English Validation Examination (EVE) after
you arrive in Wichita and have submitted an official copy of your transcript.  This
examination is an essay test that is the final examination for English Composition
at Wichita State (WSU).  It is not like the TOEFL or IELTS, and you must have met
the WSU English proficiency requirement before you are eligible to sit for the EVE. 
If you pass the EVE you will receive transfer credit for your English Composition
class(es).  If you do not pass, you will be required to take English Composition at
WSU.  After you arrive in Wichita (and we have received an official copy of your transcript),
please go to the Garvey International Center to obtain a permission letter and information
about the EVE.  It is important to take the EVE during your FIRST ACADEMIC SEMESTER
at Wichita State.

title: Transfer Credit for International Students
text:
**STEP 6 – Degree Audit Evaluation**

- This step determines if transferred classes meet graduation requirements for your
specific major.
- **A degree audit evaluation will not be completed without official copies of your transcripts.**
- For example, if you took an Algebra class at your previous school and we determined
in Step 4 that it is equivalent to the Algebra class offered at WSU, your Algebra
class would meet a degree requirement if you majored in Psychology but not if you
majored in Electrical Engineering.
- This evaluation will determine the number of classes and the approximate number of
semesters you will need in order to graduate from Wichita State.
- **Degree audit evaluations take approximately 2-4 weeks to complete.**

expenses for the given academic year at the time of its publishing. Definitive tuition
cost is annouced yearly in July for the upcoming academic year following tuition rate

to differ from the published projection.*

title: International Undergraduate Estimated Expenses
text:
The above estimate includes cost of tuition, fees, accommodations, meals, books, and
required medical insurance. The estimate assumes full-time enrollment of 12 credit
hours minimum per semester. Students are advised to take at least 15 credit hours
per semester in order to graduate in four years. The estimated amounts are averages
and may vary from student to student. Actual expenditures depend on: 1) the student's
major and number of credit hours enrolled, 2) the residence hall or apartment in which
the student lives, 3) whether or not the student has a roommate, and 4) the student’s
meal plan. All international students are required to have medical insurance. Students
who do not have medical insurance when they arrive may purchase it during enrollment.
If a student does not study during the summer but remains in Wichita, they should
budget additional money for living expenses and medical insurance (approximately $3,100).
Students should bring extra money for personal expenses (such as movies, museums,
shopping, etc).

title: Transcripts - Bangladesh
text: Enrollment Deposit Policy

title: Transcripts - Bangladesh
text:
- If admissible, the student will receive a scanned letter indicating they are admissible
and an I-20 will be prepared once the enrollment deposit is received.
- If a student enrolls in classes at WSU but owes less than the US$7,000 deposit paid
previously, the overpayment will not be refunded. Instead, the overpayment will be
applied to the student's next semester of enrollment.
- If a student transfers to another institution after completing their first semester
of enrollment at WSU, he or she will not be eligible for a refund of any balance left
in their account.
- The enrollment deposit can be made by a wired payment for those outside of the United
State. Click here for how to pay with a wired payment. If you or your family has a bank account in the U.S., you can make direct deposit.
You will need to login to  myWSU  and follow the instructions on  How do I set up direct deposit?  webpage. If you have difficulties logging in to your myWSU, you may contact IT support
on  helpdesk@wichita.edu  for assistance.

title: Transcripts - Bangladesh
text: Refund Policy

title: Transcripts - Bangladesh
text:
The deposit will be used to pay for the student’s tuition, fees, on-campus housing,
and medical insurance after the student has enrolled. If the student fails to enroll,
the enrollment deposit is not refundable unless the student completes a Refund Request Form and agrees to the following terms:
- By requesting a refund, the student’s admission and I-20 will be automatically canceled.
Once canceled, the I-20 cannot be used to enter the U.S.
- Before issuing a refund, Wichita State University will look in SEVIS, a U.S. federal
database, to confirm that the student’s I-20 was not used to enter the U.S. If the
I-20 was used to enter the U.S., the student will not be eligible for a refund of
the enrollment deposit.
- Payments that were made more than two years ago could have been sent to the State
of Kansas as unclaimed property. In that case, students will need to contact the State
of Kansas to request a refund.
- Refunds may take up to 60 days to be processed.

title: Transcripts - Bangladesh
text:
Refund Methods
If an applicant qualifies for a refund, the money will be sent as follows:
1) If the original payment was made by credit card, the refund will be credited to
the same credit card.
2) If the original payment was made by international wire transfer through Flywire (formerly peerTransfer), the refund will be processed through Flywire .
3) If the original payment was made by a U.S. bank check, the refund will be processed
through direct deposit to the U.S. bank account upon the student setting up eRefund
in myWSU.
4) If the original payment was made by bank draft or money order, the refund will
be returned by direct deposit to a U.S. bank account assigned by the student who applied
for admission (regardless of who actually paid the money).

title: International Freshman Admission
text:
# International Freshman Admission

## OPTION 1: ADMISSION BASED ON GRADES FROM HIGH SCHOOL

title: International Freshman Admission
text:
- For this option, the **SAT or ACT is NOT required** for admission**.**
- This option is for students who have already graduated from high school (or will soon
graduate from high school).
- Students who have attended another college or university will be considered for transfer
admission -- even if they do not want transfer credit from their previous school.
- Students who have completed AP , IB , or Cambridge A or AS level curriculum are eligible to receive transfer credit.
- Students must submit final high school transcripts .
- You must submit your official final high school transcript as soon as it is available.
**If you do not submit your final official transcript to us by the end of your first
semester at Wichita State University, you will not be allowed to enroll for subsequent
terms.**
- Transcripts or examination results may be sent away for verification. If selected,
it may take some time for the verification results to be returned.
- The TOEFL or IELTS are not required to apply. View English Requirement .

title: International Freshman Admission
text:
**OR**

## OPTION 2: ADMISSION BASED ON SAT OR ACT RESULTS

- The **SAT or ACT is required** for this option**.**
- This is the best option for students who want admission before completing high school,
attended an unrecognized school, or do not meet the admissions requirements in Option
1.
- If you have taken the SAT or ACT, you may apply during your final year of high school.
- SAT results must be sent directly from the  College Board . Our institution code is 6884.
- ACT results must be sent directly from  ACT . Our institution code is 1472.
- To be considered for admission, you must obtain the required scores as follows:

title: International Freshman Admission
text:
| SAT REQUIREMENT | OR | ACT REQUIREMENT |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **March 2016 & after** - A combined Evidence-Based Reading and Writing score and Math score of 1060 or higher **AND** - A minimum score of 490 or higher on each of the Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and Math sections. | | - A composite score of 21 or higher on the English, Math, Science, and Reading sections **AND** - A minimum score of 18 or higher on each of the sections for English, Math, Science, and Reading. \*The Writing Test score will not be used in our admissions decision. |

title: Health Profession Majors
text:
# Health Profession Majors

## Undergraduate Admission Information for Health Professions Majors

Admission to our Health Professions programs is competitive. With the exception of
the B.S. in Health Science, you must first have admission to Wichita State University in order to be considered for admission to any Health Professions program. If you
are accepted to Wichita State University, you will be admitted to the College of Health
Professions as a “Pre-Professional” major. Students will study as Pre-Professional
majors in the College of Health Professions until they have completed all prerequisite
subjects, which normally takes about two years to complete.

title: Health Profession Majors
text:
Except for the B.S. in Health Science, admission to a specific program in the College
of Health Professions requires a separate application to the professional curriculum
after the student has completed all prerequisites. Admission to the professional curriculum
is not guaranteed – **even if you have completed all of the prerequisites and meet the minimum GPA to apply**. The professional curriculum will require an additional two years of study after
the completion of the prerequisite requirements (a total of four years of study at
Wichita State University).

The table below gives a brief overview of the majors in the College of Health Professions
and their requirements. Don't forget:

Pre-Professional Study = the first two years of study at Wichita State

Professional Curriculum = the final two years of study at Wichita State

title: Health Profession Majors
text:
You may click on any of the links below to obtain more detailed information about
your program of choice.

| | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Major** | **GPA Required for Pre-Professional Admission to the College of Health Professions** | **Is a Separate Application Required for the Professional Curriculum?** | **GPA Required to Apply to the Professional Curriculum** |
| Communicative Sciences and Disorders (CSD) | 3.00 | Yes | 3.00. Students must also have a “B” or higher in all CSD courses. |
| Dental Hygiene | 2.75 | Yes | 2.75 |
| Health Science | 2.00 | No | N/A |
| Medical Laboratory Sciences | 2.50 | Yes | 2.50 |
| Nursing | 2.75 | Yes | 2.75 |
| All other majors | 2.00 | No | 2.00 |

title: Health Profession Majors
text:
As a reminder, the first step is to apply to Wichita State University . At a later date when you have completed all of the prerequisites required for your
major, you will submit a separate application for admission for the professional portion
of your program. After you arrive in Wichita and begin classes, your advisor in the
College of Health Professions can answer any questions you might have about applying
for the professional curriculum. If you are later denied admission to the professional
curriculum, you may apply for admission to a different Health Professions major (or
to a different major in one of the other colleges at Wichita State University). Many
of the prerequisite classes taken during your first two years of study at Wichita
State can be used for other majors as well.

# From The WorldGrad to Wichita State

##

## The WorldGrad + Wichita State

Wichita State University partners with The WorldGrad's All American Undergraduate
Program. This partnership enables students to complete one year of online study with
The WorldGrad and ensures all credits earned can be transferred to help complete a
4-year degree at Wichita State.

Students transferring to Wichita State University may be eligible to receive our **Global Select Scholarship** , valued at US$15,000 over three years of study.

***Students participating in The WorldGrad's All American Undergraduate Program can receive
admission to Wichita State University as long as the below requirements are met.***

Requirement 1 - Your CGPA

title: From The WorldGrad to Wichita State
text:
Complete The WorldGrad's All American Undergraduate Program with a CGPA that meets
or exceeds the minimum grade point average required by your intended college at Wichita State University.\*

*\* All university level coursework is considered when calculating cumulative grade
point averages. Students who have completed university level coursework outside of
The WorldGrad's All American Undergraduate Program must provide Wichita State with
transcripts from all post-secondary coursework taken in accordance with Wichita State
University's application requirements. Students who apply to Wichita State prior to
completing 24 university credit hours will also be required to provide secondary/high
school transcripts with their application for admission.*

Requirement 2 - Your Application

title: From The WorldGrad to Wichita State
text:
Complete Wichita State University's application for International Undergraduates with
all required application materials prior to the application deadline for your intended
semester. Refer to www.wichita.edu/applyinternational for more information about our application process.

Requirement 3 - Your English Proficiency

Meet the English proficiency requirement of Wichita State University. Completion of
24 or more credit hours with The WorldGrad will fulfill this requirement. Students
applying for admission to Wichita State University prior to completing 24 credit hours
will be required to meet the English proficiency requirement in another way in order to receive full admission to their chosen program.

**We encourage all students to send any accepted English test score earned within the
past 2 years with their application for admission.**

title: Example of Syllabus
text:
# Example of Syllabus

# \*\*\* Example Syllabus \*\*\*

## INTI COLLEGE MALAYSIA

### COURSE STRUCTURE

**COURSE:** BIO101 ESSENTIALS OF BIOLOGY, LAB (4 cr)

**PREREQUISITE:**  None

**COURSE DESCRIPTION:**
This one-semester course is designed for non-science majors. It enables students to
see the relevance of science in their everyday lives and appreciate how biology is
woven throughout the fabric of their lives. This course introduces the scientific
method and focuses on cells and metabolism, biodiversity and classification, the genetic
basis of life, evolution, health and disease, as well as ecology and the environment.
Laboratory work is used toillustrate some of the concepts covered in the lectures.

**LEARNING OBJECTIVES:**
The aims of this course are to enable students to:

title: Example of Syllabus
text:
- Identify biological facts and principles relating to cells and metabolism, biodiversity
and classification, the genetic basis of life, evolution, health and disease, as well
as ecology and the environment.
- Apply the biological knowledge learned in making conclusions from data, solving problems,
and discussing issues faced by contemporary society.
- Acquire laboratory skills including proper handling and use of laboratory apparatus
and materials.

**LEARNING OUTCOMES:**
Successful students will be able to:

title: Example of Syllabus
text:
- Apply general principles in biology related to cells and metabolism and biodiversity
and classification.
- Describe the inheritance of traits and discuss some of the applications of genetic
engineering.
- Evaluate the evidence supporting the evolutionary process and explain the role of
natural selection and the concepts of species and race.
- Describe health and disease issues related to infectious agents and the immune system,
gender, and brain structure and function.
- Discuss issues related to ecology, conservation biology and the ability of earth to
support human population.
- Carry out some procedures and techniques for practical investigations and interpret
the results by application of principles and theories.

title: Example of Syllabus
text:
**COURSE FORMAT:**
Lecture: 3 hr per week, Tutorial: 1 hr per week, Laboratory Work: 2 hr per week.
[For short semester, Lecture: 6 hr per week, Tutorial: 2 hr per week, Laboratory Work:
4 hr per week.]

**STUDENT EVALUATION:**
Test 1: 20%, Test 2: 20%, Assignments/Quizzes: 10%, Laboratory Work: 10%. Final Examination:
40%.

**FINAL EXAMINATION FORMAT:**
Duration: 3 hours
Section A (40 marks): Answer ALL FOURTY multiple-choice questions.
Section B (60 marks): Answer ALL the SIX to SEVEN structured-type questions.

**GRADING SCALE:**
A+ (90-100), A (85-89), A (80-84), B+ (7579), B (70-74), B (65-69), C+ (60-64),
C (55-59), C (50-54), D+ (45-49), D (40-44), F (0-39)

**BASIC TEXT:**
Belk, CM & Borden, VM. Biology: Science for Life. 1st ed., Prentice Hall, 2004.

title: Example of Syllabus
text:
**REFERENCES:**
1. Campbell, NA, Reece, JB & Simon, EJ. Essential Biology. 2nd ed., Benjamin Cummings,
2004.
2. Krogh, D. Biology: A Guide to the Natural World. 3rd ed., Prentice Hall, 2005.
3. Audesirk, G, Audesirk, T & Byers, BE. Biology: Life on Earth. 7th ed., Prentice
Hall, 2005.

**CLASS SYLLABUS:**
Lecture(s) Topics:

**1 & 2 Introduction To The Scientific Method**
The process of science. Evaluating scientific information. Is there a cure for the
common cold?

**3 & 4 Cells And Metabolism**
Nourishing your body. Converting food into energy. Body fat and health.

**5 & 6 Biodiversity And Classification**
The organization of life's diversity. Locating valuable species. Tools for the bioprospector.

**7 & 8 The Science Of Inheritance**
The inheritance of traits. The role of genes in determining traits. Genes, environment
and the individual.

title: Example of Syllabus
text:
**9 & 10 The Cell Cycle And Cell Division**
What is cancer? Cell division. Diagnosis and treatment.
Test 1

**11 & 12 DNA Structure And Replication**
Chromosomes and DNA. DNA fingerprinting.
Meiosis
How DNA passes from parents to their children.

**13 & 14 Genetic Engineering**
Genetic engineers. Genetic engineers can use bacteria to synthesize human proteins.
Genetic engineers can modify food. Genetic engineers can modify humans.

**15 & 16 The Evidence For Evolution**
What is evolution? Charles Darwin and the Theory of Evolution. Evaluating the evidence
for evolution. Evaluating the hypotheses.

**17 & 18 Natural Selection**
AIDS and HIV. The evolution of HIV. How understanding evolution can help prevent AIDS.

title: English Proficiency Exam Sample Questions
text:
# English Proficiency Exam Sample Questions

# English Proficiency Examination (EPE)

# Sample Questions

---

**NOTE:** You must bring your passport with you to the test.

The WSU Proficiency Test contains three parts (five sections):
**Part I:** Written Essay (30 minutes)
**Part II:** Listening Comprehension (45 items, about 15 minutes)
**Part III:** Grammar, Vocabulary and Reading Comprehension (75 minutes)

title: English Proficiency Exam Sample Questions
text:
**Part I:  The WRITTEN ESSAY (30 minutes)**
Various topics will be selected at the time of each administration. You should select
one of the three selected topics, organize your
thoughts, compose an essay with as much information and detail as you can. While length
is not the most important factor, a longer
essay sometimes indicates a person’s fluency with the language.  Essays are graded
on:
1) how well you addressed the specific topic chosen; i.e., you did not wander  into
topics unrelated to the one chosen.
2) the mechanics of punctuation, spelling, and sentence structure (verb usage,  appropriate
tense selection, etc).
3) organizational structure, including paragraphing.
4) fluency in the English language, including style and idiomatic control.

title: English Proficiency Exam Sample Questions
text:
**Part II:  LISTENING COMPREHENSION (45 items, about 15 minutes)**
Each problem will be spoken only ONCE. You will select an appropriate answer and mark
your answer choices on the answer sheet.

**Example A**
(You will hear) Are you busy? (pause 12 seconds)

(You will read)
a) Yes, I am.
b) Yes, you are.
c) Yes, he is.
“Yes, I am” is the correct answer. You would mark choice a on the answer sheet.

**Example B**
(You will hear) I’ve just begun. (pause 12 seconds)

(You will read)
a) I am almost finished.
b) I just finished.
c) I just started.
I just started means about the same thing as I’ve just begun. Choice c is the correct
answer, so you would mark choice c on the
answer sheet.

title: English Proficiency Exam Sample Questions
text:
**Part III contains 3 sections: Grammar, Vocabulary and Reading Comprehension.** You will have 75 minutes to complete all 3
sections of Part III. This section contains 100 items. Do not spend too much time
on any one problem or you will not have time to
finish the test. Mark only ONE answer for each problem.

**Part III: Grammar**
Example C “What is that thing?”
“That \_\_\_\_\_ a spider.”
a) to call
b) for calling
c) be called
d) is called
The correct English sentence is “That is called a spider.” Therefore, you would mark
choice d on the answer sheet.

**Part III: Vocabulary**
**Type 1:** Example D It’s too windy to go for a stroll.
a) swim
b) sail
c) drive
d) walk
The word walk means about the same thing as stroll in this sentence, so you would
mark choice d on the answer sheet.

title: English Proficiency Exam Sample Questions
text:
**Type 2:** Example E Because of the storm and the rough waves, it would be foolish to go sailing
today in a small \_\_\_.
a) automobile
b) house
c) boat
d) beast
The word boat fits the best in the sentence, so you would mark choice c on the answer
sheet.

**Part III: Reading Comprehension**
The test contains four or more reading passages, each followed by approximately five
questions about each passage. You should
read each passage carefully and then try to answer the questions following the passage.
Sometimes it helps to read over the
questions quickly before you read the passage.

title: English Proficiency Exam Sample Questions
text:
**Example F**
While I was getting ready to go to town one morning last week, my wife handed me a
little piece of red cloth and
asked if I would have time during the day to buy her two yards of cloth like that.
I told her I would be glad to do it. And
putting the piece of cloth into my pocket, I took the train for town.
1) The person telling the story is . . .
 a) a married lady
 b) an unmarried lady
 c) a married man
 d) an unmarried man
You know the person telling this story is a married man because he says, “…my wife
handed me…” The correct answer is c, so
you would mark choice c on the answer sheet.

2) The author was given a piece of red cloth . . .
 a) in the morning
 b) at noon
 c) in the afternoon
 d) in the evening
The passage says, “…one morning last week, my wife handed me a little piece of red
cloth…” The correct answer is a, so you
would mark choice a on the answer sheet.

title: English Proficiency Exam Sample Questions
text:
(There are usually five questions following each passage, not just two) Naturally,
the passages used in the test are much more
difficult than this example and are often paragraphs that have an informational format
rather than a story-like one. For example,
some topics might include conversation techniques, the development of urban life,
the discovery of a famous landmark, or directions
for playing a game.

title: Visa Tips
text:
# Visa Tips

# Visa Tips

**1. Prepare for the Visa Interview**

- Visit the nearest EducationUSA Advising Center to check the availability of visa information session.
- Prepare Required Documents for a Visa
- Your local U.S. Embassy or Consulate may require additional documentation.
- Take a  Complimentary F-1 Visa Preparation Course . 
Disclaimer: This complimentary course is offered by Catalyst GEM, an independent third-party
provider. Wichita State University does not endorse, administer, or assume responsibility
for the course content, services, or outcomes. Participation is voluntary, and all
inquiries or concerns should be addressed directly to Catalyst GEM.

**2. Apply Early!**

title: Visa Tips
text:
- The visa wait time in many countries can be several weeks or months so **APPLY EARLY!**
Visa Wait Times
Requesting an Expedited Visa Appointment
- Make sure all your social media accounts are set to public visibility since U.S. embassies
and consulates may review them during the visa approval process. Failure to do so
could result in a visa denial.
- Apply for a visa up to 1 year before the start date on your I-20 or DS-2019.  Some
countries are subject to a 90-day visa validity period, which means that your visa
can only be used during a 90-day window from the date it is issued until the date
it expires.  Check the U. S. Visa Reciprocity table to find out the F-1 visa validity period for your country of citizenship/residence. 
If your country is subject to a 90-day validity period, you should not schedule a
visa interview appointment that is more than 90 days before the program start date
on your I-20.  Otherwise, your visa could expire before you can use it to enter the
U.S.
- How to Apply for an F-1 Visa or J-1 Visa
- Pay the I-901 SEVIS Fee before your visa interview

title: Visa Tips
text:
**3. During the Visa Interview**

- Most visa interviews are only about 3 minutes long.
- During the interview, be honest, friendly, and organized.
- Visa officers often ask why you chose a specific major, why you chose to study at
Wichita State, or why you chose to study in Wichita. You must be prepared to answer
these questions.
Information About Wichita State
Information About Your Major
Information About the City of Wichita

**4. Reasons for Visa Denials**

The most common reasons for visa denials are:

title: Visa Tips
text:
1. The visa officer suspected the student of wanting to immigrate to the U.S. You must
prove to the visa officer that you plan to return home after graduation. Examples
of proof:
\* Owning a house or business in your country
\* Having a guaranteed job when you return home
\* Having a spouse, children, or close family at home
\* You will inherit property, a business, or assets in your country
\* Have admission to a major that will allow you to get a job when you return home.
For example, if you major in Aerospace Engineering, an aerospace industry must exist
in your country so that you can find a job after you graduate.
2. You do not have enough money to study in the U.S.
3. You did not bring all required documents with you to the U.S. Embassy for the interview.
4. You lied about something on your visa application or during the visa interview.
5. You failed a security background check (called "Administrative Processing)

title: Visa Tips
text:
**5. Help! I Was Denied a Visa!**

- Visa Denial Help
- If you are denied a visa and would like to try again, you may need to request readmission for a future term and get a new I-20.
- No university in the U.S. can control the outcome of a visa application. We cannot
require the embassy to grant you a visa or influence their decision in any way.

# Transfer Credit Part II

## Transfer Credit Agreements with Wichita State University (Part II)

**STEP 8 -- DETERMINATION OF EQUIVALENCIES**
After you have provided all of the items requested in PART I , we will begin a transfer credit evaluation. This process involves our sending the
syllabus for each subject to the WSU department which offers a comparable class. **The evaluation process can sometimes take more than two months to complete.**

title: Transfer Credit Part II
text:
**STEP 9 -- DEGREE AUDIT EVALUATION AND CREATION OF STUDY PLANS**
After Step 8 is complete, we will use this information to determine whether or not
any transferrable classes meet the degree requirements for the majors you provided
in Step 5 . This process is called a degree audit. It is important to note that not all of the
classes that a student completed previously, even if they are comparable to subjects
offered at WSU, may satisfy the degree requirements for a particular major at WSU.
For example, if a student took a math class at your school and we determined that
it is equivalent to an Algebra class offered at WSU, Algebra would meet a degree requirement
for MANY majors at WSU -- but not for Engineering majors. A degree audit evaluation
will determine the number of subjects (and approximate amount of time) required for
a student to complete their degree at WSU. Both of our institutions would then know
if a 2+2 or 3+1 agreement might be possible. **Degree audit evaluations can take more than one month to complete.**

# Enrollment Deposit and Refund Policy

## Enrollment Deposit and Refund Policy for Undergraduate Applicants

Wichita State University's refund policy for international applicants is as follows:

title: Enrollment Deposit and Refund Policy
text:
- - - **The Undergraduate & Intensive English Application Fee**
The undergraduate & Intensive English application fee is not refundable - even if
the applicant is not accepted for admission.
- **Enrollment Deposit Policy**
- WSU assesses a US$7,000 deposit on those applicants: (1) who are physically located
in ***Bangladesh, Nigeria, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Fujian Province, China*** at the time they submit their application; and/or (2) who provide transcripts from
schools or documents from banks located in the above countries.
- If admissible, you will receive a scanned letter indicating you are admissible and
the I-20 will be prepared once the enrollment deposit is received.
- If a student enrolls in classes at WSU but owes less than the US$7,000 deposit paid
previously, the overpayment will not be refunded. Instead, the overpayment will be
applied to the student's next semester of enrollment.
- If a student transfers to another institution after completing their first semester
of enrollment at WSU, and their deposit has not been fully exhausted, the student
can complete a Refund Request Form .  Any remaining balance will be returned to the student in the manner in which it
was paid.
- The deposit will be used to pay for the student’s tuition, fees, on-campus housing,
and medical insurance after the student has enrolled.
- **How to Pay the Enrollment Deposit** 
The enrollment deposit can be made by a wired payment for those outside of the United
State. Click here for how to pay with a wired payment. If you or your family has a bank account in
the U.S., you can make direct deposit. You will need to login to myWSU and follow the instructions on How do I set up direct deposit? webpage. If you have difficulties logging in to your myWSU, you may contact IT support
on helpdesk@wichita.edu for assistance.
- **Enrollment Deposit Refund Policy**
- If the student fails to enroll, the enrollment deposit is not refundable unless the
student completes a Refund Request Form and agrees to the following terms:  By requesting a refund, the student’s admission
and I-20 will be automatically canceled. Once canceled, the I-20 cannot be used to
enter the U.S.
- Before issuing a refund, Wichita State University will look in SEVIS, a U.S. federal
database, to confirm that the student’s I-20 was not used to enter the U.S. If the
I-20 was used to enter the U.S., the student will not be eligible for a refund of
the enrollment deposit.
- Payments that were made more than two years ago could have been sent to the State
of Kansas as unclaimed property. In that case, students will need to contact the State
of Kansas to request a refund.
- Refunds may take up to 60 days to be processed.

title: Enrollment Deposit and Refund Policy
text:
- - - ******Refund Methods******
If an Applicant qualifies for a refund, the money will be sent as follows:
1) If the original payment was made by credit card, the refund will be credited to
the same credit card.
2) If the original payment was made by international wire transfer through Flywire (formerly peerTransfer), the refund will be processed through Flywire .
3) If the original payment was made by a U.S. bank check, the refund will be processed
through direct deposit to the U.S. bank account upon the student setting up eRefund
in myWSU.
4) If the original payment was made by bank draft or money order, the refund will
be returned by direct deposit to a U.S. bank account assigned by the student who applied
for admission (regardless of who actually paid the money).
- ******Voluntary Prepayment of Tuition******
**IMPORTANT NOTE:** Most students are NOT required to pay their tuition and fees before arriving at Wichita.
However, you can elect to make a prepayment. If you decide to make a payment in advance,
it will be used to pay for WSU tuition, fees, on-campus housing, and medical insurance
purchased through the University. No portion of your prepayment will be refunded to
you to pay for books, off-campus housing, personal expenses, etc. For this reason,
you should bring extra money to pay for these expenses. If the amount of your prepayment
exceeds the amount you owe, any extra amount will be applied to your next semester's
tuition. If you transfer to another school in the U.S., your prepayment will be returned to the original payer in the manner in which it was paid.

text:
# International Transfer Degree Programs

# Wichita State University

# International Transfer and 2+2 Degree Programs

**INTRODUCTION**

In order to explore the possibility of a dual degree program with your school, Wichita
State University (WSU) must first conduct a thorough transfer credit evaluation to
determine if the coursework taken at your school is equivalent to classes offered
at WSU.  Please provide the items below so that we can begin our evaluation:

**STEP 1 -- PROVIDE SYLLABI FOR CLASSES THAT YOU WOULD LIKE US TO EVALUATE**

title: International Transfer Degree Programs
text:
Because of the differences between the educational system in your country and the
American system, we must have syllabi (in English) for all classes that students would
like to transfer to Wichita State University. The syllabi should include as much detailed
information as possible about the material studied in each subject as well as the
amount of time spent in lectures and laboratories.  Syllabus Example

**STEP 2 -- SEND US A TYPICAL TRANSCRIPT FROM YOUR SCHOOL**

Transcripts or marksheets list the classes a person studied as well as the grades
received in each of those classes. It is helpful for us to have a typical transcript
from your school. The transcript needs to be in English.

**STEP 3 -- PROVIDE YOUR SCHOOL CALENDAR**

title: International Transfer Degree Programs
text:
It is always helpful to know the months in which classes normally begin and end at
your school. To help with our transfer credit review, please provide us with your
school's academic calendar.

**STEP 4 -- HOW LONG IT TAKES TO COMPLETE A DEGREE AT YOUR SCHOOL?**

Depending on the school, a typical diploma or degree may take two, three, four, or
even five years to complete. Please let us know how long it typically takes for a
student to complete a diploma/degree at your school for the program you would like
us to evaluate.

**STEP 5 -- WHAT MAJORS WILL YOUR STUDENTS TYPICALLY STUDY AT WSU?**

title: International Transfer Degree Programs
text:
Wichita State University offers more than 200 different majors and specializations .  In order to conduct a transfer credit review, however, we will need to know 15-20
majors that your students would typically want to pursue at Wichita State. Our review

title: Transfer Students
text:
# Transfer Students

# You indicated that:

1) You previously attended WSU
**AND**2) You last attended as an academic student
**AND**3) You are currently in the U.S.
**AND**4) You last attended WSU less than two years ago

---

**STEPS TO TRANSFER BACK TO WICHITA STATE UNIVERSITY**

1) Pay any remaining balance owed to WSU. If you are unsure if you have a balance,
contact  WSUAccountsReceivable@wichita.edu .

2) Complete a new Financial Statement and email it to International Student Services (ISS) at iss@wichita.edu in the Office of International Education. Include in your email your complete name,
date of birth, and myWSU ID (if known), and the semester you intend to resume your
studies at WSU.

Please wait for a reply from ISS. You cannot resume studies at WSU until ISS confirms
you are eligible to return.

title: Transfer Students
text:
3) If you are eligible to return, you will be sent a Transfer Request Form.  Please
complete and return the form to iss@wichita.edu .

4) Once WSU receives your completed Transfer Request Form and your SEVIS record is
transferred to WSU from your previous school, we will issue your transfer pending
I-20.  The I-20 will be emailed to you at the address listed on the Transfer Request
Form.

5) When instructed, complete the SEVIS check-in online for the upcoming term. Once
you submit the check-in, ISS will remove the SEVIS hold from your account. You will
need to clear all holds with other departments before you can enroll.

6) Make arrangements to travel to Wichita.  If you need airport arrival assistance,
please notify us of your travel itinerary . For recommended dates of arrival and more, please read our Pre-Departure Information .

title: Transfer Students
text:
7) You will automatically be charged for medical insurance each semester you enroll
at WSU unless you submit a Medical Insurance Waiver before the deadline. For more
information, please visit Medical Insurance . Be sure you observe the deadline for submitting an insurance waiver- no exceptions
will be made.

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
# Pre-Departure Information

##

## Preparing for Your Arrival: Fall 2025 – Summer 2026

1. Pay the SEVIS Fee

The U.S. Department of Homeland Security **requires** that all F-1 visa applicants pay a nonrefundable US$350 SEVIS Fee at least three days
before they apply for a visa.

You can find more information about the SEVIS Fee by visiting:   https://www.wichita.edu/SEVIS.

2. Apply for a Student Visa

Most students will need to obtain an F-1 visa (student visa) at the nearest U.S. Embassy
or Consulate before coming to Wichita. Depending on the country, obtaining a visa
can range from being quite easy to very difficult. To apply for an F-1 student visa,
you must submit the following to the nearest U.S. Embassy or Consulate:

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
1. Form DS-160 (completed online)
2. Nonrefundable US$160 visa application fee
3. Receipt\* that you paid the US$350 nonrefundable SEVIS fee.  *\*Make sure to keep the receipt and bring it with you to the U.S.*
4. A passport valid for at least 6 months (plus any old passports you may have)
5. A current Form I-20 from Wichita State University
6. A photo (visit: http://travel.state.gov/content/visas/english/general/photos.html for details)
7. Evidence of sufficient funds to study in the U.S. including a bank statement
8. U.S. Visa requirements differ from country to country, find visa information for your
country by visiting:   http://www.usembassy.gov/

Check out our Visa Interview Tips

3. Apply to Live on Campus

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
All first-year students, including undergraduate international students and Intensive
English students (unless otherwise eligible for an exemption under provision two of
this policy statement), must live in Shocker Hall, The Suites, or The Flats during
their first two semesters at Wichita State University.

First-year students who meet one or more of the following criteria are exempt from
living on campus:

1. Twenty-one (21) years of age or older.
2. Transferring 24 or more credit hours.
3. Married and living with spouse.
4. Living with an approved relative (parent/legal guardian, grandparent, aunt or uncle)

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
**We recommend that you make a housing reservation before coming to Wichita.** We require new International Students to arrive at WSU before the residence halls
officially open for the semester. If you are living in Shocker Hall, The Flats, or
The Suites you must email housing@wichita.edu to let them know when you plan to move into your room so they can prepare it as an
early arrival.

Apply for Housing

4. Buy an Airline Ticket

The Wichita airport is called Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport (airport code
ICT). If you are coming from a country outside of the U.S., you will have at least
one connecting flight before arriving in Wichita. We suggest you allow for at least
a 3-hour layover in your first arrival city in the U.S. so that you have sufficient
time for immigration processing, customs inspection, and a required security check
before your connecting flight leaves for Wichita.

day on Friday December 19, 2025, through January 4, 2026. The university will reopen

We offer FREE airport transportation from the Wichita airport. If you would like a
free ride from the airport, fill out the form at: https://www.wichita.edu/arrival at least 48 hours before arrival. **We only provide rides from Wichita Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport and will
not provide pickups from any other airport.** You can choose to take a taxi or Uber/Lyft to the University, taxi fare is approximately
US$30-$40.

If you arrive late and do not arrange airport pickup, you may have to stay in a hotel
for one night at your own expense. There are many hotels near the airport that cost
approximately US$150 per night.

5. Arrive on Campus

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
You will receive further email communication from our office on how to schedule your
check-in time approximately one month before the start of classes. You will not be
allowed to enroll without completing the check-in process.

You will need your passport and I-20 (if you are on an F-1 visa) for check-in. If
you did not submit official transcripts when you applied for admission, please bring
your official final transcripts with you to Wichita. For details on our transcript
requirements, visit: https://wichita.edu/CountryRequirements

All University offices are open Monday - Friday from 8:00am to 5:00pm. Offices are
closed on Saturdays and Sundays.

6. Open a Bank Account

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
After arriving in Wichita, you may open a bank account. We have popular banks nearby
- Campus Credit Union at the Rhatigan Student Center (RSC), Meritrust Credit Union
at Braeburn Square on campus, and Bank of America has a branch next to our campus.
Most of these banks have an ATM located in the RSC.

In order to open an account, you will need to show the bank your passport, your I-20,
and proof of your address in Wichita (such as your housing contract or apartment rental
contract). You will receive an ATM card after opening an account so you can get cash
quickly and easily.

7. Pay Tuition & Fees

Students are not required to pay their tuition and fees before coming to Wichita.
Tuition, fees, and housing payments are charged on a semester-by-semester basis. Payment
deadline is usually two weeks after school starts. There are several options to make
payment to the university:

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
- **Direct Deposit from U.S. Bank Account:** After you open a bank account in the U.S., you can setup direct deposit from your
U.S. bank account to your student account at WSU.
- **Electronic Bank Transfer:** Wichita State University uses a payment platform called Flywire to process international
payments via wire transfers. Please visit our website for details: https://www.wichita.flywire.com/
- **Check, Bank Draft, Money Order, or Traveler’s Checks:** If you bring a check or bank draft with you to Wichita, it is very important that
the check be made payable to “Wichita State University” (and not to you). Your check
should include the address of the bank in the U.S. for collections. If the check is
made payable to you, you may not be able to use the money for 1-2 weeks after the
check is deposited to your bank in the U.S. If your check is for an amount that exceeds
what you owe, any extra amount will be applied to your next semester’s tuition and
will not be refunded to you.

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
**NOTE:** For any student who does not have an existing bank account, for your convenience
you can take your cash and get a cashier’s check at the Campus Credit Union in the
Rhatigan Student Center. Let them know that the cashier’s check is for payment of
your tuition, fees, or housing so that you will not be charged a fee.
- **Credit Card:** If you use a credit card to pay for your tuition, fees, medical insurance, or housing,
a nonrefundable 3% service fee will be added to domestic transactions and 4.25% for
international transactions. Credit cards are accepted online only.
- **Debit Card - VISA, MasterCard:** Payment is available online only through the Student Account Suite. To avoid the 3% - 4.25% fee associated with credit card payments, we encourage you
to pay using electronic check process by entering the bank routing and account number
attached to the debit card. Debit card payments cannot be made to a cashier in the
Accounts Receivable office.
- **Installment Payment Plan:** This allows you to pay for your tuition and fees in smaller installments each semester.
With this plan, you can make a nonrefundable payment of US$130 (which includes a US$30
administrative fee) before the payment deadline in each semester. After the initial
payment of US$130, the balance will be split into three equal installments due on
the 15th of each month. You can arrange the Payment Plan by logging into your WSU
student account.

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
8. Know Your Cost of Education

The cost listed on your I-20 is an estimate. Actual tuition and fees depend on your
major and number of classes you take. The amount you owe will be posted in your WSU
student account. Actual housing expenditures depend on 1) the residence hall or apartment
in which you live, 2) whether you have a roommate, and 3) your meal plan. You should
bring extra money for personal expenses (such as shopping, entertainment, etc.).

Check out undergraduate tuition and fees         Intensive English tuition and fees

9. Learn about Health Matters

Wichita State University requires international students to have medical insurance.
You will be automatically charged for medical insurance unless you can provide proof
of medical insurance coverage from another provider that meets U.S. Affordable Care
Act benefit requirements.

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
A tuberculin (TB) blood test, requiring an initial payment of US$80, is required for
all new students and is given by WSU’s Student Health Service. Please bring your vaccination
records with you to the U.S. If you need any vaccinations when you arrive, your student
health insurance will cover them and you can get them at Student Health.

We recommend that you take care of any existing medical or dental problems at home
since student medical insurance does not cover routine dental work or eye examinations.

Medical Insurance         TB Testing and Routine Medical Care

title: Mission Statement-International Education
text:
# Mission Statement-International Education

## Mission Statement

International Education is the Wichita State University office primarily responsible
for all aspects of interaction with international students and scholars that relate
to two main areas of service: #1- providing support and assistance necessary for them
to achieve their educational and professional goals, and #2- ensuring institutional
compliance with U.S. immigration regulations that govern their visa status.

title: Mission Statement-International Education
text:
This includes marketing WSU in other countries and recruiting international students;
processing international undergraduate and Intensive English Language Center applications;
advising on immigration and personal matters with appropriate referrals; providing
authorized immigration documents; conducting new-student orientations; and arranging
programming for international students involving the WSU campus and Wichita communities.

It also includes obtaining employment authorization, such as the H-1B Specialty Worker
and J-1 Exchange Visitor programs for international faculty and staff.

title: Mission Statement-International Education
text:
In addition to serving international students, scholars, faculty, and staff, International
Education also serves domestic students through its study abroad program. Its function
is to promote the concept of studying outside the U.S. as part of their WSU experience;
to accept and process applications for spending one or more semesters as an international
student at a university in another country; to place qualified applicants in a country
and school of their choice; to conduct a series of advising and pre-departure orientations;
and to oversee the transfer of academic credit to their WSU academic records upon
completion of their overseas studies. WSU maintains student exchange agreements with
15 universities in other countries. WSU students can request placement in any of them,
or be placed at another university through an affiliated program provider.

title: International Student Fee
text:
# International Student Fee

**What is the International Student Fee?**
The International Student Fee is a new, one-time fee of $200 that international students
will be required to pay starting with the Fall Semester 2014. The fee was approved
by the Kansas Board of Regents and is in Wichita State's Comprehensive Fee Schedule.

**Who has to pay it?**
All new international students are required to pay the fee their first semester of
enrollment. They will not have to pay it again regardless of how long they study at
Wichita State. Former students who have been away from WSU for more than one year
will be required to pay the International Student Fee. Exchange students are exempted.

**Is the fee refundable?**
The fee is not refundable after the 100% refund deadline.

title: International Student Fee
text:
**Do other universities charge a special fee to international students?**
Yes. In fact, most of the regents universities in Kansas have charged a special fee
to international students for many, many years.

**What will the fee be used for?**
The fee will be used to pay for items or services that directly or indirectly benefit
international students. Examples of these items may include:

title: International Student Fee
text:
- Salary and benefits for an International Programming Coordinator (who will assist
students with nonimmigration-related issues)
- Salary for a student employee to assist with sponsored students – especially SACM
students.
- New computers and furniture for the student lounge in the Garvey International Center.
- Monthly activities for international students.
- Events during International Education Week.
- Partial sponsorship for events such as Aikya (India Nite), Eid al-Fitr, the Asian
Festival, ISU, Inter-Fest, and more.
- Glacier Tax Prep for International Students.
- Payments to international student associations for new student airport pickups.
- Membership dues for professional international organizations.
- Overtime compensation for international advisors during peak SEVIS processing times.
- Publications for International Student Advisors.
- Professional development including conferences, advisor training, webinars, and teleconferences
so that our office always has the latest immigration-related knowledge.
- Orientation materials (such as welcome bags, blankets, door prizes, etc) and refreshments.
- Emergency supplies for newly arrived students (such as toiletries, linens, clothing,
etc).
- Equipment and specialized software for international offices to maintain international
student records.

title: International Student Fee
text:
**Will Wichita State profit from this fee?**
No. If any money from the collection of this fee is unspent at the end of our fiscal
year in June, a portion of the excess fees will be rolled over to the next fiscal
year (so that we can pay bills at the beginning of the next fiscal year). Any extra
money beyond that will be awarded as scholarships to international students.

title: System Requirements
text:
# System Requirements

When you take classes online, it is important to know that your computer or laptop
meets the system requirements necessary to be successful in your studies.

This page will help you determine what you need to be successful studying Intensive
English Online.

---

## Questions to ask yourself before starting your class:

What web browser should I use?

You will access your classes using Blackboard. The following are web browsers that
support the Blackboard website.

1. Chrome (Desktop versions 49+)
2. Microsoft Edge (Desktop versions 20+)
3. Firefox (Desktop versions 48+)
4. Safari (Desktop versions 9+)

You can also access Blackboard using the browsers above on a mobile phone, but you
should do most of your class work on a desktop computer or laptop.

**Note: Do not use Internet Explorer to access your Blackboard account.**

title: System Requirements
text:
How strong does my Internet connection need to be?

The best connections will use DSL or Cable. Wireless connections are unreliable, so
try to avoid using wireless internet connections when trying to stream instructor
videos or taking a quiz.

Do I need any browser plug-ins? (ex: Java)

Yes. It is possible you will need a browser plug-in such as Java to be successful
in your online classes. Blackboard recommends JRE (Java) versions 7 and 8.

Does my computer/laptop have all necessary updates?

Make sure your computer/laptop is updated. Getting behind on computer updates can
affect how well Blackboard operates on your computer.

---

### Equipment needs

Intensive English Online requires the following equipment for successful completion
of class activities.

title: System Requirements
text:
1. Microphone (can be built into your computer or mobile device)
2. Webcam/Video recording capabilities
1. Some class assignments may require you to record yourself, so having a webcam or other
video device (such as a mobile device or tablet) is necessary.
3. Headphones/earbuds
1. Some class assignments may require you to listen closely; headphone or earbuds will
help reduce distractions.

## Do you have more questions?

Visit the webpage below to get additional information on system requirements.

More Information

title: SEVIS Fee
text:
# SEVIS Fee

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the SEVIS Fee?**
The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) requires people who want F-1
or J-1 visas to pay a one-time SEVIS Fee before applying for a visa. The SEVIS Fee
for F-1 visas is $350. The SEVIS fee for J-1 visas is $220. This is in addition to
the normal visa processing fee of US$160. The SEVIS fee helps to pay for SEVIS (Student
and Exchange Information System) that U.S. schools use to issue I-20 forms (DS-2019s
for J-1s).

**How do I pay the SEVIS Fee?**
The SEVIS I-901 fee can be paid to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) online by credit or debit card, by mail with a check or money order, or by Western Union Quick Pay . To pay your SEVIS Fee, you must have:

title: SEVIS Fee
text:
**Form I-20 for F-1 Visas:**
School Code for Wichita State University: KAN214F00668000
SEVIS Identification Number: Located above the bar code on the right side of your
I-20 starting with "N"

**Form DS-2019 for J-1 Visas:**
Program Code: P-1-01549
SEVIS Identification Number: Located on your DS-2019

To pay your SEVIS Fee, please go to the following website for complete details: https://www.fmjfee.com/i901fee/index.html

**When must I pay the SEVIS Fee?**
The fee should be paid at least three business days before you apply for your visa,
change of status, or reinstatement application.

title: SEVIS Fee
text:
**Can Wichita State University help me to pay my SEVIS Fee?**
No, the SEVIS Fee is not a fee charged by Wichita State University. The SEVIS Fee
is charged by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. The University cannot help
you in any way to pay your SEVIS Fee. For details on how you pay your SEVIS Fee, please
visit: https://www.fmjfee.com/i901fee/index.html

**I have many questions about the SEVIS Fee. Can Wichita State University answer my
questions about the SEVIS Fee? Where can I go for more information?**
The U.S. Government charges the SEVIS Fee and is responsible for making sure you have
all of the information you need to pay the fee. This is an excellent website where
you can get the answers to dozens of questions, please be sure to visit: https://www.ice.gov/sevis/i901/faq

title: SEVIS Fee
text:

Please visit the above website for the latest information on the SEVIS Fee.**

text:
# Engineering Transfers

## Undergraduate Transfer Agreements for Engineering

If we are able to do a 2+2 agreement, students would attend their first 2 years at
your school and then complete their degree after attending 2 additional years at Wichita
State University. If you would like to be considered for a 2+2 agreement with Wichita
State, we must have the items below to begin an evaluation:

**1) Program Overview / Program Description**
Please send general information that introduces your school to us such as when your
school opened, how many programs you offer, accreditation information or recognition
by your Ministry of Education, etc. We also need to know general requirements for
the program you would like us to evaluate, the classes required for graduation, how
many years it typically takes to complete a degree or diploma, and other general information.

title: Engineering Transfers
text:
**2) School Calendar**
The academic calendar for your school tells us when your classes begin and end each
term, when your break periods are, etc.

**3) Typical Transcript**
We need a sample transcript that you would send to us whenever a student applies
to Wichita State. The transcript should list the classes the student has taken and
the grades received in those classes. If desired, you may send a transcript of a real
student. However, please mark out the name of the student and any other identifying
information.

title: Engineering Transfers
text:
**4) Instructional Hours**
How many hours of instruction does a student typically receive per class during one
of your terms or semesters? If your school assigns credit hours to each class, the
transcript you send to us will provide that information. At Wichita State, for example,
most classes are 3 credit hours -- which means that students typically receive 3 hours
of instruction per week for 16 weeks.

**5) Intended Majors**
What majors will most of your students apply to at Wichita State University?

**6) Send the Above Information**
Please send the above information to Michelle.Barger@wichita.edu.

After receipt of the above items, the College of Engineering will conduct a preliminary
review to determine if a transfer agreement might be possible. If yes, we will ask
you to submit detailed syllabi of each class so that we can fully evaluate the classes
you offer.

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
All University offices are open Monday - Friday from 8:00am to 5:00pm, with the exception
of holidays. Offices are closed on Saturdays and Sundays.

Open a Bank Account

After arriving in Wichita, you may open a bank account. We have popular banks nearby
- Campus Credit Union at the Rhatigan Student Center (RSC), Meritrust Credit Union
at Braeburn Square on campus, and Bank of America has a branch next to our campus.
Most of these banks have an ATM located in the RSC.

In order to open an account, you will need to show the bank your passport, your I-20,
and proof of your address in Wichita (such as your housing contract or apartment rental
contract). You will receive an ATM card after opening an account so you can get cash
quickly and easily.

Know the Cost of Your Education

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
The cost listed on your I-20 is an estimate. Actual cost of tuition and fees will
depend on your major and the number of classes you take. The amount you owe will be
posted in your WSU student account. Actual housing expenditures depend on: 1) the
residence hall or apartment in which you live, 2) whether or not you have a roommate,
and 3) your meal plan. You should bring extra money for personal expenses (such as
shopping, entertainment, etc).

Check out undergraduate tuition and fee estimates at http://www.wichita.edu/UGExpenses or Intensive English tuition and fees at http://www.wichita.edu/IEExpenses .

Pay Tuition and Fees

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
Students are not required to pay their tuition and fees before coming to Wichita.
Tuition, fees, and housing payments are charged on a semester-by-semester basis. Deadline
for payment is usually two weeks after school starts. There are several options to
make payment to the university:

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
- **Direct Deposit from U.S. Bank Account**: After you open a bank account in the U.S., you can setup direct deposit from your
U.S. bank account to your student account at WSU.
- **Electronic Bank Transfer**: Wichita State University uses a payment platform called Flywire to process international
payments via wire transfers. Please visit our website for details of wire transfers .
- **Check, Bank Draft, Money Order, or Traveler’s Checks**: If you bring a check or bank draft with you to Wichita, it is very important that
the check be made payable to “Wichita State University” (and not to you). Your check
should include the address of the bank in the U.S. for collections. If the check is
made payable to you, you may not be able to use the money for 1-2 weeks after the
check is deposited to your bank in the U.S. If your check is for an amount that exceeds
what you owe, any extra amount will be applied to your next semester’s tuition and
will not be refunded to you.

title: Pre-Departure Information
text:
**NOTE:** For any student who does not have an existing bank account or has been restricted
to pay by personal check, for your convenience you can take your cash and get a cashier’s
check at the Campus Credit Union (located next to the University Police Department).
Let them know that the cashier’s check is for payment of your tuition, fees, or housing
so that you will not be charged a fee.
- **Credit Card**: If you use a credit card to pay for your tuition, fees, medical insurance, or housing,
a nonrefundable 3% service fee will be added to domestic transactions and 4.25% for
international transactions. Credit cards are accepted online only.
- **Debit Card - VISA, MasterCard**: Payment is made online only by going to the  Student Account Suite . To avoid the 3% - 4.25% fee associated with credit card payments, we encourage you
to pay using electronic check process by entering the bank routing and account number
attached to the debit card. Debit card payments cannot be made to a cashier in the
Accounts Receivable office.
- **Installment Payment Plan**: This allows you to pay for your tuition and fees in smaller installments each semester.
With this plan, you can make a nonrefundable payment of US$130 (which includes a US$30
administrative fee) before the payment deadline in each semester. After the initial
payment of US$130, the balance will be split into three equal installments due on
the 15th of each month. You can arrange the Payment Plan by logging into your WSU
student account.

title: Location and Weather
text:
# Location and Weather

##

## Location & Weather

---

## City and State

City Population: 630,000
Size in Area: 423 sq km
Campus to Airport: 20 minutes

Wichita is the largest city in Kansas. It is the cultural, industrial, and financial
center of Kansas. The city has a top-rated symphony orchestra, ballet, beautiful parks,
and interesting museums. More than 800 corporations conduct international trade in
the city and Wichita Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport (ICT) is one of the fastest-growing
airports in the nation.

title: Location and Weather
text:
Wichita is known for its warm and friendly people, good schools, and low crime rate.
The city has been given the prestigious All-American City award three times. This
award is given to the 10 best cities in the U.S. Kansas has also been cited as being
the 4th most livable state in America because of its attractive employment opportunities,
quality education, affordable housing, and strong economy.

## Weather

Wichita enjoys four seasons a year. Spring has mild temperatures and the city receives
rain more often during this season than any other time of the year. Thousands of flowers
bloom on the campus during the spring. Summer is hot and somewhat humid with bright
and sunny days. Fall has mild temperatures and the city is especially colorful during
this season. Winter is our coldest season and light snowfall occurs every few weeks.

# Request Readmission

**You indicated that:**
1) You previously attended WSU
**AND**
2) You last attended as an academic student
**AND**
3) You are NOT currently in the U.S.
**AND**
4) You last attended WSU two years ago or longer (or you could not remember when
you last enrolled)

---

**STEPS TO RETURN TO WICHITA STATE UNIVERSITY**

In order to transfer to Wichita State University, please do the following:

1) Request Reactivation  by following the instructions on the Registrar's Office website.  After requesting
reactivation, an employee in the Registrar's Office will contact you. As you will
see on the above Web page, you must provide official transcripts from any school you
attended after you last attended WSU. **WSU cannot determine your eligibility to return until all needed transcripts have
been received.**

title: Request Readmission
text:
2) Complete a new Financial Statement and return it to the address on the form.

3) Email International Student Services (ISS) at iss@wichita.edu about your desire to return to WSU.

Please wait for a reply from ISS. You cannot transfer back to WSU until ISS confirms
you are eligible to return.

4) If you are eligible to return, you will be sent an I-20 to re-enter the U.S. to
attend Wichita State University.

5) Read our Pre-Departure Information . The Pre-Departure Information will explain how to apply for a visa, pay the SEVIS
fee, make arrangements to travel to Wichita, and more.

title: ACIREMA Workshop
text:
# ACIREMA Workshop

## ACIREMA Workshop

---

**What is ACIREMA?**
ACIREMA (America spelled backwards) is a workshop that includes a simulation exercise
designed to sensitize participants to the months of difficulties that international
students encounter in their quest for a U.S. education. It acquaints the participants
with the procedures and obstacles students must follow from the initial contact with
a U.S. educational institution to their arrival on campus. A facilitated discussion
takes place after the simulation to address the specific issues at stake, as well
as what participants can do in the future to help support international students at
Wichita State University.

**Workshop Schedule**
***Dates:*** Friday, April 1, 2022
***Time:*** 12:15 - 1:45 p.m., 12:30 - 2 p.m., 12:45 - 2:15 p.m., 1 - 2:30 p.m.
***Location:*** Rhatigan Student Center, 2nd floor, Room 226 Pike Room

---

title: J-1 Exchange Visitors
text:
# J-1 Exchange Visitors

## Bringing Exchange Visitors to Wichita State

### When completing required forms, download the form and open it in Adobe Acrobat. Do not fill out the forms directly in your browser.

### STEP 1

The prospective Exchange Visitor should make initial contact with an academic department
at WSU.

### STEP 2

If the department is interested in potentially hosting the visitor, the department
should request the prospective Exchange Visitor to complete an Exchange Visitor Application . For more information about the different categories of exchange visitors that WSU
is approved to host, please visit www.wichita.edu/J-1categories .

### STEP 3

The prospective visitor should complete the Exchange Visitor Application and return it to the department with the following documents:

title: J-1 Exchange Visitors
text:
- Dependent Information for Exchange Visitors Form (if bringing dependents)
- Passport copies for exchange visitor and any dependents
- Sponsorship documentation (if being sponsored by a university, government, or organization)
- Copy of diploma or any English test scores from Part D of the Exchange Visitor Application
- Curriculum Vitae (CV) or résumé

### STEP 4

The department reviews the application and supporting documents to determine if they
would like to host the visitor.

### STEP 5

title: J-1 Exchange Visitors
text:
If the WSU department decides to host the visitor, the DS-2019 Request Form must be completed. After Parts A-E have been completed, the department chair will
need to initial by each number in Part F (numbers 9-20 are only required for the student
intern category) and sign in Part G. In order to complete the form, the department
must determine if it will financially sponsor the visitor and, if so, the amount of
sponsorship. In addition, the department must obtain evidence that the Exchange Visitor
has sufficient English to participate in the exchange program. The department will
need to conduct an interview with the exchange visitor and complete the J-1 English Proficiency Evaluation if the visitor does not have other acceptable evidence of English proficiency. See
the DS-2019 Request Form for more details.

title: J-1 Exchange Visitors
text:
As part of the DS-2019 Request Form, the department will also need to draft the department
invitation letter. A link to a sample invitation letter can be found on the DS-2019
Request Form. The invitation letter should not be shared with the exchange visitor
until the given department has been granted approval to do so (Step 8).

The university offers instructions for Adobe Digital Signatures here .

### STEP 6

The department should print all documents and send them to the college dean for approval.
The documents should include:

title: J-1 Exchange Visitors
text:
- DS-2019 Request Form
- Department Invitation Letter ( Sample)
- J-1 English Proficiency Evaluation (if used to verify English proficiency) with list of interview questions, if applicable
- Exchange Visitor Application
- Dependent Information for Exchange Visitors Form (if visitor is bringing dependents)
- Passport copies for exchange students and any dependents
- Sponsorship documentation (if visitor is being sponsored by an outside university,
government, or organization)
- Copy of diploma or any English test scores (if used to verify English proficiency)
- Curriculum Vitae (CV) or résumé

### STEP 7

title: J-1 Exchange Visitors
text:
The college dean will review all documentation. If approved, the dean will sign the
DS-2019 Request Form and forward the documentation on for the next approval signature
according to the instructions in Part G of the DS-2019 Request Form. Ultimately, the
documents will be reviewed and approved by the Office of Export Controls and Compliance,
the Office of General Counsel, and the Office of Academic Affairs before finally being
sent to Tonya Baldwin at the Office of International Education.

### STEP 8

Tonya Baldwin will email the department to notify them that the exchange visitor request
has been approved and that the department can share the invitation letter with the
exchange visitor.

### STEP 9 (Student Intern category only)

title: J-1 Exchange Visitors
text:
If the visitor will be coming under the Student Intern category, the department must
also complete the Form DS-7002, Training/Internship Placement Plan . See the Guide to Form DS-7002 for details on how to complete the form. The department should send the completed
Form DS-7002, Training/Internship Placement Plan to the visitor to sign. The exchange
visitor should provide a copy of this document to his/her home institution and request
that the institution complete the Home Institution Certification Form . The exchange visitor should send the signed DS-7002 and the completed Home Institution
Certification Form to Tonya Baldwin in the Office of International Education at tonya.baldwin@wichita.edu .

### STEP 10

Tonya Baldwin will email the exchange visitor (and copy the department) the following:

title: J-1 Exchange Visitors
text:
- A Certification of Financial Support for the exchange visitor to sign and return with,
if applicable, evidence of financial support.
- Information about purchasing WSU medical insurance.

### STEP 11

Once Tonya Baldwin receives the completed Certification of Financial Support and funds
for the WSU medical insurance, she will prepare the Form DS-2019 and send it to the
department or directly to the exchange visitor as indicated on DS-2019 Request Form.
For visitors coming under the Student Intern category, the Office of International
Education will also send the final DS-7002 signed by the Responsible Officer.

### STEP 12

The exchange visitor pays the I-901 SEVIS fee and applies for a J-1 visa. After obtaining a visa, the visitor should make arrangements
to come to WSU.

title: Autonomous University of Chihuahua (UACH)
text:
# Autonomous University of Chihuahua (UACH)

# Wichita State University / Autonomous University of Chihuahua

# Dual Degree Program

**INTRODUCTION**

Wichita State University (WSU) is excited about the possibility of developing a dual
degree program with the Autonomous University of Chihuahua (Universidad Autónoma de
Chihuahua or UACH).  To explore if this type of agreement is possible, WSU must first
conduct a thorough transfer credit evaluation to determine if the classes taken at
UACH are equivalent to classes offered at WSU.  In order to begin an evaluation, please
follow the steps below:

**STEP 1 - GATHER SYLLABI FOR CLASSES THAT YOU WOULD LIKE US TO EVALUATE**

title: Autonomous University of Chihuahua (UACH)
text:
Because of the differences between the educational system in Mexico and the U.S.,
we must have syllabi (in English) for all classes that students would typically take
at UACH as part of the dual degree program.  The syllabi should include as much detailed
information as possible about the material studied in each subject as well as the
amount of time spent in lectures and laboratories.  Example of a Syllabus

**STEP 2 - COLLECT A TYPICAL UACH TRANSCRIPT**

It is helpful for us to have a typical transcript from UACH so that we can see grades
(and a grading scale), course numbers, and credit hours/units (if applicable). The
transcript should be in English.

**STEP 3 - PROVIDE YOUR SCHOOL CALENDAR**

title: Autonomous University of Chihuahua (UACH)
text:
When conducting an evaluation, it will be helpful for us to know the months during
which classes are normally in session at UACH.  For this reason, please provide your
school's academic calendar.

**STEP 4 - SEND THE ABOVE ITEMS TO WICHITA STATE UNIVERSITY**

Please send the above items to Ms. Michelle Barger at intltransfer.eval@wichita.edu
or post to:

Ms. Michelle Barger
Office of International Education
Wichita State University
1845 Fairmount Street
Wichita, Kansas 67260-0122
USA

Telephone: +1-316-978-3232

**STEP 5 - DETERMINATION OF COURSE EQUIVALENCIES**

After you have provided all of the items in Steps 1 to 3, Wichita State University
will begin a transfer credit evaluation. This process involves our sending the UACH
syllabus for each subject to the WSU department which offers a comparable class.

**STEP 6 - DEGREE AUDIT EVALUATION AND CREATION OF STUDY PLANS**

title: Autonomous University of Chihuahua (UACH)
text:
After Step 5 is complete, we will use this information to determine which UACH classes
meet the degree requirements for the majors included in our agreement.  This process
is called a degree audit. It is important to note that not all of the classes that
a student completed previously, even if they are comparable to subjects offered at
WSU, may satisfy the degree requirements for a particular major at WSU. For example,
if a student took a math class at your school and we determined that it is equivalent
to an Algebra class offered at WSU, Algebra would meet a degree requirement for many
majors at WSU -- but not necessarily for Engineering majors. A degree audit evaluation
will determine the number of subjects (and approximate amount of time) required for
a student to complete their degree at WSU.  Wichita State University is interested
in pursuing dual degree programs for the following majors offered at WSU:

title: Autonomous University of Chihuahua (UACH)
text:
**Liberal Arts and Sciences**
• Bachelor’s Degree in Chemistry
• Bachelor of Communication Sciences 
• Bachelor of Arts in Hispanic American Literature

**Barton School of Business**
• Bachelor of Business Administration
• Bachelor of International Business

**College of Fine Arts**
• Bachelor of Visual Arts
• Bachelor’s degree in Audiovisual Production

**College of Engineering**
• Bachelor of Aerospace Engineering
• Bachelor’s Degree in Industrial Process Engineering

**NOTE:** If a UACH student is interested in pursuing a major at WSU that is not listed above,
we would be happy to consider the student for admission and conduct an individualized
degree audit for that particular student.  The student would then know how long it
will take to graduate from Wichita State University with a major that is not included
in our agreement.
