# Request Readmission

**You indicated that:**
1) You previously attended WSU
**AND**
2) You last attended as an IELC student
**AND**
3) You are currently in the U.S.

---

**STEPS TO RETURN TO WSU**

1) Please complete our Readmission Form to indicate your desire to return to WSU.

2) After you submit the Readmission Form, your Admissions Officer will contact you
about any items that are needed.

3) If you are accepted for admission, you will be sent a Transfer Request Form with
your admission documents. Please complete the top part of the Transfer Request Form
and ask an International Student Advisor at your current school to complete the bottom
portion of the Transfer Request Form.

title: Request Readmission
text:
4) Once WSU receives your completed Transfer Request Form and electronic SEVIS record
from your previous school, we will issue your transfer pending I-20. The I-20 will
either be mailed to your current address or kept at the Garvey International Center
for you to pick up according to which option you indicated on the Transfer Request
Form.

5) Read our Pre-Departure Information and make arrangements to come to Wichita. Notify us of your travel itinerary.

6) Upon arriving in Wichita, you should come to the Garvey International Center to
complete the new student check-in process which will begin approximately three weeks
before the semester begins. Bring your passport and I-20 from your previous institution.
During check-in, you will receive information about new student orientation, academic
advising, and more.

title: Request Readmission
text:
7) You will automatically be charged for medical insurance each semester you enroll
at WSU unless you submit a Medical Insurance Waiver before the deadline. Be sure you observe the deadline for submitting an insurance
waiver- no exceptions will be made.

title: Transfer Students
text:
# Transfer Students

**You indicated that**:
1) You previously attended WSU
**AND**2) You last attended as an academic student
**AND**3) You are currently in the U.S.
**AND**4) You last attended WSU two years ago or longer (or you were not sure when you last
enrolled)

---

**STEPS TO TRANSFER BACK TO WICHITA STATE UNIVERSITY**

1) Pay any remaining balance owed to WSU. If you are unsure if you have a remaining
balance, contact WSUAccountsReceivable@wichita.edu .

2)  Request Reactivation  by following the instructions on the Registrar's Office website.  After requesting
reactivation, an employee in the Registrar's Office will contact you. As you will
see on the above web page, you must provide to the Registrar official transcripts
from any school you attended after you last attended WSU. WSU cannot determine your
eligibility to return until all needed transcripts have been received.

title: Transfer Students
text:
3) Once your reactivation has been confirmed, complete a new Financial Statement and email it to International Student Services (ISS) at iss@wichita.edu in the Office of International Education. Include in your email your complete name,
date of birth, and myWSU ID (if known), and the semester you intend to resume your
studies at WSU.

Please wait for a reply from ISS. You cannot transfer back to WSU until ISS confirms
you are eligible to return.

4) If you are eligible to return, you will be sent a Transfer Request Form.  Complete
and return the form to iss@wichita.edu .

5) Once WSU receives your completed Transfer Request Form and your SEVIS record has
been transferred to WSU from your previous school, we will issue your transfer pending
I-20.  The I-20 will be emailed to you at the email address you listed on the Transfer
Request Form.

title: Transfer Students
text:
6) When instructed, complete the SEVIS check-in online for the upcoming term. Once
you submit the check-in, ISS will remove the SEVIS hold from your account. You will
need to clear all holds with other departments before you can enroll.

7) Make arrangements to travel to Wichita.  If you need airport arrival assistance,
please notify us of your travel itinerary . For recommended dates of arrival and more, please read our Pre-Departure Information .

8) You will automatically be charged for medical insurance each semester you enroll
at WSU unless you submit a Medical Insurance Waiver before the deadline. For more
information, please visit Medical Insurance . Be sure you observe the deadline for submitting an insurance waiver- no exceptions
will be made.

title: International Students FAQ
text:
# International Students FAQ

## Frequently Asked Questions from International Students

Before Applying Money Matters Submitting an Application Conditional Admission English Requirements After Admission/Pre-departure After Arrival

Before Applying

1. Can I find out if I will be accepted before I apply for admission?

No. Pre-evaluation of documents are not given before you apply for admission. You
must formally apply for admission and submit the required application materials before
your application will be evaluated.

Students are encouraged to review our admission requirements to see if they are likely to be eligible for admission.

2. Is admission guaranteed if I apply and submit all required documents?

No. Wichita State University cannot guarantee admission. An admission decision is
determined based on the evaluation of a student’s application and related documents.

title: International Students FAQ
text:
3. Can I email application materials such as transcripts, test scores, etc.?

The preferred method of submitting application materials is through your personal
application status portal . This is a secure way to submit all of your application materials.

4. Can I find out how many credits will transfer from my previous school before I
apply?

Evaluation of transfer credits does not begin until you have applied and are accepted
for admission to Wichita State University. The process of evaluating transfer credit
can take up to two months to complete depending on how many credits you request to
transfer. Please plan accordingly. For additional information regarding how transfer
credit from international schools is awarded, please click here .

title: International Students FAQ
text:
If you are seeking transfer credit from some U.S. universities or an American Degree
Transfer Program, you may be able to estimate how many of your credits will transfer
by using our transfer gateway portal . Please note that this portal does not necessarily contain a comprehensive list of
every course at every school, only those that have been previously evaluated.

5. What is the minimum GPA required for admission?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
The ***undergraduate*** minimum GPA requirement for admission is 2.5 on a 4.0 grading scale or the international
equivalent. GPA is not the only factor taken into consideration when a student applies.
If a student does not meet the minimum GPA requirement for admission, they can submit
SAT or ACT scores for consideration instead. Students must formally apply and submit transcripts and/or
test scores in order for the Office of International Education to determine if they
are eligible for admission to Wichita State.

GPA requirements for admission to the Graduate School vary by major and range from 2.75 - 3.00 on a 4.0 grading scale.

6. Can I apply with a 3-Year Bachelor's Degree?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
3-year degrees are accepted for admission to some graduate programs . Pre-evaluations are not available. Interested students must formally apply for graduate
admission to find out if their 3-year degree will be accepted for their program of
interest. Admission requirements vary by program.

For information on acceptable 3-year bachelor’s degrees, please contact the graduate
school at wsugradschool@wichita.edu .

7. How long will it take to complete my degree/program?

**Undergraduate**

Most bachelor's degrees require about 4 years to complete. This estimate depends on
how many credit hours a student takes per semester. Students who wish to graduate
in the estimated 4 years should take at least 15 credit hours per semester. Students
will also meet with an academic advisor to decide their plan of study.

**Intensive English**

title: International Students FAQ
text:
There are 7 levels of Intensive English. Each level lasts 8 weeks or approximately
half an academic semester. The length of time a student studies in Intensive English
depends on the individual’s level of English proficiency at the beginning of their
study.

**Graduate**

Most graduate programs will last about 2 years, but the actual duration depends on
a student’s personal plan of study.

8. What are the minimum/maximum number of credit hours I can transfer to Wichita State?

**Undergraduate**

There is no minimum number of credit hours you can transfer to Wichita State. The
maximum number of credit hours you can transfer is 60 from a 2-year college or 90
credit hours from a 4-year university.

Note that it is not guaranteed that all of your transfer credits will apply toward
your intended degree program at Wichita State.

**Graduate**

title: International Students FAQ
text:
Please contact the Graduate School for more information about transfer credit for
graduate degree level coursework.

9. Can I apply before I graduate from high school?

Yes. You can apply for admission to Wichita State before you finish high school. Most
students will begin applying to universities approximately one year or one semester
before they intend to graduate from high school.

Once you complete your high school education, our office will ask for final scores
and/or grades to confirm you still meet Wichita State’s standards for admission.

10. Is a GRE or GMAT required for my graduate application?

GRE or GMAT is required for some graduate programs in order to apply for admission.
View admission requirements for your program of interest.

11. Is a SAT or ACT score required to apply?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
No. You are not required to take an SAT or ACT to apply, but is an option for Freshman Admission . SAT or ACT scores can also be used for determining English proficiency and beginning
coursework in Math and English if you are admitted to Wichita State. If you have these
scores, we encourage you to request them be sent to Wichita State University.

Back to Top

Money Matters

1. Can I have an application fee waiver?

No, Wichita State University does not provide application fee waivers. Applications
and related materials will not be considered without an application fee. Wichita State
University understands currency exchange is difficult in certain countries, however,
submission of an application fee is still required.

The application fee cannot be paid after you get admission or after you arrive.

2. How do I pay the application fee if I don’t have a credit card?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
**Undergraduate or Intensive English:**

Students who are unable to pay by credit card can use our payment partner, Flywire , to pay their application fee.

**Graduate:**

View information about the graduate application fee.

3. Why am I being asked to pay an application fee when I already paid through CommonApp?

It can take Wichita State University several days to receive application fee payments
made through CommonApp. Please allow up to one week for your application fee payment
to be received.

4. Why is my payment through Flywire not showing in my student account?

Flywire allows students/payers to track the status of their payment. It can take 1-2
days for the university to reconcile payments and post to your student account after
the payment is received from Flywire.

5. What financial documents do I need to apply?

**Undergraduate or Intensive English:**

title: International Students FAQ
text:
The Certification of Financial Support Form must be submitted with all applications. An instructional video walking through how
to complete a Certification of Financial Support can be found here . Bank statements or other financial documents will also accompany this form and are
required. A list of acceptable financial documents can be found here .

**Graduate:**

The Graduate Certification of Financial Support Form must be submitted with all graduate applications. Instructions for completing this
form are on the form.

6. What is the estimated cost of attendance?

An updated cost estimate is released every academic year. Exact cost estimates for
a full 4-year degree are not available, as there are too many variables that may influence
the cost of your education over a 4 years.

**Undergraduate:** View Costs

**Intensive English:** View Costs

**Graduate:** View Costs

title: International Students FAQ
text:
7.Can you tell me what the exact cost of my bill will be?

No. We cannot give an exact cost for any student’s studies at Wichita State University.
The exact cost of study will depend on your major, what classes you take, and how
many classes you take each semester. Please review our estimated costs for a general
idea of the expected costs for the current academic year.

Undergraduate Costs

Intensive English Costs

Graduate Costs

8. How much funding do I need to show the U.S. Embassy?

**Undergraduate or Intensive English:**

See the amount shown on your personalized Certification of Financial Support Form . This is the minimum amount the U.S. Embassy will expect to see.

**Graduate:**

See the amount shown on your personalized Graduate Certification of Financial Support Form . This is the minimum amount the U.S. Embassy will expect to see.

9. Is an enrollment deposit required?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
An enrollment deposit is required for applicants from Nigeria , Democratic Republic of Congo , Fujian, China , and Bangladesh before an I-20 will be sent. The payment of an enrollment deposit improves chances
of being granted a visa in these countries or provinces.

If desired, students who are not from one of the four countries or provinces above
may pay tuition in advance to improve chances of receiving a visa. The student may
choose the amount they wish to pay. Learn about payment options here .

View Wichita State University's policy for the refund of enrollment deposits and advanced tuition .

10. What is Wichita State University’s bank account information?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
Wichita State University does not share its bank account information. To send payments
to the university, students should use our international payment portal, Flywire , to make payments in local currency or in U.S. dollars through bank transfer or credit
card. In countries that require government approval to send money to the U.S., Flywire
helps students prepare required forms and paperwork for payment. If you have questions
about the payment process you may reach out to the Flywire customer support team at
support@flywire.com for assistance.

11. What scholarships and financial aid are available?

As a U.S. public university, Wichita State does not offer full scholarships. Please
view links to scholarships and other financial aid opportunities below.

**Undergraduate:**

Global Select Scholarship *\*most popular\** Scholarships and other Financial Aid

**Intensive English:**

title: International Students FAQ
text:
Not eligible for scholarship assistance.

**Graduate:**

Assistantships
Graduate School Awards
Global Select Scholarship

12. What are my job opportunities while in the United States?

Wichita State University has 250+ unique employers on-campus. There are many immigration
laws that determine an international student’s work eligibility in the United States.
Please review the information below to learn about your work eligibility while in
the U.S.

Employment Information for Undergraduate or Intensive English students

Learn about graduate assistantships

13. Do I need to pay the full amount of my tuition all at once?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
No. Wichita State University offers a payment plan for students where they may pay
their tuition in installments. A US$30 administrative fee is charged for the set-up
of the payment plan. Students cannot apply for a payment plan until after arriving
in Wichita and enrolling in classes, which will determine the total cost of tuition
for the semester. Amount of payments cannot be calculated prior to the selection of
classes. Housing expenses are not included in the tuition payment plan.

**IMPORTANT:** You must choose to enroll in the payment plan each semester. This is not done automatically.
Visit your Student Account Suite in your myWSU portal under the myFinances tab to
enroll in and set-up the payment plan option.

Payment schedule:

title: International Students FAQ
text:
*Fall Semester:* First payment due in August after selecting classes then September 15, October 15,
and November 15.
*Spring Semester:* First payment due in January after selecting classes then February 15, March 15,
and April 15.
*Summer Session:* First payment due in June after selecting classes then July 15

14. Are graduate assistantships available?

Wichita State University provides assistantships to graduate students each year. However,
graduate assistantships cannot be guaranteed. All students must submit an assistantship
application to be considered.

Learn more

15. What is the SEVIS fee and how do I pay?

The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) requires people who want F-1
or J-1 visas to pay a one-time SEVIS Fee before applying for a visa.

Get more information about the SEVIS fee including how to pay here .

16. Can I get a refund?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
We provide a detailed refund policy regarding the payment of advanced tuition, application
fees, and enrollment deposits.

View Details

Back to Top

Submitting an Application

1. How do I apply?

**Undergraduate or Intensive English:** Steps to Apply

**Graduate:**

1) Apply for Admission
2) Submit all materials required for the student's major (such as letters of recommendation,
GMAT or GRE scores, etc). Admission Requirements by Major

2. What are the admission requirements?

**Undergraduate:**

Freshman Admission : Minimum GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 grading scale or international equivalent.

Transfer Admission : GPA requirements vary by major.

Also review our list of Required Application Materials .

**Graduate:**

View Admission Requirements by Major

3. What are the intake deadlines?

Undergraduate intakes :  Spring, Summer, and Fall

title: International Students FAQ
text:
Intensive English intakes : Spring, March, Summer, Fall, and October

Graduate intakes : Spring and Fall

4. When does my semester start and end?

**Fall Semester:** mid-August – mid-December
**Spring Semester:** mid-January – mid-May
**Summer Semester:** June-July

Exact start and end dates for upcoming semesters can be found here . You should plan to arrive to Wichita State based on the recommended arrival dates
for your intended semester found under the “Buy an Airline Ticket” heading on our
pre-departure information page .

5. What majors/degrees are offered?

Wichita State University offers more than 225 majors and specializations. Find the
major that is right for you!

Undergraduate

Graduate

6. Do I need a letter of recommendation for my application?

**Undergraduate:** Letters of recommendation are not required.

title: International Students FAQ
text:
**Graduate:** A letter of recommendation is required for a few majors. View graduate admission requirements for your program of interest to see if a letter of recommendation is required.

7. How fast will I get a decision on my application?

Wichita State University offers three different service levels for our *undergraduate* international applicants. Each level relates to a specific application deadline.
Depending on the service level you select, application processing can take anywhere
from 5 weeks to 3 business days. These service levels and processing times do not
apply to graduate applications, as graduate applications are processed by Wichita
State University’s Graduate School.

View Details

8. How can I get updates on the status of my application?

**Undergraduate:**

title: International Students FAQ
text:
After we review your application, we will automatically send an e-mail message to
you to let you know your application status. In our message, we will let you know
if you have been accepted, denied, or if we are missing any required application materials.
We will also send you periodic reminders and other correspondence by e-mail. For this
reason, it is VERY important that you check your e-mail often for updates from Wichita
State University. You can also check your application status at any time through your
application status portal .

**Graduate:**

For updates on your graduate application, please contact the Graduate School or view your application status portal.

9. How can I send my test scores?

**Undergraduate:**

title: International Students FAQ
text:
*English test scores:* Can be submitted to our Office of International Education and we will verify your
score with your testing company. Certain test scores must be submitted directly from
the testing agency, such as Duolingo English Test scores.

*SAT scores:* To be considered official, SAT score reports must be received from College Board.

*All other test scores:* Please review our requirements for your country here .

**Graduate:**

Please review the graduate school application checklist to determine how your test scores should be submitted.

Back to Top

Conditional Admission & English Proficiency

1. What does it mean if I receive conditional admission?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
Students who receive conditional admission to Wichita State University meet our academic
requirements for admission, but DO NOT meet our English proficiency requirement for
admission to an academic program or have not submitted an English proficiency score.

Students with conditional admission receive an I-20 listing Intensive English as their
area of study and their academic major. Students who wish to receive an I-20 listing
only their academic program should submit an approved English test score .

**Undergraduate:**

If granted Conditional Admission, you must sit for the English Proficiency Exam (EPE)
after arrival in Wichita, if no other acceptable English test score is submitted.
If you pass, you will begin full-time academic study in your major. If you do not
pass, you must study in Intensive English until you meet the undergraduate English requirement .

**Graduate:**

title: International Students FAQ
text:
If you have not met our English requirement, you MUST apply for both graduate admission
AND to Intensive English. No I-20 will be issued until:

1) You submit an approved English test score that meets the English proficiency requirement.

*OR*

2) You apply to Intensive English .

You must meet our English requirement before beginning graduate classes. If the GMAT or GRE is required for admission,
official scores must be submitted before an admission is made. Please review the graduate admission requirements for your program of interest to see if a GMAT or GRE score is required for admission.

2. What is your English requirement?

**Undergraduate:** Ways to Demonstrate English Proficiency

**Graduate:**

*TOEFL iBT*: 79 for most majors

*IELTS*: 6.5 for most majors

View majors with a higher English requirement .

title: International Students FAQ
text:
Test scores must be sent to Wichita State directly from the testing company.

3. Do I have to apply to your ESL program?

**Undergraduate:**

If you have met the undergraduate English requirement, you do not need to apply to
Intensive English.

If you have not met the English requirement before arriving at Wichita State, you
are not automatically required to apply to Intensive English. If you have not met
our English requirement by the time you arrive in Wichita, we will test your English
before you begin classes. If you pass our English test, you will begin full-time study
in your academic major. If you do not pass, you will be required to study in Intensive
English.

**Graduate:**

title: International Students FAQ
text:
If you have met the graduate English requirement, you do not need to apply to Intensive
English. However, if you have not met the English Requirement at the time you apply
for graduate admission, you should apply to Intensive English as well. The Graduate
School will not issue and I-20 until:

1) You submit an approved English test score that meets the English proficiency requirement.

*OR*

2) You apply to Intensive English .

Your I-20 will be for Intensive English and not your academic major.

Back to Top

After Admission & Pre-departure

1. Do I need to receive any vaccinations before I travel to the U.S.?

International travelers are NOT required to show proof of full COVID-19 vaccination
prior to boarding their flight to the United States. View Details

title: International Students FAQ
text:
If you plan to live in one of Wichita State University’s residence halls, you must
be vaccinated for meningitis. We recommend that you get the meningitis vaccine before
coming to the U.S. If you get the vaccine in your country, you must bring proof of
your vaccination with you to the U.S. If desired, you may get the meningitis vaccine from Student Health Services. If you purchase medical insurance through WSU, you
will not be charged for the vaccine.

2. What airport should I fly to?

Your final destination should be Wichita, Kansas (Airport Code: ICT).

For undergraduate students: After you are accepted, we will enclose Pre-Departure information with your I-20 that includes airport arrival details and recommended dates of arrival.

3. Will you come pick me up when I arrive?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
Yes, you can request pick-up from the airport for free. Airport pick-up cannot be
guaranteed, as it is dependent on the number of volunteer drivers available. You will
be notified if your request for pick-up could not be fulfilled.

Please complete the airport pickup form so we know when to expect you.

4. Do I need to purchase my own medical insurance?

You will be automatically charged for medical insurance unless you can provide proof
of medical insurance coverage from another provider that meets U.S. Affordable Care
Act benefit requirements.

Learn more

5. How do I apply for on-campus housing?

Follow the instructions for reserving your on-campus room by selecting “Apply Now”
on Wichita State’s housing webpage . We encourage you to wait to submit your housing application until after you know
if you have been granted a visa for study at Wichita State.

title: International Students FAQ
text:
Note: On-Campus housing is not available for married students or students with children.
Married students or students with children will need to find housing accommodations off campus .

6. Can I live off-campus?

All first-year students at Wichita State University are required live on campus for
their first year of study. Also note that homestays are not available.

Exceptions to living on-campus:

1. You plan to live with a family member who is one of the following: parent, legal
guardian, aunt, uncle, or grandparent.
2. You are 21 or older.
3. You are married and/or have children you will be living with.
4. You have 24 or more transferable credit hours.

Living Off-campus :

title: International Students FAQ
text:
Students who want to live off campus must complete a Housing Exemption request form.
To access the form, log in to your myWSU portal , and select **Campus** **Housing** from the *Student Tools* box in the center of the screen. Next, select **Manage My Forms**at the top of the page and use the **Form Selector** to find the Exemption Request form. Fill out the rest of the request form as prompted.
A Housing staff member will respond to your request within 3 business days.

7. When and where do I pay my SEVIS fee?

The SEVIS Fee can be paid to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) online, by
mail with a check or money order, or by Western Union. You will pay the SEVIS fee
after you receive admission and before you apply for a student visa.

**F-1 Visas:**

School Code for Wichita State University: KAN214F00668000

title: International Students FAQ
text:
SEVIS Identification Number: Located above the bar code on the right side of your
I-20 starting with "N"

**J-1 Visas:**

Program Code: P-1-01549

SEVIS Identification Number: Located on your DS-2019

To pay your SEVIS Fee, please go to the following website for complete details: https://www.ice.gov/sevis/i901/index.htm .

More information about the SEVIS fee

8. Where can I find information about what to do before I arrive?

Pre-Departure information will be sent to you after you receive your I-20. This information
includes when to arrive, how to apply for a visa, opening a bank account, how to pay
tuition after arrival, and much more. Or office also prepares a suggested packing
list.

Learn More

9. Can Wichita State University help me get a visa?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
Wichita State University is not permitted to influence any student’s visa application
process. We cannot contact the U.S. embassy on your behalf and encourage them to grant
you a student visa.

We do provide students with a page dedicated to tips for visa interviews . We encourage all students to review this information before a via interview.

10. When can I enroll in classes?

You can enroll in classes after you complete the following steps.

1. Arrive in Wichita
2. Complete the check-in process with the Office of International Education
3. Meet with your academic advisor

***IMPORTANT:*** Arriving during our recommended arrival dates will give you plenty of time to complete
all the processes necessary before you can enroll in classes. If you arrive after
these dates, you will risk delaying your class enrollment for your intended semester.

title: International Students FAQ
text:
11. How can I defer my admission and get a new I-20?

Students who wish to defer their admission to a later term must complete the readmission
process by following the instructions at www.wichita.edu/readmission . Our office must receive your readmission application and any required updated documents
before issuing a new I-20.

12. Can I arrive late?

U.S. Customs and Border Protection expects students to arrive no later than the program
start date listed on their I-20. Wichita State’s recommended dates of arrival each
semester follow this expectation. Arrival after your program start date requires written
approval from Wichita State. Late arrivals are approved on a case by case basis.

In general, you will not be granted late arrival approval if any of the following
statements apply to your situation.

title: International Students FAQ
text:
1. You have not been granted a visa interview by the U.S. embassy.
2. The visa interview date you received is scheduled for a date after the program
start date and/or recommended arrival dates for your intended semester.
3. You receive your visa after the recommended arrival dates.
4. You are requesting to arrive after the first day of classes for your intended semester.

Late arrivals are approved sparingly in the best interest of our students. Arriving
late causes many delays that negatively impact a student’s academic performance and
overall well-being. We want all students beginning their studies at Wichita State
to start on the path to success. We suggest students in any of the situations above
request readmission to a later semester.

13. Can I bring my parents with me while I study?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
Your parents will not be able to stay with you for the duration of your studies at
Wichita State. They are welcome to accompany you to help you get settled in Wichita
when you first arrive, or even visit you during your studies. Note that your parents
will need to follow a different visa application process in order to travel with you
or visit you in the United States. Contact your local U.S. embassy for more information
on this process.

14. Can I bring my children and/or spouse with me while I study?

title: International Students FAQ
text:
Yes, it is possible to bring your children or spouse with you while you complete your

title: International Travel Tips
text:
# International Travel Tips

## International Travel Tips

title: International Travel Tips
text:
- Complete an International Travel Authorization Form  so that WSU will have your contact information in the event of an emergency.
- Keep your cell phone and computer equipment safe by following the tips from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) , a division of the Department of Homeland Security.
- Check with the embassy or consulate of the countries you will be visiting to see if you will be required to have a visa.
- Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) , which is a free service that allows U.S. citizens to stay safe and keep informed
by registering with the closest U.S. Embassy or Consulate.
- Make sure your passport has not expired or will not expire within six months of your
expected return date to the U.S.  Many countries require passports to be valid for
at least six months beyond a traveler's planned return date.  In addition, make sure
you have plenty of blank visa pages in your passport.
- In the event that your passport gets lost or stolen, make a copy of your passport
and any relevant visa pages and store them in a safe place. Consider making scans
or taking pictures of the needed passport pages and send them to your email account
so you have them, if needed.  Never store your passport and the passport copies in
the same location.
- Notify your bank and credit card company of your travel plans. To prevent your card
from being used fraudulently, your bank or credit card company may automatically block
any usage from outside of the U.S.  Notifying your bank or credit card company in
advance ensures that your card will work when needed.
- In case your credit card or debit card is lost or stolen, it's a good idea to write
down the last four digits of each card number and the customer service telephone number
located on the back of the card. **IMPORTANT:** In general, you cannot call toll-free telephone numbers from outside of the U.S. 
As such, you should use whatever telephone number that your bank or credit card company
provides you for use outside of the U.S.  To keep your account safe, never copy or
scan your credit/debit cards.  Store your bank cards and the customer service contact
information in different locations.
- Never rely solely on the use of debit cards or credit cards during your trip. In some
countries, card use is much less common than in the U.S.  Be sure to have some cash
available – especially if your cards are lost or stolen.
- Print a copy of your itinerary and hotel reservations. At some international airports,
you may be required to show your itinerary in order to enter the airport check-in
area.
- Consider purchasing a travel adapter to use with any electronics that you carry with you. Consider taking a power bank
with you since power outlets are not always readily available for travelers.
- Check out exchange rates before you go by visiting websites such as Oanda.com .
- Check to see if you have received all recommended vaccinations for the countries you will be visiting. Some countries require evidence of vaccinations. 
Check with the embassies of the countries you're visiting to find out their vaccination
requirements.
- Pack any prescription medications in your carry-on bags. Make sure that medications
are stored in their original prescription bottles and that you carry a copy of the
prescription with you in case you're questioned by a customs agent at your port of
entry.  Please note that some medications prescribed in the U.S. may not be legal
in other countries.  Visit the International Narcotics Control Board for more information.
- Check with your health insurance provider to see if they will provide coverage outside
of the U.S. If not, consider purchasing a travel insurance policy.
- To determine if the water in the country you're visiting is considered safe for drinking,
visit the website for the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . If the water is not potable, don't use it to brush your teeth or wash fruits and
vegetables.  Place a hand towel over the faucet to help remind you not to use the
tap water.
- Learn more about Sexually Transmitted Infection (STI) . Students can also visit Student Health Services to obtain more information before departure.
- Avoid the use of narcotics. Drug offenses are punishable by death in at least 35 countries
worldwide.
- Educate yourself about the countries you will be visiting . Familiarize yourself with local laws and customs including dress standards, photography
restrictions, liquor laws, and more.
- Learn how to recognize culture shock and strategies to cope with it.

title: International Travel Guidelines
text:
# International Travel Guidelines

## International Travel Guidelines

To ensure compliance with federal and state export control regulations and adherence
to enhanced cybersecurity measures at Wichita State, an International Travel Authorization
Form must be completed by all international travelers on official university business.

An International Travel Authorization Form must be completed:
1)  By all international travelers **at least 30 days prior to their scheduled departure date**.

2)  For any international travel **(****business OR pleasure)**which meets one or more of the following conditions:

title: International Travel Guidelines
text:
- Travel being paid with WSU funds (GU, RU, Grant, Foundation, etc).
- Travel in which any WSU-owned hardware, software, electronic equipment, cell phones,
materials, or data will be used.
- Travel in which you plan to connect to any WSU-owned or operated folders, files, servers,
or networks.
- Travel that is sponsored in any way by a foreign government, foreign academic institution,
or foreign entity.
- Travel in which you will be collaborating or receiving compensation from a foreign
government, foreign academic institution, or foreign entity.
- Travel in which you will be receiving fringe benefits (honoraria, gifts, meals, etc)
from any entity -- foreign or domestic.
- Travel for Study Abroad including faculty-led trips involving students.

title: International Travel Guidelines
text:
**Travelers should NOT book tickets or make any travel arrangements** until their travel request has been reviewed and approved.  International travel
requests are **normally reviewed in 3 to 4 business days** but may take longer in some cases.  **NOTE:** Travel to Crimea-Region of Ukraine, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Sudan, or Syria may
require special approval.  An export license, if required, may take several months
to obtain.  For this reason, plan accordingly.

The International Travel Authorization Form is optional, but highly recommended, for
all other international travel by faculty, staff, or students that does not meet any
of the above requirements.  By completing the form, WSU will have your contact information
in the event of an emergency.

---

title: FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020
text:
# FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020

## FAQs for International Students Enrolling for Fall 2020

**IMPORTANT:** **Return often for updates**
Last Updated:  July 27, 2020

Is it safe to study at Wichita State because of COVID-19?

title: FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020
text:
- The Wichita metro area has not seen large numbers of COVID-19 cases like other cities
have.  Our hospitals and clinics are operating normally.
- The University is doing everything it can to keep students as safe as possible.
- Everyone is expected to wear face masks while on campus.
- Social distancing is required.  You must keep at least 2 meters away from other people.
- To allow for social distancing, there is reduced seating capacity in classrooms, eating
areas, lounges, and public areas.
- Public areas are sanitized at least once daily.
- We are here to help for our international students!  We provide assistance in-person
or by email, phone, WhatsApp, Zoom, or Facebook Messenger.

Do I need to let you know that I plan to come to Wichita for Fall 2020?

title: FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020
text:
Yes!  Please complete our Fall 2020 Questionnaire if you have not already done so.  Complete a questionnaire AS SOON AS POSSIBLE even
if you don't yet have a visa or if your plans might change later on.

How will classes be taught?

Because of COVID-19, classes for Fall 2020 will either be offered **FULLY ONLINE** or **HYBRID** depending on the class.  Please note that new students entering the U.S. for the
Fall 2020 must enroll in at least one course with an in-person component.

**Fully Online Classes:**  You may continue living where you are and take online classes for Fall 2020 without
having to come to Wichita. You will be charged an extra online fee of $97.25 per credit
hour when taking online classes.

title: FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020
text:
**Hybrid Online Classes:**  A hybrid class often has a mixture of both in-person and online instruction.  Some
hybrid classes are offered completely online but the professor may require students
to come to campus for exams.  There is no extra fee charged for hybrid classes.  Depending
on the class, the content will be delivered as:

1)  **Asynchronous** - Students can view online content and do assignments whenever it is convenient for
them.

OR

title: FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020
text:
2)  **Synchronous** - Students will meet in-person or online on specific days/times like you would for
a traditional in-person class.  For example, you might have a synchronous hybrid class
that meets online on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 09:00-10:15am Central U.S. time. 
In this example, the professor also requires students to come to campus twice during
the semester for exams.  When taking a synchronous hybrid class, students should consider
the class meeting time if they are living in a different time zone.  In addition,
the student should be aware of whether or not the professor requires students to physically
come to campus for lectures or examinations.

title: FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020
text:
**VERY IMPORTANT:**  Visit https://wichita.edu/Fall2020 to find out if a class is offered online or hybrid and whether the class is asynchronous
or synchronous.  As a new student, it is very important to look up each class to ensure
that you are taking at least one course with an in-person component.

What health-related matters  should I take care of before coming to the U.S.?  Can
I receive medical care on campus after I arrive in Wichita?

Student Health Sevices at Wichita State University provides a variety of medical services including routine medical examinations, laboratory services, vaccinations, prescription
medications, and much more.

Watch the video produced by Student Health Services to learn what new students need to know before coming to Wichita.  The video also
provides information about the tuberculosis (TB) testing requirement , medical insurance , and more.

title: FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020
text:
Learn more about mental health services available on campus.

Do I have to be quarantined when I arrive?

Maybe.  Because all countries currently have a CDC Level 3 Travel Notice, the State
of Kansas requires travelers from **ALL COUNTRIES** to be quarantined for 14 days starting with the day after their arrival in Kansas. 
In addition, Kansas requires travelers from **CERTAIN U.S. STATES** to be quarantined as well. Because the list of U.S. states requiring quarantine in
Kansas is updated often, we won't know if you might be subject to quarantine until
closer to the time that you arrive on campus.  For details, visit  https://www.coronavirus.kdheks.gov/175/Travel-Exposure-Related-Isolation-Quaran .

Where will I quarantine?  What will quarantine be like?

title: FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020
text:
- You should begin to quarantine yourself as soon as you arrive in Kansas.
- Your quarantine will last for 14 days. Day 1 of your quarantine begins the morning
after your arrival in Kansas. If you do not develop COVID-19 symptoms by the end of
your 14th day, you may leave quarantine without seeking permission from a health care provider
or public health official.
- Monitor your symptoms and read the Quarantine FAQs provided by the Kansas Department of Health and Environment for travel-related quarantine.
- As long as you wear a mask and remain at least two meters (6 feet) away from other
people, you may temporarily leave quarantine for these reasons only:
○  To seek medical attention or to obtain medication
○  To do laundry
○  To get food from a restaurant in your hotel to take back to your room to eat
- If you need medical assistance during your quarantine, please contact  Student Health Services . If you have already set up your password in the myWSU portal, you may ask questions
or schedule an appointment using the  myShockerHealth portal .  Otherwise, call (316) 978-4792.  If you contact Student Health Services, please
let them know that you are currently in travel-related quarantine. If you develop
COVID-19 symptoms during quarantine, contact Student Health Services **BEFORE** coming to campus for medical assistance.
- If you need non-medical assistance during quarantine, please contact Tonya Baldwin,
Assistant Director in the Office of International Education. **Email:**  tonya.baldwin@wichita.edu |  **Telephone:**  (316) 978-6037
- To learn more about how to reserve a room and get food during your quarantine, visit the FAQs provided by the Office of Housing and Residence Life . Please note the following:

title: FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020
text:
○  Quarantine spaces in the residence halls on campus are very limited. Rooms are only
available to students who have already signed a housing contract to live on campus.
In order to get a room, students must arrive on July 25.  Since this may not be possible
for most international students, you will likely need to stay in a hotel during quarantine.

○  The University has obtained discount pricing for students at nearby hotels for their
quarantine. Complete details about the hotels, the cost, food options, and more can
be found on the above webpage.  You should reserve a hotel room BEFORE coming back
to Wichita so that you can go directly from the airport to your hotel room to begin
your quarantine. When making a hotel reservation, let the hotel know that you are
a Wichita State University student in order to get the special discount rate.

title: FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020
text:
○  You are allowed to quarantine in the home of a friend or family member as long as
you adhere to the requirements provided by the Kansas Department of Health and Environment .

text:
What should I do if I have not yet met your TOEFL or IELTS requirement?

If you have not met our English requirement by taking the TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, or some other method, we recommend you sit
for the Duolingo English Test as soon as possible.

Are there any countries with travel restrictions when coming to the U.S.?

Yes.  Due to COVID-19, travelers from certain countries are temporarily barred from
entry to the U.S.  See https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/2019-ncov/travelers/from-other-countries.html .  **Update from 7/17/2020:**  While the travel ban is still in effect for most people, students on F-1 visas may

# Important Announcements

## Important Announcement

## for Current International Students

**Release Date:  July 7, 2020**

The Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) has released guidance for the Fall
2020 term.  This guidance is different than previous guidance for Spring and Summer
2020.

title: Important Announcements
text:
- For universities that will only be offering online classes for fall (such as many
colleges and universities on the coasts), students will be required to leave the U.S.
or transfer to another university which does not provide fully online instruction.
- Students at universities with a hybrid model, such as WSU, will be permitted to remain
in the U.S. as long as our office certifies that each student is not enrolled entirely
online and the student is taking the minimum number of online classes required to
make progress toward their degree.  To do this, we must reissue new I-20s to all of
our international students and notate this information in the remarks area of the
I-20.
- Students at universities offering hybrid classes (such as WSU) will not be allowed
to maintain an active SEVIS record if they will remain outside of the U.S. for the
Fall 2020 term.  Instead, we must terminate the SEVIS record for Authorized Early
Withdrawal. Students can still continue to enroll in as many online classes as they
want at WSU – they will simply need a new I-20 when they return to the U.S. in a future
term. Please note that in order to issue a new I-20, a new financial statement may
be required. You may also have to pay the I-901 SEVIS fee again (currently $350) and
your practical training eligibility may reset (meaning you will have to study for
one full academic year before you can do CPT or OPT).

title: Important Announcements
text:
We are still developing a system by which students will need to report to OIE their
future plans. In the meantime, it is important that students who will remain in the
U.S. for the Fall 2020 or, if currently abroad, return to the U.S. for Fall 2020,
enroll in a full course of study that is not all online or hybrid without a physical
presence component. Students who have no physical presence requirement for any of
their Fall 2020 courses will be required to leave the U.S.

We understand that students have many questions regarding their Fall plans and we
are working diligently to develop an FAQ section that should be published on our website
in the next few days. We appreciate your patience.

title: Five Things To Know About Financial Aid
text:
# Five Things To Know About Financial Aid

As you or your student(s) are preparing for the next step in your educational journey,
there are a million things to remember, plan out, think about and pay for. Finances
can be such a stressor for students and families, and unfortunately it can really
impact your future plans if the right things don’t fall into place at the right time.
However, we want you to know that we’re here to help you through it all! Here are
five things you need to know to increase your odds of financial success as you begin
this next chapter of your life:

title: Five Things To Know About Financial Aid
text:
1. **Deadlines are coming!** Don’t let this alarm you, there is still plenty of time to make these deadlines:
- **Accept your scholarships by May 1!** Don’t let your merit and other Wichita State scholarships expire. You can do this
any time in your myWSU student portal . This doesn’t commit you to Wichita State but does allow you to claim YOUR money!
- **Submit your final high school transcripts by June 1!** Your final high school transcript must be submitted to Wichita State by June 1 in
order to receive federal aid.
- **Bonus Tip:** Read the details page - page 2 = of your scholarship award notification. There is
important information here you don’t want to miss.
2. **Never quit applying for scholarships!** We have a really cool tool called ScholarshipUniverse in which you can be matched to and apply for scholarships as a new or current student!
Outside scholarships are open year-round, so always keep looking for more!
3. **Be informed on different types of student loans!** There are many loan types out there. Be informed to save yourself time and money down
the road. These websites will help you understand different types of loans and various
definitions of financial aid terms you’ll hear often throughout this process:
- Office of Financial Aid website for various loan types for all students .
- Office of Financial Aid website for Financial Aid Terms and Conditions that outlines various terms and definitions.
4. **Get familiar with your Student Aid portal!** The myWSU portal has so many functions and buttons it can be somewhat overwhelming,
but your Financial Aid Dashboard is very user-friendly! Within the dashboard you can
view the status of your financial aid for each academic year, accept awards, and more.
Your dashboard guide can tell you a lot, but videos make it much easier to understand:
- Accessing your Financial Aid Dashboard
- View holds and requirements.
- How to accept and finalize your award/aid offer .
5. **PLAN, PLAN, PLAN!** The No. 1 mistake students and families make before and during their financial aid
process is not planning for college costs or preparing a budget. Save as much money
as possible for books, supplies and emergencies. Also, don’t forget to apply for as
many scholarships as possible! It will pay off, literally.

title: Five Things To Know About Financial Aid
text:
## Honorable Mention FAQ

*What if my family’s financial situation has changed since we completed the FAFSA*?

Changes in finances due to a reduction in income, a change in marital status, death
of a parent/spouse, or other special circumstances may greatly impact a family’s ability
to pay for college. The Department of Education allows financial aid administrators
to use Professional Judgment on a case-by-case basis to make adjustments to the data
used in calculating the estimated family contribution (EFC) to reflect these special
circumstances.

If your family is experiencing financial issues (such as the loss of a job, reduction
of income, or other extenuating circumstance) and would like to discuss financial
aid options and information about the process of a Professional Judgment for the next
academic year, schedule an appointment to meet with a financial aid advisor .

The basis on which credits are awarded for the bachelor’s degree must be consistent

More details on general Graduate Admissions requirements can be found in the **graduate catalog** .

*Not an international applicant? **Find the domestic application steps here** .*

title: International Graduate Application Checklist

Tuition at Wichita State University is assessed per credit hour.  There are also fees
associated with enrollment. These fees may include student service fees and college/program
fees.  Because tuition and fees vary based on a student's enrollment and degree program,
we cannot provide a specific estimate.  Please review the following resource to better
understand your expected cost.

- Basic Cost of Attendance - Including the funding required to receive an I-20

title: International Graduate Application Checklist
text:
If you receive a graduate assistantship position or the global select tuition discount,
these will impact only the tuition portion of your total cost.  Fees are not included
in tuition discounts and awards. The Global Select tuition discount does not reduce
the amount that must be shown on the financial documents to receive an I-20.

Additional application requirements

### Additional Requirements and English Proficiency

The materials listed below are **not** required to submit the application and receive an admission recommendation.

They are **required** to receive final admit decision and an I-20.

- copy of passport (if available)
- **financial certification**
- **financial support documents**
- **proof of English proficiency**

### Complete your Online Application \*

The online application process includes five steps:

title: International Graduate Application Checklist
text:
1. **Create an account** using your **personal email address**.
**Do Not** use an address provided by an agent or third party partner. The university will communicate
with you at this email address until your arrival on campus. You should retain access
to this email for at least 3 years.
2. Begin the online application form. Complete all fields. The final page will notify
you if any incomplete fields are needed.
3. Provide payment details for the application fee.
4. Submit the application.
5. **Upload transcripts, supporting materials and supplemental items as required** .

#### \* Agents

Agents **should not** submit applications on behalf of students, as the account that is created will then
serve as the student activity portal. Instead, please direct your students to create
their own account, and submit the application and supporting materials themselves.

title: International Graduate Application Checklist
text:
### Check your application status

Initial review and admission recommendations are completed by the program to which
you applied. The application process is described below:

title: International Graduate Application Checklist
text:
- Apply to a graduate program online, submit all required materials, and pay the application
fee.
- You may access the application and check your status through the **application portal** .
- Check your email. We may contact you with questions about your application. If we
request anything additional, you will be able to upload it directly to your student
activity page within the application portal.
- The graduate program to which you applied reviews the application and forwards a recommendation
for admission or denial to the Graduate School.
- Graduate Admissions reviews the application materials and the departmental recommendation
and sends the official decision notification to the applicant through the application
portal.

### If offered admission

title: International Graduate Application Checklist
text:
Students offered admission based on uploaded documents will need to submit official
materials to finalize admission, as indicated below. All required official documents
should be submitted by the start of the fourth week of classes for the fall and spring
semesters, and the second week for the summer semester:

- Have **official transcripts** sent to Graduate Admissions. Transcripts and degree certificates from non-US schools
may be provided when you come to the university.
- Have **official test scores** sent directly to our office. At this time, Duolingo English Test, TOEFL, and IELTS
score reports do not need to be sent. Graduate Admissions can verify the unofficial
copies uploaded into the application.

Levels of Admission

### Admission Levels

Read more about admission levels

#### Full Standing

title: International Graduate Application Checklist
text:
Students who have fulfilled all of the admission requirements for a given program,
including admission grade point average, entrance exams if required, reference and
credentials if required, and have no prerequisites, may be granted admission on a
full-standing basis. Students admitted to full standing are eligible for consideration
for assistantships and federally-funded financial aid.

#### Conditional Standing

title: International Graduate Application Checklist
text:
Students who have background deficiencies or requirements assigned by the program
or Graduate School at the point of admission may be granted admission on a Conditional
basis. All conditions will be stated in the acceptance letter. Students must complete
all conditions within one year of matriculation unless otherwise specified in the
acceptance letter. Students may be admitted with both conditions and on probation,
as these two levels of admission are not exclusive. Students admitted with conditions
may be eligible for federally funded financial aid, and may be considered for graduate
assistantship positions for which they are qualified.

title: International Graduate Application Checklist
text:
Transfer to an appropriate nondegree category may result if the conditions are not
satisfactorily met within the specified time limit. Reentry into the degree program
will require reapplication, and readmission is not guaranteed. Students would be required
to meet all requirements in place at the time that they reapply for reentry.

#### Probationary Standing

title: International Graduate Application Checklist
text:
Students who do not meet the minimum academic requirements for full-standing degree
program admission may be admitted on probation when reasonable evidence exists to
indicate their ability to do satisfactory degree program work. In order to clear the
probationary status, students must complete their first 9 credit hours of graded graduate-level
coursework at Wichita State University with a minimum 3.000 grade point average. Only
courses numbered 500 and above which are letter graded (*A, B, C, D, F*) can be used toward the 9-credit-hour requirement. *S/U, Bg/NBg* and *Cr/NCr* courses will not count toward the 9-credit-hour requirement.

Students who have a graduate history at WSU must also raise their graduate grade point
average to a 3.000 or better to be removed from probation.

title: International Graduate Application Checklist
text:
Students admitted on probation or placed on academic probation following admission
may be eligible for federally-funded financial aid, and may be considered for assistantship
positions in some cases.

#### Tentative Standing

This status can be used in conjunction with any of the above statuses and means that
the student's admission was processed before the award of their degree. In order to
clear this status, the student must submit official and attested final transcript
or marksheets. If the transcript does not specifically state the title and date of
the degree award, the student must also provide degree certification. The missing
items must be on file no later than the end of the student's first semester of enrollment.
Failure to provide this evidence will result in removal from the Graduate School.

title: International Graduate Application Checklist
text:
If you have any questions or concerns at any time, please do not hesitate to contact
our office at 316-978-3095, or by email at **graduate.admissions@wichita.edu** .

The Graduate Admissions Application Checklist presents and clarifies information found
in the Graduate Catalog and is not intended to contravene or supplant any Graduate
Admissions policies. Please refer to the Graduate Catalog for all Graduate Admissions
policies, including those found on, or linked to from, this page.

## Important Information for You

Fee Waivers

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
The Graduate School does **not** provide application fee waivers. All applicants are required to pay the fee in order
to have their application processed and reviewed.

U.S. Bachelor Equivalency

When reviewing academic records from institutions outside the U.S., the university
will determine whether an applicant's education is equivalent to a U.S. bachelor's
degree. View a list of diplomas and certificates from various countries that may be considered
equivalent .

Application Status

You can check the status of your application in your application portal . We cannot give you an estimated time of when a final decision will be made, however
when there is an update to your status, your portal will reflect that.

Application Materials

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
Admission requirements are listed on the website for each graduate program. We ask that applicants not submit
materials that are not required as it can hold up the application / review process.

Programs Not Eligible Under F1 Visa

Some programs are unable to meet the enrollment requirements necessary for F1 Visa
eligibility. International students who wish to study on an F1 Visa at Wichita State
University should apply to one of our other programs . To see if a program is eligible, refer to the list below:

- Arts Leadership & Management\*
- Health Administration\*
- Human Resource Management\*
- Nursing
- School Psychology
- Special Education\*
- Sport Management
- Teaching

\*These programs may be completed online.

Decisions

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
Depending on the program you apply for and the volume of applicants, decisions can
take a few days to a few months. It's important to check your application portal for
missing materials. When a decision is made on your application, you will receive an
email to check your portal for the decision**.**

Changing Majors / Switching Programs

At the graduate level, you cannot simply notify us that you want to change your major.
In order to get into a new program, you have to apply, submit the app fee, and be
re-evaluated based on that program's admission requirements. Please be aware that
the app fee amount is based on date and cannot be changed. Certain programs have deadlines for application submission.

Conditions / Pre-requisites

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
If you have certain conditions or pre-requisite courses listed in our admission letter,
the expectation is that you clear those within your first semester to first year as
a graduate student. These were assigned to you based on the review the program did
of your transcripts / marksheets. They are to help prepare you for the rigor of the
graduate program and make sure you are successful in higher level coursework.

If you think you should not have been assigned certain pre-requisite courses, please
reach out to your academic advisor listed in your admission letter.

English Proficiency

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
It is mandatory for international applicants to provide an acceptable TOEFL, IELTS,
PTE, or Duolingo score report for admission. We understand that many countries have
English as an official language along with other languages that are native to that
country. Many, if not most, of our foreign students are educated (at least at the
college level) in English. However, we find that the experience of being educated
in English vs. living in a country where the native language is English, to be very
different.

To ensure the success of our graduate students, we require demonstration of high level of proficiency in English.

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
The only time the TOEFL/IELTS/PTE/Duolingo requirement is waived is when the applicant
has graduated from a university located in the US/UK/Canadian/New Zealand, or Australia
within the last 2 years. Testing English proficiency is not only to our benefit, but
yours as well. It will help you measure your preparedness for reading, writing, and
comprehending English at a level sufficient for a higher education setting. We want
all of our students to be successful, and excellent English language skills are a
key to that success.

Graduate Assistantships

Financial assistance for graduate students usually comes in the form of an assistantship with the department. Assistantships provide a wage and, if you work enough hours,
may entitle you to a lower in-state tuition rate.

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
Each department does its own hiring. You should contact the graduate coordinator of the department regarding assistantship opportunities, however Shocker Central is a great place to start looking. You can search and apply for on-campus employment
via the Shocker Central website.

Keep in mind that most departments will not consider a student for an assistantship
until they have completed at least one semester of study at WSU. Assistantships are
very competitive, so there is no guarantee you will be given an assistantship.

## Graduate Coordinators

You'll contact your graduate coordinator whenever you have questions about courses
or your degree program. There are a variety of reasons to contact your coordinator,
including:

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:

you start

## Visa Fee and Application Tips

Helpful tips for obtaining your visa.

Visa tips

### SEVIS Fee Information

What is the SEVIS fee? The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) requires
people who want F-1 or J-1 visas to pay a one-time SEVIS Fee before applying for a
visa.

Learn more

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
The SEVIS Fee for F-1 visas is $350. The SEVIS fee for J-1 visas is $220. This is
in addition to the normal visa application fee of US$185 and the visa integrity fee
of $250. The SEVIS fee helps to pay for SEVIS (Student and Exchange Information System)
that U.S. schools use to issue I-20 forms.

How do I pay the SEVIS Fee?

The SEVIS Fee can be paid to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) online, by
mail with a check or money order, or by Western Union. To pay your SEVIS Fee, you
must have:

- **F-1 Visas:**School Code for Wichita State University: KAN214F00668000
SEVIS Identification Number: Located above the bar code on the right side of your
I-20 starting with "N"
- **J-1 Visas:**Program Code: P-1-01549
SEVIS Identification Number: Located on your DS-2019

To pay your SEVIS Fee, please go to the following website for complete details: https://www.fmjfee.com/i901fee/index.html

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
When must I pay the SEVIS Fee?

The fee should be paid at least three business days before you apply for your visa,
change of status, or reinstatement application.

## Pre-Departure Information

Pay tuition and fees

### Pay Tuition and Fees

Students are not required to pay their tuition and fees before coming to Wichita.
Tuition, fees, and housing payments are charged on a semester-by-semester basis. Deadline
for payment is usually two weeks after school starts. There are several options to
make payment to the university:

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
- **Direct Deposit from U.S. Bank Account:** After you open a bank account in the U.S., you can setup direct deposit from your
U.S. bank account to your student account at WSU.
- **Electronic Bank Transfer:** Wichita State University uses a payment platform called Flywire to process international
payments via wire transfers. Learn more about Flywire .
- **Check, Bank Draft, Money Order, or Traveler's Checks:** If you bring a check or bank draft with you to Wichita, it is very important that
the check be made payable to "Wichita State University" (and not to you). Your check
should include the address of the bank in the U.S. for collections. If the check is
made payable to you, you may not be able to use the money for 1-2 weeks after the
check is deposited to your bank in the U.S. If your check is for an amount that exceeds
what you owe, any extra amount will be applied to your next semester's tuition and
will not be refunded to you.
- **NOTE:** For any student who does not have an existing bank account or has been restricted
to pay by personal check, for your convenience you can take your cash and get a cashier's
check at the Campus Credit Union (located at 21st & Oliver). Let them know that the
cashier's check is for payment of your tuition, fees, or housing so that you will
not be charged a fee.
- **Credit Card:** If you use a credit card to pay for your tuition, fees, medical insurance, or housing,
a nonrefundable 2.85% service fee will be added.
- **Debit Card - VISA, MasterCard:** Payment is made online only by going to the Student Account Suite . To avoid the 2.85% fee (min $3) associated with credit card payments, we encourage
you to pay using electronic check process by entering the bank routing and account
number attached to the debit card. Debit card payments cannot be made to a cashier
in the Accounts Receivable office.
- **Installment Payment Plan:** This allows you to pay for your tuition and fees in smaller installments each semester.
With this plan, you can make a nonrefundable payment of US$130 (which includes a US$30
administrative fee) before the payment deadline in each semester. After the initial
payment of US$130, the balance will be split into three equal installments due on
the 15th of each month. You can arrange the Payment Plan by logging into your WSU
student account.
- **International Payments Through Flywire:** WSU accepts international payments through Flywire . This allows payers to make payments in local currency or in US dollars by credit
card, bank transfer (wire transfer), and other payment options from over 100 countries.

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
Know the cost of your education

### Know the cost of your education

The cost listed on your I-20 is an estimate. Actual cost of tuition and fees will
depend on your major and the number of classes you take. The amount you owe will be
posted in your WSU student account.

Buy an airline ticket

### Buy an airline ticket

The Wichita airport is called Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport (airport code
ICT). If you are coming from a country outside of the U.S., you will have at least
one connecting flight before arriving in Wichita. We suggest you allow for at least
a 3-hour layover in your first arrival city in the U.S. so that you have sufficient
time for immigration processing, customs inspection, and a required security check
before your connecting flight leaves for Wichita.

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
Please refer to dates in the pre-departure information when you book your air tickets. You must arrive to the United States by the start
date on the I-20 or you risk being barred entry. The Graduate School does not permit
late arrival entry after that date.

**\* Note: If starting classes in January, the University is typically closed between
December 24 through January 2. You should not plan to arrive on these dates.**

Our free airport pickup service is available from Wichita D. Eisenhower National Airport
(ICT). Fall 2025 free airport pick up is available from **August 4 to 13, 2025.** Please note: you will need to submit your pick up request at least 48 hours before
arrival.

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
If you arrive before the listed dates, there are many options of ground transportation
at the Wichita Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport. You may choose to take a taxi
or Uber/Lyft to the University, taxi fare is approximately US$30. For details of airport
amenities and ground transportation options, please visit www.flywichita.com .

Off-campus housing

### Off-campus housing

Most graduate students choose to stay in off-campus housing because of the significant
cost savings that comes with sharing a rented home.

The university is happy to provide a centralized place to start your search for an
off-campus apartment or house. Please visit https://offcampushousing.wichita.edu/listing .

Many communities are located within a radius of 1 mile around the campus:

title: International Graduate Admissions
text:
- 3 Community apartments on N Oliver Avenue.
- 1 Community apartment on the 21st Street
- 2 Community apartments on 17th Street beside the Garvey International Center.

Wichita State University partners with Wichita Transit to offer fast, free transportation for the Wichita State community. Communities further
out may require other modes of transportation.

text:

of 10 hours of an appropriate foreign language is required. Students who already have
language skills beyond the elementary level should consult with an advisor.
