title: Procedure for Executive Council Approval of Policies
text:
# Procedure for Executive Council Approval of Policies

## Procedure for Executive Council Approval of Policies College of Health Professions (CHP)

Approved by the College of Health Professions Executive Council on January 9, 2018

**Background**

title: Procedure for Executive Council Approval of Policies
text:
From time to time there is a need to develop new CHP policies/procedures that do not
require a college vote.  Actions requiring a college vote are explained in the CHP
Governance Code of Organization and Procedure (Bylaws). The distinction is determined
by shared governance (Bylaws) vs. administrative functions (Executive Council). Part
of the responsibility of the Executive Council is to “Provide governance code of organization
and procedure oversight” as specified in section 8.1.1 of the CHP Governance Code
of Organization and Procedure. The Executive Council will also provide oversight on
determining which proposed policies/procedures require their approval, or approval
by college vote.

**Executive Council Review and Approval**

title: Procedure for Executive Council Approval of Policies
text:
For new CHP policies/procedures that do not require a college vote, the CHP Executive
Council will serve as the body to review and approve.  Approved documents will include
a sub-heading stating “Approved by the College of Health Professions Executive Council
on (date).” New, proposed CHP policies/procedures are submitted to the Executive Council,
through the CHP Dean’s Office, in accordance with the Dean’s Office Flow Chart for
Policy Development (attached).

**Distribution**

Once a new policy or procedure is approved by the Executive Council, the document
will be posted on the CHP web site with other CHP policies. 

**College of Health Professions Dean's Office Flow Chart**

**Policy Development**

title: Procedure for Executive Council Approval of Policies
text:
- Need identified by Administrators, who communicate to Dean
- Need identified by Faculty/Staff, who communicate to Dean
- Need identified by Students/Others, who communicate to Dean
- Dean/Executive Staff/Executive Council discuss need for new or revised policy
- If Dean and Executive Staff and/or Executive Council deem that revised policy is not
needed, issue is closed, no further action is required
- If policy is needed, Dean assigns personnel/task force to study and/or draft policy
- Executive Council reviews draft policy and makes recommendation to Dean
- Dean approves policy and communicates it to CHP faculty/staff/students, others
- Policy is published on CHP website and on CHP shared network drive

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
# WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies

## University Resources & Policies

---

### Important Academic Dates

See the **University Registrar's Academic Calendar** for the last date to drop a class and received a W (withdrawn) instead of an F, as
well as other important deadlines.

### Inclement Weather Event and Emergency Event (5.17)

In the event of an Inclement Weather Event and/or an Emergency Event, the University
shall take all reasonable measures to protect the health and safety of students, faculty,
and staff.  Should such an event occur, the University may implement a temporary adjustment
to its class and/or operations, including late start and moving class instruction
and Non-Critical Campus Operations to remote delivery, when possible. *Keeping Our Community Safe During Severe Weather* *.*

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
In the event of an inclement weather event and/or emergency event, instructors are
required to either: (1) provide their plan for course delivery (for example, remote,
alternate assignments, or other pre-arranged alternatives to in-person instruction;
or (2) describe, in detail, their intended method for communicating their plan for
course delivery with students (Blackboard, email, other).

### Academic Integrity

Students at Wichita State University are expected to uphold high academic standards.
WSU will not tolerate a lack of academic integrity. Students are responsible for knowing
and following the Student Academic Integrity Policy 2.17 .

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
When the faculty member determines sanctions are warranted for violations of academic
integrity, regardless of severity, the faculty member must report the infraction to
the Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards. If you need more information
about the process or wish to appeal a decision, please visit https://www.wichita.edu/about/student\_conduct/ai.php

### Unauthorized Use of Generative AI

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
Please note in particular that *Unauthorized Use or Possession of Materials or Resources* (Policy 2.17, item IV.B.2) includes unauthorized use of generative AI like ChatGPT
or GPT4. In this course, all use of generative AI is prohibited except as may be specified
in assignment instructions. Any student suspected of unauthorized use of generative
AI may be asked to demonstrate their mastery of the assignment learning outcomes in
an alternate format, such as a verbal interview or an additional problem set, before
a determination is made as to whether an academic integrity violation report is warranted.

### Personal Identity Updates

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
Wichita State University provides an avenue for students to update their personal
identity.  For more information, please visit: www.wichita.edu/name .  To update your personal identity information, please go to myWSU Home tab, Student
Tools channel, and click on “View and Update Personal Information” link.

### Concealed Carry Policy

The Kansas Legislature has legalized concealed carry on public university campuses.
Guns must be out of view, concealed either on the body of the carrier, or backpack,
purse or bag that remains under the immediate control of the carrier.

Gun owners must familiarize themselves with WSU policy 11.19 / Weapons on University Property and the Kansas Board of Regent’s weapons policy . If you believe that there has been a violation of these policies, please contact
the University Police Department at (316) 978-3450.

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
*The language below is applicable to lab courses or other courses where student belongings
are unattended and out of immediate control.*

**Concealed Carry for lab courses or other courses where student belongings are unattended
and out of immediate control:** Under the Concealed Carry Policy, a backpack or other bag used to carry a handgun
must be within the immediate control of the individual. This course requires students
to leave belongings such as backpacks or other bags out of reach and unattended for
the duration of class time. Students who choose to carry a concealed handgun in a
backpack or other bag must plan each day accordingly and are responsible for making
alternate arrangements as necessary. Wichita State does not provide publicly available
secure storage for concealed handguns.

---

### Video & Audio Recording

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
Video and audio recording of lectures and review sessions without the consent of the
instructor is prohibited. Unless explicit permission is obtained from the instructor,
recordings of lectures may not be modified and must not be transferred or transmitted
to any other person, whether or not that individual is enrolled in the course.

### Shocker Alert System

Get the emergency information you need instantly and effortlessly! With the Shocker
Alert System, we will contact you by email the moment there is an emergency or weather
alert that affects the campus. Sign up at the ShockerAlert System page.

### Intellectual Property

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
Wichita State University students are subject to Board of Regents and University policies
(see 9.10 / Intellectual Property Policy and Institutional Procedures ) regarding intellectual property rights. Any questions regarding these rights and
any disputes that arise under these policies will be resolved by the President of
the University, or the President’s designee, and such decision will constitute the
final decision.

---

### CARE Team

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
Wichita State University is committed to the safety and success of and cares about
all members of the University community. If you or someone you know needs support,
is distressed, or exhibits concerning behavior that is interfering with their own
or others’ academic or personal success or the safety of members of our community,
resources and assistance are available. As your Faculty, I may seek support for you.
If you or another member of our campus community is in need of help, please submit
a concern at CARE Team or call any CARE team member listed on that webpage. In case of emergency, please
call the University Police Department at (316) 978-3450 or 911.

### Counseling & Prevention Services

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
WSU Counseling & Prevention Services (CAPS) provides quality mental health services
to enrolled students by licensed providers and presents programs and trainings on
topics promoting personal growth and optimal wellbeing. Services are by appointment,
low cost and confidential. They are located in the Student Wellness Center of the
Steve Clark YMCA. Their phone number is (316) 978-4SWC (4792). CAPS is open during
regular business hours. If you have a mental health emergency while Counseling & Prevention
Service is not open, please call 911 or COMCARE Crisis Services at (316) 660-7500
for 24 hour assistance.

### The Office of the Student Advocate

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
The Student Advocate is an executive, non-partisan member of the Student Government
Association at Wichita State University, who is available to assist you with problems
that haven't been resolved by other offices on campus. The Student Advocate can assist
all students with many things including but not limited to: academic appeals, traffic
appeals, parking appeals, navigating various systems on campus, and connecting students
with various resources on campus and in the community. To meet with the Student Advocate,
please fill out a submission form on the website.

### Academic Appeals

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
The process of Academic Appeals is available for students who believe they have been
treated unfairly in grading. Any student may use the appeals procedure. All student
Academic Appeals are coordinated by the Provost and Senior Vice President. All efforts
should be made to resolve the issue with the instructor. If this issue cannot be resolved
with the instructor, the student should contact the chair of the department where
the course is listed before submitting an appeal to the Associate Vice Provost for
Student Success and Persistence in Academic Affairs. Please review the policy carefully
in order to ensure that you have taken all of the necessary steps before submitting
the appeal.

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
The student may print the form, policy, and procedures from the links below or may
pick up the paperwork in the office of Academic Affairs (109 Morrison Hall). Click
here for further information on academic appeals .

### Student Health Services

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
WSU’s Student Health Services (SHS) provides professional medical care and health
education to enrolled students by licensed health care providers. General health care
services are available ranging from routine and preventive care to managing acute
illnesses and minor injuries. SHS offers convenient onsite laboratory and medication
services including vaccinations. Staff are available to provide health education on
a variety of topics, both in and out of the classroom setting. SHS is located in the
new YMCA/Student Wellness Center. Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through
Friday, and the phone number is (316) 978-4SWC (4792). See Student Health Services for health information and access to myShockerHealth, the online patient portal where
students can schedule appointments, send a secured message to a healthcare provider,
check immunizations and more. All services are confidential.

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
### Heskett Center & Campus Recreation

Whether you are wanting to be active on campus, relieve the stress from classes or
take care of your body, Wichita State Campus Recreation is the place for you. Campus Recreation, located inside the Heskett Center, contributes
to the health, education, and development of Wichita State University students, faculty,
staff, alumni, and community members by offering quality programs and services. With
many programs and facilities which are free to all students and members, Campus Recreation
offers its members limitless opportunities.

---

### First Generation Students

A first-generation (FGEN) college student is a student whose parents did not complete
a four-year college degree. WSU strongly supports First Generation students and offers them helpful resources.

### Tobacco Free Campus

title: WSU Syllabus Resources & Policies
text:
Effective July 01, 2017, Wichita State University became a tobacco-free campus to
support the health, well-being and safety of university students, employees and visitors.
The use of tobacco products, in any form, are prohibited on all Wichita State University
properties. These products include, but are not limited to: cigarettes, cigarillos,
cigars, roll your own tobacco and other spitless products, e-cigarettes, hookah, pipes
and smokeless tobacco. Follow this link to view the tobacco free campus policy . For assistance with stopping tobacco use, follow these links to contact WSU Student Health Services or WSU Counseling and Prevention Services for more information about campus tobacco cessation services.

Jönköping, Sweden is a city that is beautifully situated around Lake Vättern. Enchanting
forests, shimmering lakes, and high mountains are ready to welcome you to explore.
Enjoy popular restaurants and thrilling adventures in the city center. There are many
shops, museums, and events to take part in. Jönköping is a safe and modern city surrounded

you need to be with ease. Jönköping is in the south of Sweden about 200 miles from
the capital city, Stockholm. It is only a few hours from other Swedish cities such
as Malmö, and conveniently located centrally between Norway and Denmark so you can
visit other countries with a quick train ride.

title: ESCE International Business School
text:
ESCE International Business School is located in the north-western suburbs of Paris,
in the Hauts-de-Seine department, it extends across the communes of Puteaux, Courbevoie,
Nanterre and La Garenne-Colombes. Hop on the Paris metro to visit world famous Parisienne
sites such as the Eiffel Tower, Arc de Triomphe and The Louvre and immerse yourself
in the romantic and historic city. Paris has an estimated population of around 2 million.
It offers cool winters that have frequent rain and overcast skies, and mild to warm
summers. Easily visit nearby countries such as Germany, Belgium, Switzerland, or Spain
by taking a train, plane or bus.

A Walk in Paris Video

Academics

**Overview**

title: ESCE International Business School
text:
ESCE is a private business school located in the heart of La D*é*fense, France’s largest business district just minutes from the center of Paris. La
D*é*fense is home to the headquarters of numerous French and foreign companies as well
as the European Banking Authority, giving students plenty of opportunities to interact
with the 500 international companies and groups based there. Exchange students have
the option of taking French Language courses at different levels during the semester
in combination with business courses taught in English. Exchange students interested
in this program should have a good GPA in their business classes and be ready to take
upper-division business classes. A variety of different business classes are offered
in areas such as management, marketing, entrepreneurship, international business,
and finance. Students must pay for at least 12 U.S. credit hours at WSU, regardless
as to the number of courses they choose to take, while on the exchange.

title: International Buddy Program
text:
# International Buddy Program

# Applications are closed.

What is the International Buddy Program?

The International Buddy Program pairs incoming international short-term students with
Wichita State students to help them integrate into life here in the U.S. and at WSU
for one semester. The program also provides international short-term students an opportunity
to have a friend and resource when they arrive and throughout their time on campus.
It gives WSU students a chance to practice language skills, learn about other cultures
and gain a friend! You and your buddy can decide how often you want to do things together
and what activities you are both interested in doing.

What are the expectations of a U.S. buddy?

We want everyone to enjoy their time as a buddy so we leave most of the decision-making
up to you and your buddy. However, we do have a few expectations:

title: International Buddy Program
text:
1. Serve as a resource and good role model to your buddy as they get acquainted with
WSU and U.S. culture for one semester.
2. Have an open mind to learning about other cultures/countries and be respectful about
any differences.
3. Meet with your buddy at least once a month throughout the entire semester aside from
the group events/activities.
4. Attend our Meet N Greet, which is held at the beginning of the semester.
5. Attend any events that are held for the entire Buddy Program that are coordinated
by our office (usually 3 or 4 events a semester—1 a month).
6. Offer assistance to your buddy by helping them navigate how to purchase textbooks,
giving a campus tour, taking them to Walmart, etc.

What activities can buddies do together?

title: International Buddy Program
text:
You and your buddy can decide together whatever activities the two of you would like
to do! (Keep in mind your buddy will not have a car.) Here are some activity ideas:

- Get a cup of coffee in the RSC
- Study together
- Attend a sporting event
- Visit a museum
- Have a picnic in the park
- Go for a bike or scooter ride
- Go on a campus/Wichita tour
- Visit the Keeper of the Plains
- Try new restaurants (or food trucks)
- Check out Tanganyika or the zoo
- Have a movie night
- Play pickle ball at Chicken N Pickle
- Attend a WSU event (comedians, Karaoke, Springfest, Shockers after dark, etc.)
- Visit Botanica
- Go Bowling
- Visit Cowtown
- Go to the farmers market in Old Town
- Take your buddy to family events (if the two of you are comfortable with it)

Is there a financial obligation to be a part of the program?

title: International Buddy Program
text:
NO! The Buddy Program is completely free. The activities that you choose to do can
be free such as studying, having a movie night, or exploring downtown. The amount
of money you spend is completely up to you. You should also be mindful of the cost
of any activities when you invite your buddy so that they will be aware and can plan
accordingly.

How can I be a part of the program?

Applications for the International Buddy Program are now closed. Contact studyabroad@wichita.edu with any questions.

Where can I find more information?

Please email studyabroad@wichita.edu if you need further information or have questions.

regarding the process to apply and study online.

university activities are exempt.

U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control

Some countries (e.g., China) block or filter internet content. Use of a VPN in China

**Deadlines**

**Undergraduate** applicant deadlines differ depending on the term the student is applying for and

text:

is earlier.

Graduate Deadline

**Can students be enrolled in an online program or online classes from outside of the
U.S.?**

title: Online International Student Info
text:
In term of immigration regulations, any international student can enroll in an online
program or online classes while living **outside**of the U.S.  Aside from immigration regulations, international students need to take
notice of additional regulations they may need to follow. Any student (American or
international) living in a sanctioned country (Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, or
Ukraine-Crimea region) may have restrictions on the program or classes they can study
while in these countries. When in doubt, students should check with the Office of Research Compliance or reach out to Misha Jacob-Warren in the General Counsel's Office .  Some countries may also have laws that restrict universities from offering online
coursework or programs in their countries.

title: Online International Student Info
text:
Students on F or J visa types cannot enroll in an online program while in the U.S. 
Students on other visa types, however, do not have that restriction as long as the
student's visa type permits study.

- If the student is NOT on an F or J visa AND is eligible to study in the U.S., they
can take as many online classes they want.
- If the student is ON an F or J visa, they can enroll in ONE online class of up to
3 credit hours per semester.

---

Education Office?**

- Graduate School: All graduate applicants

title: Scholarship Policies
text:
# Scholarship Policies

## Fairmount College Scholarship Policies

When selecting recipients, considering award renewals and monitoring fund requirement
compliance, we follow these policies:

### Funds awarded by the Fairmount College of Liberal Arts and Sciences are only available for students pursuing a degree in this college:

- All recipients must be enrolled at WSU, in the Fairmount College of Liberal Arts and
Sciences, during the semester or academic year for which the award is made.

### Recipients must meet minimum fund requirements during the award term.

title: Scholarship Policies
text:
- This includes minimum credit hour enrollment, GPA, degree or major, college and any
additional requirements specified per the fund guidelines.
- Failure to meet minimum requirements will result in the withdrawal of funds, and you
will be responsible for any charges assessed by Accounts Receivable.
- Recipients who believe that extenuating circumstances may prevent them from meeting
any scholarship or fellowship requirements should contact the Fairmount College Scholarship
Coordinator immediately at las.scholarships@wichita.edu .
- WSU scholarship policy requires new students who have been awarded a scholarship to
be enrolled by July 1st. Continuing students must be enrolled by the last day to add
full semester courses each semester. (Visit www.wichita.edu/schedule to view semester calendars.)

title: Scholarship Policies
text:
### All recipients are expected to maintain satisfactory academic progress, which includes but is not limited to:

- Successful completion of courses with passing grades.
- Steady and efficient progress towards fulfilling degree requirements.
- Good academic standing.

### Renewal of awards will be decided on a case by case basis:

- Any possible award renewals will be subject to individual fund guidelines, satisfactory
academic progress, college and university policy, and the decision of the appropriate
scholarship committee.
- Within the bounds of individual fund guidelines, scholarships and fellowships are
intended to support students completing their first bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral
degree. Renewals to recipients with more than the minimum credit hours required for
their degree are not guaranteed.

### Fund requirements determine student classification eligibility:

title: Scholarship Policies
text:
- Funds designated as scholarships are for undergraduate students.
- Funds designated as fellowships are for graduate students.
- Undergraduate classifications are based on completed credit hours: freshman (0-29),
sophomore (30-59), junior (60-89), senior (90+).

### Recipients must remain in contact with the Fairmount College Dean’s Office, specifically the Scholarship Coordinator:

- It is in a recipient’s best interest to contact the Scholarship Coordinator (as well as an academic advisor) before making changes in enrollment, major or student
status. Such changes will likely affect eligibility for certain scholarships or fellowships.
- Correspondence will be conducted primarily through WSU email addresses. It is each
recipient’s responsibility to regularly check and maintain this email account.

### Showing gratitude is an essential part of receiving a scholarship or fellowship:

title: Scholarship Policies
text:
- It is important that recipients thank our donors. During the academic year, recipients
will receive an email(s) containing contact information for their donor(s).
- The WSU Foundation hosts various luncheons and dinners to connect scholarship recipients
with donors. It is expected that recipients will attend these events when invited.

### Scholarship and fellowship guidelines do not imply any contractual obligation; all awards are subject to and based on availability of funds.

title: Department Vehicle Policies
text:
# Department Vehicle Policies

## Vehicle Policies & Instructions

v. 7/2024

The Geology Department is able to obtain and maintain its own vehicle fleet solely
through the generous donations from alumni and friends of the department. We greatly
appreciate these invaluable resources to the department.

The Geology Department is **fully** responsible and accountable for use, maintenance, and damage to vehicles per Kansas
state law regarding liability and insurance. To be clear, this means that the state
of Kansas does not hold or allow the department to hold an insurance policy on the
vehicles. Therefore, the following policies apply for operation of department vehicles.

**Authorized Operators**

title: Department Vehicle Policies
text:
- Operation/driving of vehicles is limited to Geology Department employees for department
teaching, research, or service purposes.
- "Geology Department employees" encompasses any full- or part-time faculty, instructors,
staff, or GTA/GRA.
- Student GTA/GRAs **must** have a full-time faculty member present for all **out-of-state travel** using department vehicles. A travel authorization must be on file with the university.
Student GTA/GRAs may operate the vehicles in the state of Kansas without a full-time
faculty member present.
- All employees should have a travel authorization on file with the university for each
instance of travel outside the Wichita-Sedgwick Co. area.
- The department **does not** loan or rent vehicles to other units/departments on campus for use.
- If a state employee from another unit is participating in shared teaching, research,
or service activities with the Geology Department, then a Geology Department employee
must be present with vehicle during activity.

title: Department Vehicle Policies
text:
**Scheduling Vehicle Use**

- Authorized operators of department vehicles should reserve vehicles through the WSU
**"Geology Vehicle Schedule" group Outlook calendar** with your wichita.edu account.
- To request to be added to the "Geology Vehicle Schedule" group, please contact the
department HERE .

**Funding Operation of Vehicles**

title: Department Vehicle Policies
text:
- Fuel, maintenance, repair, and replacement is ultimately the responsibility of the
Geology Department. Coordinate with department chair to clarify funding before vehicle
use.
- **Teaching/Service**
- **Local-area** vehicle use (within central KS) for teaching and service purposes will generally be
funded by the department's operating funds, or by donations available for that purpose.
- **Long-distance** vehicle use (outside central KS) for teaching or department service must be coordinated
with the department chair before travel. Travel out of state will require an out-of-state
travel authorization with the university and coordination with department chair.
- **Research**
- Vehicle use for **faculty-led research** should be funded from the faculty member's awarded grants or donations. If these
are not available, then travel funding must be coordinated with the department chair
before travel.

title: Department Vehicle Policies
text: **Operation of Vehicle**

title: Department Vehicle Policies
text:
- WSU is a non-smoking campus and this extends to Geology Department vehicles. **No smoking in vehicles.**
- **No open containers of alcohol** in vehicles at any time.
- Vehicles should remain in a state of readiness. Don't bring back vehicles and assume
the next user will maintain the vehicle for you. This means vehicles have:
- **Fuel**: at least 3/4 tank of fuel ready for next trip.
- Department maintains set of fuel purchase cards. At each fillup during trip you should:
- (1) Swipe card, (2) enter odometer reading, and (3) six digit code that is printed
on front of card (sometime there are only 4 digits; add "0" to front of digits to
reach six digits).
- You must keep fuel receipt (!) and place in center console of vehicle.
- **Clean Interior**: clean up vehicle interior after trip is completed. Don't leave it trashed for the
next user to clean up.
- **Inflated Tires**: if getting low during your trip, then resolve issue.
- **Oil**: periodically check engine oil level; department changes the oil about once a year
(usually springtime).

title: Why Major in International Studies
text:
# Why Major in International Studies

## Why Major in International Studies?

In a rapidly globalizing world, the demand for college graduates who have a deeper
understanding of different regions and cultures of the world is growing. Many employers
look favorably on prospective employees with language skills and international knowledge.

title: Why Major in International Studies
text:
The International Studies Field Major at Wichita State is an interdisciplinary degree
with courses required in multiple departments. Students have the option to follow
an Area Studies Track or a Business Administration Track. Both require students to
focus on a particular region of the world, including language courses for that region.
The Core courses for each track vary, with the Area Studies focusing more on historical,
political, and cultural relations, and the Business Administration focusing on international
business courses. The International Studies degree is a BA degree in the College of
Liberal Arts and Sciences.

title: Why Major in International Studies
text:
There are many career opportunities that can be pursued with an International Studies
degree including possible employment with federal and state government executive agencies,
multinational corporations, law firms, international organizations such as the United
Nations, non-profit organizations, and public and private schools. An International
Studies degree can also prepare you for a course of study in graduate school.

title: Study Abroad
text:
# Study Abroad

## Why Study Abroad?

Practical Reasons:

- Develop a global resume
- Make yourself more marketable
- Become proficient in a language, or learn a new one.
- Decide on a major field of study
- Inspire a career
- Provide volunteer learning service in a third world country

Personal, Cultural and Romantic Reasons:

- Learn about new cultures
- Become more tolerant toward different people
- Make friends from all over the world
- Discover your heritage
- Discover the new and unexpected
- Develop confidence and independence

US News and World Report article on What Students Should Know About Studying Abroad

Chinese 104, 105  [and 104, 105 in a second language]
French 104, 105, 106, 204

Japanese 104, 105, 106, 204

\* Upper division culture classes can count toward the language requirement beyond
the 3 core courses OR as an area studies course, but not both. Literature classes
do not count toward an IS major.

\* Some languages do not offer a large number of courses. Instructors start the 3-course
cycle once every year and half. This can make it challenging to complete the language
courses unless you start them early.

title: Minor Requirements
text:
# Minor Requirements

## Minor Requirements

1. Language: four course sequence in a world language (not including ASL) (104, 105, 106, 204). 
If four courses are not available, students can complete two courses (104, 105) in
two world languages.  

2. Area Studies courses 6 hrs (2 courses)
\* See Area Studies Track for list of courses

3. Core Courses 9 hrs (3 courses)

It is possible to major in Political Science, History, and Anthropology and minor
in International Studies, but you cannot count one course towards both degrees. For
example, POLS 220 (Intro to International Relations) is required for a Political Science
degree, so you would have to take a different Core Course to count toward the 9 hours
for an IS minor.

title: Business Administration
text:
# Business Administration

## Business Administration Track

**Degree Requirements**
1. Language: four course sequence in a world language (not including ASL) (104, 105, 106, 204). 
If four courses are not available, students can complete two courses (104, 105) in two world
languages.  
2. Area Studies Courses 12 hrs (4 courses)
3. International Business Prerequisites 18 hrs (6 courses)

# International Studies

## International Studies

In a globalizing world, demand for graduates with an understanding of different regions
and cultures of the world is growing. Employers look favorably on employees with language
skills and international knowledge.

The International Studies major at Wichita State University is an interdisciplinary
degree with courses in multiple departments. Students focus on a particular region
of the world, including studying relevant languages, while pursuing one of two degree
tracks. The Area Studies Track focuses on historical, political and cultural relations,
while the Business Administration Track focuses on international business.

title: Sodance
text:
# Sodance

## Policy

Rhatigan Student Center Student Organization Dances
Scheduled On The RSC East Patio, RSC Ballroom Or Room #223

### Purpose

The Rhatigan Student Center, in an attempt to provide the necessary safeguards which
will contribute to a safe and successful event, wish to establish the following policies
and procedures.

### Programming Certification Workshop

Any student organization in good standing with Wichita State University Division of
Student Affairs is eligible to sponsor student dances.

title: Sodance
text:
The Division of Student Affairs will sponsor a Programming Certification Workshop
for student organizations. Any member of a student organization who will be responsible
for planning and hosting a dance on the East Patio, in the Ballroom or Room #223 must
attend the workshop. Upon successful completion of the Programming Certification Workshop,
those members are eligible to schedule a dance through the University Reservations
Office, and are eligible to serve as the organization's on-site representative for
events scheduled in the Rhatigan Student Center or its environs.

### Scheduling, Confirmation, Fee Payment

title: Sodance
text:
Student organizations are encouraged to reserve the East Patio, Ballroom or Room #223
in the Rhatigan Student Center for events. Each organization is allowed two scheduled
activities per month during the fall and spring semesters. No student dances will
be scheduled during the summer session.

A dance must be scheduled a minimum of two weeks prior to the event. Scheduling, confirmation,
and fee payment are handled through the University Reservations Office located on
the first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center, or by calling 978-3475. To confirm
a reservation a deposit is required. The confirmation deposit will be applied towards
the East Patio, Ballroom or Room #223 usage fees and charges.

### Contract and Fee Payment Schedule

title: Sodance
text:
The signed event contract along with all applicable fees must be received by the Reservations
Manager a minimum of five (5) working days prior to the scheduled event. Failure to
meet the deadline will constitute cancellation of the event.

Click Here to obtain a PDF of the contract

### Cancellation Procedures

The confirmation deposit is refundable if a reservation is cancelled five (5) working
days prior to the scheduled event.

Any cancellation after five (5) working days up to twenty-four (24) hours prior to
the scheduled event will constitute loss of deposit.

### Eligibility and Admittance Procedures for Student Dances

title: Sodance
text:
The student organization will control admittance to student dances under the following
guidelines and with supervision of the Rhatigan Student Center Event Manager. The
following categories of persons with valid picture identification are eligible to
attend a student dance.

- **Category 1:** A Wichita State University or other college student with a current student identification
card.
- **Category 2:** A graduate/alumni with a graduate, alumni, or Greek ID.
- **Category 3:** Active members of the Armed Forces of the United States with a current military ID.

title: Sodance
text:
To ensure the safety of students attending the dance everyone must produce a picture
ID that establishes his/her eligibility to attend the dance. Each eligible person
attending the dance may sponsor a guest, if the guest has a picture ID. An eligible
person must accompany his/her guest to the event and register with the organization
in charge. Eligible persons without a guest are not required to register.

The sponsoring organization will check ID's throughout the event and must ensure all
persons attending the event meet the established attendance criteria. The Reservations
Manager and the sponsoring organization's representative will determine a location
to check ID's and collect admission.

title: Sodance
text:
The Rhatigan Student Center Event Manager will monitor activities throughout the evening.
If a violation should occur, the Event Manager will inform the sponsoring organization,
who in turn will be expected to resolve the problem.

### Security

The Wichita State University Police Department will coordinate the hiring of security
officers for the safety of all attendees during an event held on the East Patio, in
the Ballroom or Room #223 in the Rhatigan Student Center. The number of security officers
needed will be determined by the University Police Chief based upon the nature of
the event.

Officers hired for the event will assist in all medical emergencies, provide assistance
to the Event Manager and sponsoring organization, as well as enforce policies and
procedures of the Rhatigan Student Center and Wichita State University.

title: Sodance
text:
The sponsoring organization will incur the costs for four (4) officers at dances where
alcohol is served or three (3) officers at dances where alcohol is not served. Wichita
State University will incur any further security costs in most cases, including additional
officers as determined by the University Chief of Police.

### Magnetometers

The student organization is responsible for providing ID checkers, ushers, and attendants
for the East Patio, Ballroom and Room #223, as determined by the Reservations Manager.

Loitering is prohibited on Rhatigan Student Center premises and in the parking lot.

Dances will end no later than 1:00 A.M. The East Patio, Ballroom or Room #223, surrounding
environs, and the parking lot must be vacated within thirty (30) minutes of the dance's
scheduled ending time.

title: Sodance
text:
Due to security reasons the student organization will not permit a person who leaves
the Rhatigan Student Center East Patio, Ballroom or Room #223 to return to the dance.

The sponsoring organization is responsible for handling and security of its funds.

The sponsoring organization is responsible for controlling its members and guests
during the event. Security officers will provide assistance as needed.

All policies and procedures not covered herein will be covered by the Event Manager
at an Event Briefing one hour prior to the event.

### Advertisement

Advertisement of all events is encouraged, however, it is required that groups obtain
approval from the Reservations Manager prior to advertising. The following information
is required on all advertisements:

title: Sodance
text:
1. Name of the sponsoring organization.
2. Specifically state who is eligible to attend event.
3. Identify the start and end times for the event.

Food and Beverage/Alcoholic Beverage Service

University Dining Services retains all rights to sell and/or serve food and beverages
within Rhatigan Student Center facilities and its environs. Organizations requiring
food and/or beverage service for an event must contract for the service through the
University Dining Services' Office, located on the first floor of the Rhatigan Student
Center, 978-3477.

Cereal malt beverage and/or alcoholic liquor service must be in compliance with University
policy.

### Event Briefing

title: Sodance
text:
The Rhatigan Student Center Event Manager will conduct a mandatory briefing one hour
prior to the event's scheduled starting time, for representatives of the sponsoring
organization and all security officers. Introductions, policies and procedures, and
individual assignments will be made. We strongly suggest the sponsoring organization's
faculty/graduate advisor be present as well. The sponsoring organization's certified
representative who signed the contract and any persons assigned a duty such as ID
checkers, ushers, attendants, and admission personnel are required to attend, NO exceptions.

The event briefing will start at the University Reservations Office. If the required
personnel from the sponsoring organization are not present the Event Manager is authorized
to cancel the event.

### Ending Times

title: Sodance
text:
The sponsoring organization will make an announcement fifteen minutes prior to the
end of the event, advising all persons in attendance of the scheduled end time. Music
will stop precisely at the scheduled end time. In order to ensure a safe and casual
exit, thirty (30) minutes will be allowed for the exiting of the environs and parking
lot.

### Policy and Procedure Violations

The Reservations Manager or the Event Manager may cancel any event if the sponsoring
organization fails to correct or comply with the Rhatigan Student Center Event Policy
or fulfill its responsibilities either prior to or during the event.

Any safety or security issue that may arise during an event which is not corrected
on the spot can result in the immediate termination of the dance.

title: Sodance
text:
Event policy violations can result in the suspension of the student organization's
privilege to reserve the Rhatigan Student Center environs for further events. A Division
of Student Affairs review panel hears and resolves all grievances.

### Liability

The sponsoring organization will be held responsible for the actions of the persons
attending the event regardless of whether those persons are members of their organization.
The organization is responsible for any physical damage to the premises and/or equipment.

**Effective**: 7/1994
**Revised**: 1/2003

title: Creditcards
text:
# Creditcards

**POLICY
RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER
CREDIT CARD SOLICITATION**

The Rhatigan Student Center is one of two facilities on the campus of Wichita State
University where the solicitation of credit card applications is permitted. All reservations
for scheduling space for the solicitations of credit card applications must be completed
in accord with specific requirements established by Wichita State University and the
Rhatigan Student Center. The following RSC policies apply:

title: Creditcards
text:
1. Companies who schedule space in the Rhatigan Student Center to solicit credit card
applications must do so through the University Reservations Office, located on the
first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center.
2. Companies who schedule space in the Rhatigan Student Center to solicit credit card
applications must obtain approval from the University Reservations Office for the
types of cards to be solicited.
3. No solicitation of credit card applications from students shall take place on campus
during the week before and two weeks following the beginning of each semester. This
policy shall not apply to any banking institution which has an "affinity card" contract
currently in effect with the University or an affiliated corporation of the University
or to any branch bank located in the Rhatigan Student Center or any credit union with
an office on the campus of Wichita State University.
4. Companies who schedule space in the Rhatigan Student Center to solicit credit card
applications must be provide written information on the responsible use of credit
and the risks of credit card use. The University Reservations Office will provide
the required information and the company will insure that the information is available
for students to obtain.
5. A 30" X 72" table and two chairs are provided to companies who schedule space in the
Rhatigan Student Center to solicit credit card applications. Companies are allowed
to provide additional tables or equipment on a limited basis at the scheduled location.
6. All representatives with companies who schedule space in the Rhatigan Student Center
to solicit credit card applications must check with the University Reservations Office
upon their arrival on campus and provide a copy of the on-campus representative's
identification, to be kept on file in the University Reservations Office.
7. Payment for facility rental fees must be paid to the University Reservations Office
ten business days prior to the schedule date by companies who schedule space in the
Rhatigan Student Center to solicit credit card applications. Payment may be made by
cash, certified check, credit card or money order. Failure to meet the deadline will
result in an automatic cancellation of the reservation by the University Reservations
Office without further notification to the company. Cancelations by companies must
be made ten business days prior to the scheduled date. Any cancellations made after
ten days will result in a loss in rental fees previously paid, or a charge assessed
to the scheduling party.
8. A representative from the company who schedules space in the Rhatigan Student Center
to solicit credit card applications must be at the table at all times in order that
they may answer questions, etc. Those persons must stay within proximity of the table.
9. Hawking, defined as "advertising or peddling by shouting", is not permitted by representatives
of a company who schedules space in the Rhatigan Student Center to solicit credit
card applications. Customers of the Rhatigan Student Center interested in information
about credit card applications must approach the table before a representative of
the company may initiate a conversation with the customer.
10. All items that are given away by a company who schedules space in the Rhatigan Student
Center to solicit credit card applications must have prior approval by the University
Reservations Office. All items must be removed from the table by the company at the
end of each day.
11. Companies who schedule space in the Rhatigan Student Center to solicit credit card
applications must identify the company with signage at the table. Signage may be hung
from the tables with masking tape only. Nothing may be affixed to brick, vinyl, glass
or painted wall with tape, nails or thumbtacks. Signage may be hung with string on
the bricks only.
12. The University Reservations Office reserves the right to schedule space for similar
or like companies on the same day.
13. Any deviation from the above policies must be approved by the University Reservations
Office. Requests for exceptions should be submitted in writing to the Reservations
Manager.
14. The Rhatigan Student Center is not responsible for lost, stolen or damaged personal
property or merchandise. In consideration for use of the Rhatigan Student Center facilities,
the group waives any claim for damages or injury which may arise.
15. Wichita State University's policy regarding "Solicitation on Campus by Credit Card
Companies" is available in the *University's Policies and Procedures Manual,* through the University's home page on the World Wide Web.

title: Postingnotices
text:
# Postingnotices

**POLICY
RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER
POSTING OF NOTICES**

The bulletin board on the first floor across from the display cases and next to the
E-mail station is the designated location in the Rhatigan Student Center for displaying
posters and flyers. The bulletin board is divided into sections, with each section
being designated for a specific subject. Each section is identified with a laminated
sign at the top of the board. The sections are designated as follows:

Community Information-displays notices of events or information of local interest.

Classified-displays notices of items for sale or rent or to buy.

Services-displays notices of information about services for hire (i.e. typing services,
maid services, tutoring, etc.).

Campus Organizations-displays notices about events, services or information sponsored
by a campus organization.

title: Postingnotices
text:
University Departments-displays notices about events, services or information sponsored
by a University department.

title: Postingnotices
text:
1. Postings are limited to one (1) flyer/poster per heading. The size of the postings
are limited to no larger than 11" X 17". Groups should place the flyer/poster under
the appropriate heading on the bulletin board.
2. No flyers/posters shall be posted on the exterior of the Rhatigan Student Center.
They may not be placed on painted surfaces, glass or vinyl walls anywhere on the interior
or exterior walls of the Rhatigan Student Center or its surrounding environments.
3. The bulletin board will be cleared of all flyers/posters on the last day of each month.
The Rhatigan Student Center staff will have charge of removing flyers/posters monthly
as well as any flyers/posters that do not comply with these guidelines.
4. Commercial businesses may not use Rhatigan Student Center space for posting notices
without prior approval from the University Reservations Office, located on the first
floor of the Rhatigan Student Center, 316-978-3475.
5. The Rhatigan Student Center will not accept the responsibility for any flyers/posters
taken or removed from the bulletin board.
6. Flyers/Posters or table tents may be placed in dining areas in the Rhatigan Student
Center only with prior approval from the Director of University Dining Services and
the Rhatigan Student Center's Marketing Manager.
7. During Student Government Association elections, each candidate may post up to three
(3) flyers/posters around the Rhatigan Student Center with string on brick walls only.
Tape may not be used on any walls. Flyers/posters must be removed the day following
the election.
8. Permission for exceptions to any of the above policies must be requested in writing
to the University Reservations Office.

title: Foodguidestaff
text:
# Foodguidestaff

**Wichita State University
Guidelines for
University Departments, Faculty,
Unclassified Professionals
& Classified Staff
to
Dispense Food on Campus**

**Definitions**

1. "**Food**" is any raw or processed substance or ingredients intended for consumption.
- "**Perishable Food**" is food capable of (1) supporting rapid and progressive growth of infectious or
toxigenic microorganisms that may cause food infections or food intoxications, or
(2) supporting the growth or toxin product of Clostridium botulinum. Perishable food
is considered potentially hazardous.

**Complimentary Food/Closed Potluck**

title: Foodguidestaff
text:
1. Persons providing the Food must do so at their own expense.
2. Persons eating the Food provided will not be charged.
3. Food may not be offered to the general public for consumption or offered in a public
setting.
4. Perishable Food must be maintained at its required temperature. Hot food must be kept
hot and cold food must be kept cold.
5. Closed potluck events may include Perishable Food items.

Copies of the "Guidelines for University Departments, Faculty, Unclassified Professionals
and Classified Staff to Dispense Food on Campus" are on file in the office of the
Vice President for Administration & Finance.

Effective: 4/2002

title: Foodguidestudent
text:
# Foodguidestudent

**Wichita State University
Guidelines for
Student Organizations
to
Sell/Dispense Food on Campus**

**Definitions**

1. "**Food**" is any raw or processed substance or ingredients intended for consumption.
2. "**Certified Food Handler**" is defined as any person working in a food preparation facility who engages in food
preparation or who comes in contact with any food, utensil or equipment used in connection
with preparation or service of food, and who has successfully completed food sanitation
education program provided by the Kansas Health Department.
3. "**Perishable Food**" is food capable of (1) supporting rapid and progressive growth of infectious or
toxigenic microorganisms that may cause food infections or food intoxications, or
(2) supporting the growth or toxin product of Clostridium botulinum. Perishable food
is considered potentially hazardous.

title: Foodguidestudent
text: **Permissible Food Service (Dispensing) Activities by Student Organizations**

title: Foodguidestudent
text:
1. **Closed Potluck/Complimentary Food**
1. Sponsoring student organizations must obtain approval to provide closed Potluck/Complimentary
Food prior to the scheduled event, from the administrator of the building where the
event is to be held. All applicable building policies/procedures must be adhered to
by sponsoring student organizations.
2. Persons providing the Food must do so at their own expense.
3. Persons eating the Food provided will not be charged.
4. Food may not be offered to the general public for consumption.
5. Perishable Food must be maintained at its required temperature. Hot Food must be kept
hot and cold Food must be kept cold.
6. Closed potluck events may include Perishable Food items.
7. Failure to adhere to these guidelines by student organizations may result in loss
of privileges, and/or disciplinary action instigated by the Vice President of Campus
Life and University Relations.

title: Foodguidestudent
text: **Permissible Food Service (Sales) Activities by Student Organizations**

title: Foodguidestudent
text:
1. **Bake Sales**
1. Sponsoring student organizations must obtain approval to hold a bake sale prior to
the scheduled sale, from the Office of Campus Life and University Relations as well
as from the administrator of the building where the sale is to be held. All applicable
building policies/procedures must be adhered to by sponsoring student organizations.
2. A Certified Food Handler must supervise the preparation and distribution of bake sale
items.
3. All bake sale items must be bundled into individual servings and sealed in either
plastic wrap or zip-lock bags. Non-sealing sandwich bags and aluminum foil is not
sufficient.
4. Approved signage must be located at the bake sale site identifying the sponsoring
organization and indicating that the bake sale items were prepared under the supervision
of a Certified Food Handler.
5. Perishable Food may not be sold at a bake sale.
6. Failure to adhere to these procedures by student organizations may result in loss
of privileges, and/or disciplinary action instigated by the Vice President of Campus
Life and University Relations.
2. **Perishable Food Sales**
1. Sponsoring student organizations must obtain approval to hold a perishable food sale
prior to the scheduled sale date, from the Office of Campus Life and University Relations
as well as from the administrator of the building where the sale is to be held. All
applicable building policies/procedures must be adhered to by sponsoring student organizations.
2. Certified Food Handler must be present during food preparation, distribution and sale
of perishable food items.
3. Perishable Food sales will be limited to specialty foods not otherwise available for
sale or distribution on campus or foods deemed integral to the nature of the event.
4. Approved signage must be located at the Perishable Food sale site perishable food
items were prepared under the supervision of a Certified Food Handler.
5. Failure to adhere to these procedures by student organizations may result in loss
of privileges, and/or disciplinary action instigated by the Vice President of Campus
Life and University Relations.

title: Foodguidestudent
text:
Copies of the "Guidelines for Student Organizations to Sell/Dispense Food on Campus"
are on file in the office of the Vice President for Office of Campus Life and University
Relations.

Effective: 4/2002

title: Banners
text:
# Banners

**POLICY
RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER
BANNER HANGING**

Space for departments or organizations to hang banners on the outside of the Rhatigan
Student Center may be scheduled through the University Reservations Office, located
on the first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center, 978-3475.

title: Banners
text:
1. The East Balcony is the designated area for hanging banners and is limited to three
at a time.
2. Banner sizes are limited to a maximum size of 4' X 15'.
3. Banner space is available to SGA recognized organizations, Wichita State University
departments or groups sponsored by either. Groups may reserve banner space for a maximum
of two (2) weeks consecutively and must wait two (2) weeks between reservations.
4. Groups are responsible for providing their banner along with 50' of rope that will
withstand the various elements, to the University Reservations Office no less than
two (2) days prior to the first day of the scheduled reservation. The RSC Operations
staff will hang all banners and remove banners within two (2) days after the last
day of the scheduled reservation.
5. The University Reservations Office or the Rhatigan Student Center cannot assume any
responsibility for damage while hanging or removing banners. If a banner is not picked
up in the University Reservations Office by the sponsoring organization in a timely
manner after the last day of the scheduled reservation, a fee may be assessed to the
group for the Rhatigan Student Center to store and/or dispose of the banner.
6. Banners cannot promote, advertise or otherwise advocate an illegal activity, or violate
any Rhatigan Student Center or Wichita State University policies.
7. All verbiage printed on the banner must be written in and/or translated to the English
language, and must be approved by the University Reservations Office prior to the
banner being displayed.
8. The Rhatigan Student Center cannot accept responsibility for damages or theft of banners.

title: Handbills

to instruction or study or at the immediate sites and times of enclosed public events.

title: Loungeuse
text:
# Loungeuse

**POLICY
RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER
LOUNGE USAGE**

Public lounges are located throughout the Rhatigan Student Center and are available
for scheduling special events. Lounges may be reserved by Wichita State University
departments and recognized student organizations at no charge. Groups who are not
recognized may reserve the lounges for a rental fee.

There are three (3) large lounges available for scheduling, located on the first floor
of the Rhatigan Student Center. The Fireplace Lounge is located on the North end of
the building, the Skylight Lounge at the Northeast, and the Shocker Lounge in the
center of the building.

Reservations for the Rhatigan Student Center lounges may be made through the University
Reservations Office, located on the first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center, 978-3475.
The following guidelines apply:

title: Loungeuse
text:
1. Reservations are made on a first-come, first-serve basis. A confirmation deposit may
be required.
2. The use of audio equipment is limited to one (1) public area at a time. A sound level
agreeable to the Rhatigan Student Center, as determined by the University Reservations
Office must be maintained.
3. Furniture in the lounges may be moved only upon special request. Rhatigan Student
Center personnel will be responsible for moving furniture according to any special
requests. These requests should be made at the time the area is scheduled.
4. Events in the Shocker lounge may not block entry into, nor exit from Commerce Bank
or the Shocker Card Center.
5. Cancelations should be made three (3) business days prior to the scheduled date.

Effective: 7/1994

RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER
PATIO USAGE**
