title: Alcohol
text:
# Alcohol

**POLICY
RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER
CEREAL MALT BEVERAGE/ALCOHOLIC LIQUOR POLICIES**

**CEREAL MALT BEVERAGE**

The Rhatigan Student Center holds a Cereal Malt Beverage (CMB) license only for the
Rec Center. Customers wishing to serve 3.2% beer in any other area of the RSC must
obtain a temporary license from the City of Wichita, by applying for one at City Hall
Express, in the City building on North Main street. Once a group has obtained a CMB
license, they must provide a copy of the license to University Dining Service for
their records. When these steps have been completed, the following policies will be
enforced:

title: Alcohol
text:
1. University Dining Services is in charge of checking individuals to insure all are
of legal drinking age, and for providing & dispensing the 3.2% beer and collecting
monies.
2. No persons under 21 years of age are allowed to possess or to consume 3.2% beer at
any event at which these beverages are served or sold.
3. If an event is open to the public, the sponsoring group may not purchase 3.2% beer
and then give it away to attendees.
4. University Dining Service must make available, a non-alcoholic beverage at events
where 3.2% beer is served.
5. Consumption of 3.2% beer is permitted only within the approved area designated for
the event.
6. For events scheduled in the Rec Center, the sponsoring group must purchase the 3.2%
beer from the Rec Center. It is the Rec Center's responsibility for checking individuals
to insure all are of legal drinking age, and for providing & dispensing the 3.2% beer
and collecting monies.

title: Alcohol
text:
**ALCOHOLIC LIQUOR**

Board of Regents policy states that alcoholic liquor may be served only at luncheons,
dinners or receptions which occur in connection with official university events and/or
fund-raising activities for university programs. The service of alcoholic liquor at
such events must be approved in advance by the President of the University, or the
President's designee. The service of alcoholic liquor in circumstances other than
above is prohibited unless approved by the University President, or the President's
designee.

Policies for serving alcoholic liquor in the Rhatigan Student Center are as follows:

title: Alcohol
text:
1. A letter of approval from the President or his designee must be provided to University
Dining Service for their records.
2. University Dining Service is responsible for dispensing all alcoholic liquor in the
RSC. The sponsoring group must provide the alcoholic liquor to University Dining Service
for serving. The sponsoring group must purchase the setups, bartender service, etc.
from University Dining Service.
3. At all events in which alcoholic liquor is approved for use, a non-alcoholic beverage
must also be made available to attendees.
4. Food must be made available at all functions where alcoholic liquor is served.
5. Alcoholic liquor may not be served at an event that is open to the public. Alcoholic
liquor may not be sold to attendees of an event.
6. Alcoholic liquor may not be served to persons under the age of 21.

Effective: 9/1998

title: Campusfacilities
text:
# Campusfacilities

**POLICY
WICHITA STATE UNIVERSITY
USE OF CAMPUS FACILITIES**

To carry out the University's mission, the facilities of Wichita State University
are primarily for use by its students, faculty and staff for activities and programs
that are directly related to the basic educational functions of teaching, research,
and preparation of scholarly material. University facilities shall be made available
on a basis that attempts to ensure fair and appropriate usage thereof while accommodating
the University's academic and instructional needs and protecting the investment of
the State in said facilities.

title: Campusfacilities
text:
Classrooms, laboratories and other facilities which are to be used for teaching and
instructional programs are scheduled by the Registrar on the basis of need and as
a first priority. After the initial academic schedules are reviewed and assigned space,
unscheduled space is made available to the University Reservations Office for assignment
to qualified users as a second priority on a first-request basis. All use of University
facilities for purposes other than teaching and instructional programs, whether sponsored
by individual schools, colleges or departments of the University; by bureaus, centers
or institutes of the University; or by officially recognized organizations must be
scheduled by the University Reservations Office located in the Rhatigan Student Center
or the person designated to make reservations of the Special Use Facilities listed
on the reverse side. As a third priority, the University, as a State institution with
a basic service function, may grant use of its facilities to:

title: Campusfacilities
text:
1. University, State of Kansas, and other Governmental Agencies, etc.
2. Non-University businesses, churches, groups, agencies, etc.

**General Campus Facilities**

The first priority for use of University facilities is assigned to colleges, schools,
departments, bureaus, agencies and sponsored organizations or activities in carrying
out the University's basic educational functions enumerated above.

The general public may be invited to attend activities sponsored by the University
through its colleges, schools, departments, bureaus and agencies or by a sponsored
University organization.

Colleges, schools, departments, bureaus and agencies and University-sponsored organizations
should limit the sponsorship of non-academic activities to programs which fall under
the purview of their official departmental function.

title: Overview
text:
# Overview

**The Rhatigan Student Center Facility Policies and Procedures**

title: Overview
text:
Facilities and services of the Rhatigan Student Center are open to the University
and general public, subject to Wichita State University and Rhatigan Student Center
policies and procedures. Reservations are accepted between 7:30 AM-5 PM, Monday through
Friday. A reservation may be made in person in the University Reservations Office,
located on the first floor in the Rhatigan Student Center, by calling 316-978-3475
or by e-mailing the University Reservations Office at LetsMeet@wichita.edu . E-mail or telephone requests submitted on a holiday or a Saturday or Sunday, will
not be processed until the next business day. Meeting room reservations should be
made at least 48 hours in advance. More time should be allowed for catered events,
preferably a minimum of two weeks prior to the date of the event. Requests are taken
on a first come, first serve basis. Room assignments are made according to the size
and function of the event.
The Facility Policies and Procedures are designed to give facility users a clear
understanding of their responsibilities.

title: Overview
text:
**EVENT LOGISTICS**

**Access and Event Times** Facility access and use must be within allotted confirmed times as noted on the Event
Confirmation. Confirmed times must include event preparation, decorating, and/or rehearsal
times as well as time after the event to remove decorations, user's equipment and
other items. Events that have not removed all decorations, equipment and other items
by the scheduled ending time for the event, will be assessed an After-Hours fee. The
Rhatigan Student Center staff shall have the right to access and enter the event space
for any reasonable purpose during the confirmed time.

title: Overview
text:
**Cancelation by Facility** Permission to use the Rhatigan Student Center is granted subject to observance of
regulations. The Rhatigan Student Center may revoke this permission immediately upon
failure to timely comply with pre-event requirements/deadlines, for any violation
of use conditions or regulations, or at any time for misrepresentation. The Rhatigan
Student Center may terminate any part of this permission without notice in the event
of an emergency situation that, in the opinion of the Rhatigan Student Center, would
make the event unfeasible.

title: Overview
text:
**Cancelation by User** Groups are responsible for all rental fees, when applicable, if their reservation
in the Rhatigan Student Center is canceled less than 24 hours prior to the date of
the event. For recurring events, the first time a group is a "no show", a warning
will be made with the group's contact person. A second "no show" within the same semester
will result in the group's scheduling privileges being suspended for the remainder
of that semester. Cancelations for catered events (at 316-978-5863) are to be made
no less than 5 business days prior to the event, in order to avoid incurring a cancellation
charge. To receive a refund of a confirmation deposit, notice must be received in
the University Reservations Office and acknowledged, no less than ten (10) working
days prior to the date of the event.

title: Overview
text:
**Eligibility** University departments and recognized student organizations receive priority when
requesting space in the Rhatigan Student Center, subject to Wichita State University
and Rhatigan Student Center policies and procedures. Student organizations who have
not been recognized by the Student Government Association but are in the process of
getting recognized, are entitled to two organizational meetings at no charge, prior
to its recognition. The purpose of these organizational meetings is to announce the
group's establishment to the University's student population in order to recruit new
members.

**Event Schedules** Daily Event Schedules are posted at all entrances into the Rhatigan Student Center
as well as outside of each meeting room.

title: Overview
text:
**Facilities** Users of the Rhatigan Student Center shall observe all applicable Rhatigan Student
Center and Wichita State University policies, as well as all local, state and federal
laws, statutes, and ordinances. The user shall only have the use of the facilities
as stated in the Event Confirmation. All alterations to the facility, building systems
or equipment are subject to approval from the University Reservations Office. The
user shall follow all reasonable directives from Rhatigan Student Center staff. At
the end of the event, the facility should be left in a clean, safe condition.

title: Overview
text:
**Inclement Weather Sites** Consideration should be given for events scheduled to take place outdoors, regarding
an alternative indoor location to hold the event, in the case of inclement weather.
Inclement weather sites will not be scheduled for events where control of room capacity
and banned items (donated food, alcohol, etc.) cannot be maintained.

**Insurance** Depending on the nature and scope of the facility use, the user may be required to
furnish a certificate of insurance naming the Rhatigan Student Center and various
University entities as additionally insured. Required certificates must be received
by the Rhatigan Student Center fourteen (14) days prior to the event date.

title: Overview
text:
**Liability** Users of the Rhatigan Student Center agree to indemnify, protect, defend and hold
harmless the Rhatigan Student Center, Wichita State University, its Board of Trustees,
officers, employees, agents and students from and against any and all claims, demands,
losses, costs, damages or liability of any nature or character arising out of or by
reason of the execution or performance of the rights, duties and obligations arising
out of or incidental to the use of the facility or equipment. The user agrees to abide
and enforce the rules, regulations and policies governing the facility as set forth
by the Rhatigan Student Center and Wichita State University. The user accepts all
responsibility for any damages to premises, equipment or grounds resulting from use
of the facility.

title: Overview
text:
**Premises** The Rhatigan Student Center may use any part of the premises that is not confirmed
to a user at any time, providing that such does not interfere with the user's use
of confirmed space.

**Priority** University departments as well as registered/recognized student organizations are
given priority for usage of the Rhatigan Student Center. Off-campus groups and individuals
have scheduling privileges of the facilities after campus needs are met.

**Reassignment of Facilities** Should space in the Rhatigan Student Center become unavailable due to an emergency,
the Rhatigan Student Center reserves the right to reassign the user to another space
within the facility or reschedule for another date. The University Reservations Office
will notify the user as soon as the need arises for a reassignment of facilities.

title: Overview
text:
**Reoccurring Events** Weekly meetings may be scheduled one semester at a time, beginning in July or December.
Monthly or quarterly meetings may be scheduled for the upcoming academic year, beginning
in July. The University Reservations Office reserves the right to make room changes
in order to accommodate special events.

**Responsible Party(s)/Event Coordination Deadline** The person(s) who schedules the facility shall be the responsible party. If the person
coordinating the event is not planning to be in attendance the day of the event, a
designated representative will be communicated to the University Reservations Office.
This representative shall take all reasonable actions to assure event safety, to prevent
damage to the facility and equipment, and to see that these conditions and other policies
and regulations outlined in the Facility Policies and Procedures are met.

title: Overview
text:
**Special Requirements** Special requirements, such as overnight storage of equipment, activation of data/phone
lines or signals, access for news/media, or other such requirements must be coordinated
in advance with the respective University departments. Charges for such services could
apply.

**FEES, PAYMENTS AND TAXES**

**After-Hours Fees** University departments, individuals and off-campus users desiring use of the Rhatigan
Student Center at times other than during its regular hours of operation, may be charged
an after-hours fee. Current after-hours fees may be verified with the University Reservations
Office.

title: Overview
text:
**Deposits/Payment** If applicable, a deposit may be required in order to confirm a reservation. Facilities
will not be held beyond ten (10) working days without receipt of this deposit. If
the requested date is more than three (3) months in advance, a 50% deposit of the
estimated costs is required to confirm the reservation. The balance of the estimated
costs is due ten (10) working days in advance of the scheduled date. If the requested
date is less than ten (10) working days in advance, the total of the estimated costs
is required to confirm the reservation. After final payment has been received, any
charges incurred due to last minute changes, must be paid at the time the changes
are requested.

title: Overview
text:
**Outstanding Balances** The University Reservations Office invoices weekly. All invoices must be paid within
thirty (30) days of the event date. Accounts must be paid in full in order for a University
department or student organization to be allowed to maintain scheduling privileges.

**Permits and Taxes** The scheduling organization is responsible for obtaining permits or licenses as required
by law. A copy of such permits or licenses must be provided to the University Reservations
Office five (5) working days prior to the scheduled event date.

**EQUIPMENT AND PROPERTY**

title: Overview
text:
**Abandoned Property** Any property not removed from the Rhatigan Student Center that has not been claimed
within forty-eight (48) hours following the conclusion of the scheduled event will
be considered abandoned by the user and/or its exhibitors. The Rhatigan Student Center
may take possession of it and treat it as its own or dispose of such property without
liability. The user may be liable for the costs incurred in disposing of the abandoned
property.

**Damage to Facility/Damage Deposits** Users of the Rhatigan Student Center are responsible for the condition of the facility
for the duration of their scheduled event. The Rhatigan Student Center shall inspect
the facility to determine if any damage was sustained as a result of the user's occupancy.
Repairs for significant damages will be charged to the user. Some events/organizations
may require refundable damage deposits.

title: Overview
text:
**Decorations/Signs** The University Reservations Office must approve any decorations, banners or signs.
Rhatigan Student Center signage cannot be covered or otherwise obstructed. Nothing
may be affixed to the drapes, vinyl coverings, ceilings, wood surfaces, painted walls
or floors. All decorations must be flame retardant. All decorations, props and outdoor/indoor
directional and promotional signage must be removed by the user immediately following
the event or they will be disposed of by the Rhatigan Student Center staff. Rice,
birdseed, glitter, confetti or substances that stain or become imbedded into the carpet
are not allowed in the Rhatigan Student Center.

title: Overview
text:
**Equipment** All Rhatigan Student Center equipment (i.e. tables, chairs, staging, flip charts,
etc.) will be set up by the Rhatigan Student Center staff. The user will be responsible
for all Rhatigan Student Center owned equipment and will be held liable for the equipment
if lost, stolen, damaged or misplaced.

**Special Equipment** Users of the Rhatigan Student Center intending to bring any equipment into the Rhatigan
Student Center that requires access to facility water, high voltage electrical, satellite
signals or such systems must receive advance authorization and approval from the University
Reservations Office.

title: Overview
text:
**User's Property** Users of the Rhatigan Student Center assume full responsibility to safeguard all
materials, goods or property owned or used by the user or any of its exhibitors or
guests. Users hereby waive any claims against the Rhatigan Student Center and its
employees for damages to, theft or loss of property.

**SAFETY ISSUES**

**Capacities** The Rhatigan Student Center will not permit its facilities to be occupied greater
than the listed capacities.

**Emergency Medical Service** The Rhatigan Student Center reserves the right to require emergency medical services
be present, if deemed necessary, based on the type of event scheduled.

**Flames/Fire** Open flames and the burning of any materials, including incense, is prohibited. Use
of candles must receive advance approval from the University Reservations Office and
meet fire code regulations.

title: Overview
text:
**Fire Regulations** Users, exhibitors and their guests of the Rhatigan Student Center must comply with
all Federal, State and local fire and building codes that apply to spaces of public
assembly. Facility fire fighting and emergency equipment may not be hidden or obstructed.
All emergency exits, hallways and aisles leading from the Rhatigan Student Center
must be kept clear and unobstructed.

**Recreational Devices** Bicycles, skates and other such recreational devices are not allowed to be operated
in or around the Rhatigan Student Center.

title: Overview
text:
**Security** - The Rhatigan Student Center staff and/or the WSU Police shall solely determine
and control security arrangements including but not limited to the type and number
of security personnel and placement and use of security personnel. The Rhatigan Student
Center staff and/or the WSU Police reserve the right to require police at events where
alcohol beverages are served. Only WSU Police or their designees may be hired to act
as security for events scheduled in the Rhatigan Student Center. Only licensed law
enforcement officers may carry firearms in the facility.

**Smoking** - The Rhatigan Student Center is a non-smoking facility.

**Special Effects** Fog machines, dry ice or smoke machines that may trigger the fire protection system
to be activated or impede an evacuation from the facility, are not permitted in the
Rhatigan Student Center.

title: Overview
text:
**Weapons/Firearms** All weapons and firearms are strictly prohibited in the Rhatigan Student Center.

**MISCELLANEOUS**

**Alcohol Service** Users of the Rhatigan Student Center agree to abide by and to enforce the University
policies regarding the consumption of alcoholic beverages. All alcoholic beverage
service arrangements for events in the Rhatigan Student Center must be coordinated
through WSU Dining Services.

**Animals** Animals are prohibited in the Rhatigan Student Center with the exception of service
animals assisting persons with special needs.

title: Overview
text:
**Conduct** Users and guests of the Rhatigan Student Center shall not interfere with the regular
use of the Rhatigan Student Center by the public or other facility guests. Excessive
noise or other disruptive behavior is prohibited. The Rhatigan Student Center may
remove any person whom they believe is disrupting or obstructing the daily operation
and management of the facility. Users who abuse their usage of the facility will be
denied future scheduling privileges.

**Food and Beverage Service** WSU Dining Services is the exclusive vendor of all food and beverage services in
the Rhatigan Student Center. Copies of the Food Guidelines-University Departments
and Food Guidelines-Student Organizations may be obtained from the University Reservations
Office for reference.

title: Overview
text:
**Gambling** Users of the Rhatigan Student Center agree to abide by and enforce the University
policies regarding gambling in the facility.

**Publicity** The Rhatigan Student Center reserves the right to approve, in advance, all forms
of advertising or publicity for any activity scheduled in its facility. Users shall
not advertise any event until a confirmed reservation has been made.

title: Overview
text:
**Vehicle Parking/Unloading** Users and guests of the Rhatigan Student Center must abide by all University parking/traffic
requirements, including but not limited to passenger and equipment loading/unloading
regulations, observance of authorized parking locations, payment of fees, and display
of vehicle parking permits. Access to the loading docks must be coordinated with the
University Reservations Office prior to the event. Parking in the loading docks is
prohibited and violators will be ticketed and/or towed at the owner's expense.

**ADDITIONAL POLICIES**

Additional policies for the Rhatigan Student Center may be found in their entirety,
on the Rhatigan Student Center's website at www.wichita.edu /rsc . They are listed under Policies and Procedures:

title: Overview
text:
- Banner Hanging
- Credit Card Solicitation
- Food & Beverage Service
- Guidelines for Student Organizations to Sell/Dispense Food on Campus
- Guidelines for University Departments, Faculty, Unclassified Professionals and Classified
Staff to Dispense Food on Campus
- Lost & Found
- Patio Usage
- Plastic Table Tents
- Posting of Notices
- Serving Cereal Malt Beverage/Alcohol
- Student Organization Events Scheduled on the East Patio, RSC Ballroom or Room #223
- Student Organization Events Scheduled in the CAC Theater
- Table Usage/Merchandise Sales
- Tent Usage
- Usage of Facility Beyond Scheduled Building Hours

title: Tableuse
text:
# Tableuse

**POLICY
RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER
TABLE USAGE/MERCHANDISE SALES**

Tables available for distributing information and/or merchandise sales in the Rhatigan
Student Center are reserved through the University Reservations Office, located on
the first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center, 978-3475. The following guidelines
apply:

**RESERVATIONS**

title: Tableuse
text:
1. Tables available for scheduling are located on the first floor of the Rhatigan Student
Center. There are four (4) stationary locations which are reserved on a first-come,
first-serve basis. A 30" X 72" table and two (2) chairs are provided. Groups are not
allowed to provide additional tables or equipment at the locations.
2. There is no rental charge for table usage to SGA recognized organizations, Wichita
State University departments or groups sponsored by either. Groups who are not recognized
or sponsored will be charged a daily rental fee. This fee must be paid by cash, certified
check or money order ten (10) business days prior to the scheduled date. Failure to
meet the deadline will constitute an automatic cancellation of the event.
3. Cancellations must be made ten (10) business days prior to the scheduled date. Any
cancellation made after ten (10) days will constitute a loss in rental fees previously
paid, or a charge assessed to the scheduling party.
4. Signage may be hung from the tables with masking tape only. Nothing may be affixed
to brick, vinyl, glass or painted walls with tape, nails or thumbtacks. Signage may
be hung with string on the brick walls only. A maximum of two (2) signs may be used.
5. A person affiliated with the sponsoring organization must be at the table at all times
in order that they may answer questions, etc. These persons must stay within the proximity
of the table.
6. Hawking, defined as "advertising or peddling by shouting", is not permitted.
7. All items must be removed from the table by the sponsoring organization at the end
of each day. Cleaning up of the area is the responsibility of the sponsoring organization.
8. Groups reserving table space must identify the table as being sponsored by their organization.
A sign for the table must be provided by the organization.
9. Groups wishing to use any type of electronic equipment must have approval of the University
Reservations Office prior to its use. In the event that extension cords are needed,
groups are responsible for providing their own, subject to approval by the University
Reservations Office.
10. Secured facilities for items to be stored overnight are available upon request, at
an additional charge. However, the Rhatigan Student Center cannot be held liable for
the damages to or loss of such items due to accidents, riots, acts of God or other
legitimate conditions beyond its control.

title: Tableuse
text: **MERCHANDISE SALES**

title: Tableuse
text:
1. The sponsoring organization agrees to display or make available, all refund and guarantee
policies.
2. The Rhatigan Student Center reserves the right to schedule sales of similar or like
items on the same day.
3. The sponsoring organization is responsible for all loading and unloading of products
to be sold. The Rhatigan Student Center cannot provide assistance. Carts/dollies are
not available.
4. Certain types of promotional activities/merchandise sales are not allowed in the Rhatigan
Student Center. They include, but are not limited to:
- Food sales of any kind.
- Sales of items with copyrighted University logos.
- Sales that require people to pay in advance and receive their merchandise at a later
date.
- Services and/or sales of items that conflict with services and/or items already being
provided and/or sold by the Rhatigan Student Center, Wichita State University and/University
Dining Services.
5. Any items given away by the sponsoring organization must not conflict with items sold
or given away by the Rhatigan Student Center. Approval of items may be obtained through
the University Reservations Office. Certain items to be given away may be available
through the University Bookstore or University Dining Services for purchase by the
sponsoring organization.
6. Sponsoring organizations who are soliciting credit card applications must obtain approval
from the University Reservations Office for the types of credit cards to be promoted.
Credit card solicitations may not occur beginning one week prior to the start of each
semester, through the end of the 2nd week of the semester.
7. Any deviation from the above policies must be approved by the University Reservations
Office. Requests for exceptions should be submitted in writing to the Reservations
Manager.
8. The Rhatigan Student Center and/or Wichita State University are not responsible for
lost, stolen or damaged personal property or merchandise. In consideration for use
of the Rhatigan Student Center facilities, the group waives any claim for damages
or injury which may arise.

title: Beyondbldghours
text:
# Beyondbldghours

**POLICY
RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER
USAGE OF FACILITY BEYOND SCHEDULED BUILDING HOURS**

The Rhatigan Student Center has established operating hours for each fall and spring
semester and each summer session.

1. Groups or individuals who desire usage beyond the established operating hours must
obtain approval from the Reservations Manager.
2. Requests will be addressed on an individual case basis.
3. An hourly charge will be assessed for each hour that the building is open before or
after established operating hours.
4. The current hourly charge for overtime usage will be quoted by the Reservations Manager.

Effective: 7/1994

title: Forms and Policies
text:
# Forms and Policies

## Forms

If you have questions about these forms or policies, please call (316) 978-3475, email
letsmeet@wichita.edu or visit Rhatigan Student Center Room 234.

- **Approved Caterer Application** — Submit this application to become a RSC approved caterer.
- **Approved Alcohol Provider Application** — Submit this application to become a RSC approved alcohol provider.
- **Sponsorship Request** — Submit this form to provide WSU departmental sponsorship of a non-WSU group usage
of facilities.
- **University Alcohol Service Request Form** - Submit this application to request alcohol or cereal malt beverage service on campus.

### Policies

---

## RENTAL FEES

Any room charges must be paid 2 weeks in advance. If no payment is made, the event
will be cancelled.

---

## EVENT TIMES

title: Forms and Policies
text:
All reservations made through the Event Services office include additional set up
time before and after an event. Please note, that if additional time (over those set
by Event Services) is needed there may be an added charge.

---

## EVENT DETAILS / SET UPS

Set-up notes for room reservations in the RSC or CAC Theater must be provided to the
Event Services staff 2 weeks in advance of your events. Receiving your set up notes
in a timely manner will allow us the opportunity to coordinate our services in preparation
for your event. Note: Last-minute changes to your set-up (on the day of your event)
may result in an additional charge of up to $100.

---

## CANCELLATIONS / NO SHOWS

title: Forms and Policies
text:
Guests who fail to cancel their reserved space and do not show up for their event
will receive a warning letter and may be billed for set-up charges. Student organizations
will have warning letters sent to Student Engagement and Belonging (SEB) and the organization’s
advisor. If this occurs more than 2 times in a semester the group will lose its privilege
to use Rhatigan Student Center facilities for the remainder of the semester. The Rhatigan
Student Center reserves the right to change and/or cancel a reservation or alter the
use of other assigned space with the understanding that, at all times, every effort
shall be made to provide comparable facilities.

---

## PARKING

title: Forms and Policies
text:
Parking for events held at the RSC is available on the 2nd and 3rd floor of the parking
garage located directly beside the RSC. Parking in the Parking Garage is $1.50 per
hour. Parking lots on the perimeter of the campus can be reserved for large events
that require additional space. Contact your Event Coordinator to request reserved
parking. Validation codes for parking are available on request. Contact your Event
Coordinator for additional information.

---

## DAMAGES

In the event that damage to RSC property or equipment occurs by an RSC guest, its
employees, agents, patrons or additional guests, the cost of repair and replacing
the damaged property may be charged to the guest.

---

## FACILITY SERVICES TABLES AND CHAIRS

title: Forms and Policies
text:
Outdoor tables that originate and are delivered by WSU Facility Services must be returned
to the original delivery location. Facility Services may charge customers for damages
or cleaning. If not needed table and chair orders must be cancelled, through your
Event Coordinator, 24 hours in advance.

---

## RSC CLEANING FEES

RSC guests are responsible for returning space to its original condition when their
event is completed. Any equipment, props or decorations belonging to RSC guests must
be removed promptly following the event. Event space requiring additional cleaning
maintenance may be billed at the rate of $75.00 per hour. The RSC does not allow the
following inside building spaces: use of open flame decorations, paint, glitter or
confetti.

---

## AUDIO / VISUAL EQUIPMENT

title: Forms and Policies
text:
For your convenience, RSC meeting rooms are equipped with large screen televisions
or projectors. All rooms are set up with A/V inputs. Occasionally, cables are needed.
The RSC Building Managers (978-3028) have a limited number of HDMI and Mac Adapters.
To make certain that the appropriate cable is available guests should provide their
own. Microphones are available for the Beggs Ballroom and Santa Fe Trail meeting room.
Guests requesting the use of microphones should arrive a minimum of 30 minutes in
advance to test microphones levels for their presentation. Audio/visual equipment
provided by the RSC should be left in the room and will be picked up by a Building
Manager following your event.

---

## AUDIO / VISUAL EQUIPMENT – LARGE EVENTS

title: Forms and Policies
text:
Events with complex audio/visual needs may require additional assistance. Customers
needing complicated or advanced audio/visual assistance should notify their Event
Coordinator in advance. RSC Event Coordinators may recommend contacting WSU Media
Resources at 978-3588 no less than 1 week in advance for support.

---

## CAC THEATER – PERFORMANCE FACILITIES

Events held in the Campus Activities Center (CAC) Theater that necessitate stage lighting
and sound may require the assistance of Performance Facilities. Your Event Coordinator
will advise you if you need to contact Performance Facilities at 978-3587 for your
event.

---

## TELECOMMUNICATIONS

If your meeting involves a conference call, broadcast or internet access, please email
the Telecommunications Office at telecomservices@wichita.edu

---

## CATERING / DINING SERVICES

title: Forms and Policies
text:
WSU Dining (Chartwells) is the on-campus provider of dining service needs. WSU Dining
can be reached at 978-3477. Rhatigan Student Center has a flexible catering policy
that allows approved off-campus food providers to cater events. A list of RSC approved
caterers can be found at: https://www.wichita.edu/services/rsc/eventservices/Catering.php .

Note To Approved Caterers- the Rhatigan Student Center charges caterers 10% of food
sales for events catered in the Rhatigan Student Center.

NOTE: Customers choosing an off-campus caterer for their event must remove all food
service containers and disposable items immediately following their event. Failure
to clean up after the event will result in a service charge for cleaning. For additional
information contact your Event Coordinator 978-3475.

---

## SECURE WIRELESS ACCESS

title: Forms and Policies
text:
WSU can provide secured hard-wired internet connections by request. For a secure WIFI
connection, contact your Event Coordinator at 978-3475 a minimum of 3 weeks in advance.

---

## ALCOHOL SERVICE

Requests for alcohol service must be approved by the WSU General Counsel prior to
the date of the event. The service of alcohol without prior approval is prohibited.

Approval is obtained by completing the following 2-3 weeks in advance:

- Notify your Event Coordinator of your request
- Complete a University Alcohol Request form available here .
- Off-campus guests must provide proof of liability insurance at time the request is
submitted.
- Guests will receive written notification of approval from the WSU General Counsel.

NOTE: Alcohol service requires a licensed bartender and that bartender must be present
throughout the event.

title: Forms and Policies
text:
A list of approved caterers offering alcohol service is available at: https://www.wichita.edu/services/rsc/eventservices/Approved\_Alcohol\_Service\_Providers.php

---

## DONATED FOOD REQUEST

On-campus groups wishing to serve donated food should refer to the Wichita State University
Food Service Policy 20.16 https://www.wichita.edu/about/policy/ch\_20/ch20\_16.php

---

## RECOGNIZED STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS

Recognized Student Organizations are required to meet guidelines established by the
Student Engagement and Belonging Office. Additional information is available at: https://www.wichita.edu/student\_life/seal/student\_organizations/forms\_policies.php

---

## INFORMATION TABLES

The RSC provides table space on the first and second floor for use by student organizations
and guests.

title: Forms and Policies
text:
- Table space is available to individual students, student organizations, WSU departments
and off-campus guests.
- Reservations for table space are required and must be made, in advance, either on-line
or at the Event Services office.
- Off-campus guests will be charged a daily rate for use of Information Tables.
- Information Table space may be used to promote an organization and/or activity.
- Individuals or groups, utilizing Information Tables, must remain behind their tables
when talking to RSC guests. “Hawking” (actively or aggressively pursuing students
to sell or promote) is not allowed.

---

## DONATION BOXES

title: Forms and Policies
text:
The RSC can provide Donation boxes for fundraising efforts. The boxes area available
for a 2 week period. Reservations can be made by contacting the RSC Event Services
office. Users must provide identification for the outside of the boxes. The RSC is
not responsible for items that have been lost or stolen.

---

## GRACE MEMORIAL CHAPEL

This interfaith prayer space is open on a first come, first serve basis to anyone
wishing to use it for private events.

The building is open Monday through Friday from 6 am to 8 pm and Saturday/Sunday by
reservation.

It is the responsibility of the guest to set up the space as needed and return it
to its condition. Food and beverages are prohibited. The RSC and Wichita State University
will not assume responsibility for items left in the Chapel following events.

---

## LOST / STOLEN ITEMS

title: Forms and Policies
text:
The Rhatigan Student Center is not responsible for items lost, stolen or damaged during
an event held in our facilities.

Guests looking for a lost item in the RSC should contact the RSC Event Services office
at 978-3475.

---

## FREEDOM OF EXPRESSION

Wichita State University and the Rhatigan Student Center are committed to preserving
and supporting freedom of thought, speech, and expression on our campuses.

Visit https://www.wichita.edu/about/policy/ch\_11/ch11\_12.php for more information.

You can also view the Kansas Board of Regents Statement on Free Expression here. https://www.kansasregents.org/resources/PDF/Students/Boards\_Statement\_on\_Free \_ Expression\_031721.pdf

---

# Catering Guidelines

## Application and Approval

The Rhatigan Student Center allows flexible catering options for campus events.

title: Forms and Policies
text:
For additional information contact the RSC Event Services office at 316-978-3475 or
letsmeet@wichita.edu

- Application to become an Approved Caterer is available here .
- Include a Certificate of Liability insurance naming Wichita State University Union
Corporation as additional named insured.
- When we have received your application, it will be reviewed and within approximately
10 days you will receive email notification as to whether it has been approved.
- Wichita State University and the Rhatigan Student Center have an exclusive beverage
contract with Coca Cola. All drinks served must be Coca Cola products.

---

## General Guidelines

title: Forms and Policies
text:
- Visit here to view the University's Food & Beverage Policies
- Catering must be provided by an approved caterer.
- All catering requests should accompany an existing space reservation.
- If your client has not already made a space reservation, please encourage them to
contact their event coordinator or department office as soon as possible.
- At the Rhatigan Student Center, caterers may unload at either the west dock located
off Isley Lane or the south dock located near the parking garage.
- A service elevator is available near each loading dock to access meeting spaces on
the second and third floor.
- Caterers may set up 2 hours in advance of the event start time. If you need additional
time please contact your Event Coordinator.
- You must clean up immediately following your event. The Rhatigan Student Center may
charge a $25 clean-up fee if facilities are not left in their original condition.
- The Rhatigan Student Center offers a prep kitchen on the third floor. Please note,
we do not have kitchen facilities for cooking. All food must be prepared in advance.
- The Rhatigan Student Center will supply table and chairs, however, caterers must supply
all tablecloths, napkins, glassware, serving ware and any items needed for catering
your event.

title: Forms and Policies
text:
The Rhatigan Student Center will charge caterers a 10 percent commission on food sales
at the Rhatigan Student Center. This commission is for food sales only and does not
include beverages.

---

## Alcohol Service Guidelines

- Alcohol can be served in the Rhatigan Student Center by licensed providers. Caterers
should be familiar with Wichita State University policy 11.07 available at http://webs.wichita.edu/inaudit/ch11\_07.htm
- Please notify us if you are licensed to serve alcohol in the state of Kansas. There
is an approval process.
- Your client must complete an alcohol request form and submit it 10 business days in advance with a certificate of insurance naming
Wichita State University Union Corporation as named insured.
- All requests for alcohol service must be approved through the Wichita State University
General Council’s office.

---

# RSC Customers, Events and Spaces

title: Forms and Policies
text:
## RSC Customers

### WSU Students and Recognized Student Organizations

- Student organizations that are officially recognized through Student, Engagement and
Belonging (SEB). RSOs are able to schedule meeting space in the Rhatigan Student Center,
the surrounding outdoor areas and the CAC Theater, free of charge during normal business
hours.
- Events scheduled outside of normal operating hours may be subject to “after hours”
charges.
- All events scheduled by RSOs must be approved through ShockerSync prior to scheduling.

### WSU Departments

- Official, recognized administrative and academic departments.
- WSU departments may schedule meeting rooms and spaces in the RSC, the surrounding
outdoor areas and the CAC Theater, free of charge during normal business hours.
- Events scheduled outside of normal operating hours may be subject to “after hours”
charges.

### Faculty and Staff

title: Forms and Policies
text:
- WSU employees with a current Shocker identification number.
- Faculty and staff may schedule space in the Rhatigan Student Center, surrounding outdoor
areas and the CAC Theater free of charge during normal business hours.
- Events scheduled outside of normal operating hours may be subject to “after hours”
charges.

### WSU Campus Partners

- All WSU Campus Partners, WSU departments located off-campus, and Innovation Campus
partners will receive a discounted rate for events scheduled in the RSC during normal
operating hours.
- Events scheduled outside of normal operating hours may be subject to “after hours”
charges

### External Off Campus Users

title: Forms and Policies
text:
- Any individual or organization located off campus and not directly affiliated with
WSU.
- External Off Campus Users will be charged a retail rate for the rental of space within
the RCS, surrounding outdoor spaces and the CAC Theater
- Events scheduled outside of normal operating hours may be subject to “after hours”
charges

### Non-profit Organizations

- Any organization holding official non-profit status with the government organizations.
- Non-profit and government organizations will receive a discounted rental rate.
- Events scheduled outside of normal operating hours may be subject to “after hours”
charges

---

## Event Classifications

### Internal (on-campus) Events

title: Forms and Policies
text:
- Events that are hosted by a WSU department or RSO and meets the following criteria.
- The event is fully funded by a WSU department or WSU recognized student group via
org/fund or foundation account.
- The WSU department or student organization is responsible for all aspects of the event
including attending pre-event meetings and being on-site during the event.
- The event is free to attendees, or revenue generated from the event is fully allocated
to the WSU department or student organization hosting the event.
- The event is not co-hosted or co-sponsored with a WSU department or organization.

### Sponsored Events

title: Forms and Policies
text:
- An event sponsored between a WSU department or Innovation Campus partner and an external
entity.
- The Sponsored group will receive a 30% discount on the rental fee.
- Both the WSU department and the Sponsored group must sign a sponsorship agreement.
- The RSC requires one point of contact for sponsored events.
- The RSC must receive payment within 30 days of the invoice, or the Sponsoring department/Innovation
Partner will be billed in full for all charges and fees.

### External (Off-Campus) Events

- Those events that do not meet the criteria for Internal or Sponsored Events.
- The retail or non-profit/government, Campus Partners rental rate will be charged accordingly.

---

## Misrepresentation

title: Forms and Policies
text:
WSU student organizations and WSU departments may not reserve space for other organizations
for the purpose of securing lower rental rates. The organization is, or individual(s)
named on the reservation are, the client and remain solely responsible for communicating,
initiating, planning, implementing, attending, and financing the event in coordination
with WSU.

Space reserved by an organization or individual must be used for the sole intended
purpose described on the Facility Use Agreement or EMS confirmation.

Clients may not give reserved space to another group.

WSU reserves the right to evaluate and make the final determination of all appropriate
fees and rates applied to event requests.

title: Forms and Policies
text:
Misrepresentation or violation of the conditions outlined herein will result in the
client being charged the higher rate structure and result in the suspension of reservation
privileges for the individual(s) and/or organization for whom the event was originally
intended.

title: Non-Benefit Eligible International Student Employment Checklist
text:
# Non-Benefit Eligible International Student Employment Checklist

## 1) Arrive in the United States

Welcome! We’re happy you’re here.

## 2) Enroll in Classes

You can enroll in classes after you complete the following steps:

- Arrive in Wichita.
- Complete the check-in process with the International Education department.
- Meet with your academic advisor.

## 3) Search and Apply for On-Campus Employment

Most on-campus positions are posted on Shocker Central .

- Use your myWSU ID and password to log in.
- If you have questions or need more information about Shocker Central call the Shocker
Career Accelerator at (316) 978-3688, or email us at SCA@wichita.edu .

## 4) Get a Job Offer

title: Non-Benefit Eligible International Student Employment Checklist
text:
You will need to receive an official offer. The Hiring Manager must complete the International Job Offer Form in **BLUE** ink. At this time, your Hiring Manager will also submit a Non-Benefit Eligible Hiring
Form, which indicates to Human Resources they wish to hire you for an on-campus position.

## 5) Request Employment Eligibility Verification

Take your completed International Job Offer Form and I-94 to the International Education
Department located in the Garvey International Center (GI) at 3203 E. 17th Street N. Wichita, KS 67208.

- If you need help finding this building, use this interactive map.
- Your I-94 can be obtained on the Customs and Border Protection site.

## 6) Pick up your Employment Eligibility Verification (EEV) at International Education

title: Non-Benefit Eligible International Student Employment Checklist
text:
After documents are provided, International Education will prepare your Employment
Eligibility Verification (EEV) within 2-4 business days. You will be contacted when
your EVV is ready to be picked up at the Garvey International Center.

## 7) Complete the online application for a Social Security Number

After you receive your Employment Eligibility Verification (EVV), complete the online application for a Social Security Number.

## 8) Complete In-Person Meeting at the Social Security Administration office

Go to the Social Security Administration office to show the appropriate documentation.

- The International Job Offer completed by a campus department.
- Employment Eligibility Verification prepared by International Education.
- Continued Attendance I-20 (for F-1 students) or DS-2019 with work authorization (for
J-1 students).
- Valid passport and I-94.

title: Non-Benefit Eligible International Student Employment Checklist
text:
The local Social Security Administration office is located at 3216 N Cypress Street,
Wichita, Kansas 67226. Visit Social Security Administration for office hours and additional information.

## 9) Wait for Social Security Card to Arrive

The card will arrive via mail and on average can take two weeks.

## 10) Receive Social Security Card

The card will arrive via mail and on average can take two weeks.

## 11) Complete all Onboarding Tasks

You cannot complete necessary forms until your Social Security card has been received.
At that time, complete all onboarding tasks assigned by Human Resources. These tasks
will be received via email. Human Resources cannot put you into WSU’s system without
all forms completed.

## 12) Complete I-9

title: Non-Benefit Eligible International Student Employment Checklist
text:
Human Resources allows walk-in appointments to complete your I-9 Form; however, you
can also schedule a specific appointment. Please use our online scheduling tool to set up an appointment to complete Section 2 of the Form I-9.

- Bring all necessary documentation which proves eligibility to work at Wichita State
University as an International Student.

## 13) Your Hiring Manager will submit an electronic personnel action form (ePAF)

Your Hiring Manager will submit an electronic personnel form (ePAF). Once approved,
your department contact or hiring manager notify you of a start date dependent on
your specific type of employment.

## 14) Begin Work

Congratulations!

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
# Tuition Assistance Program Policies

## Program Policies

Tuition assistance is available for eligible Wichita State University employees and
their dependents and/or spouses who wish to further their education through classes
in an eligible program at the University. Eligibility requirements and tuition assistance
policies vary by applicant type. Please see below for additional information on the
tuition assistance program.

Program Timelines

Employee Assistance

Spouse/Dependent Assistance

Additional Program Information

Availability of Funds

---

### Program Timelines

Applications for employees, spouses and dependents may be submitted annually beginning
May 1st for the upcoming academic year that begins in Fall.  You may apply for any
and all applicable semesters (Fall, Spring and Summer) for which the application deadline
has not passed at the time of your application.

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
All applications are reviewed in full before a final decision is made, and the official
notification of award status will be sent to applicants within 30 days of the deadline
for each academic term.

**Due to the volume of applications received, applications received after the applicable
semester deadline will be automatically denied. There will be no exceptions.**

| | | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Term** | **Application Deadline** | **Notification of Award** |
| Fall | PRIORITY: July 1\* FINAL: August 4 (Award is based on funding availability. ) | August 23 |
| Spring | PRIORITY: Dec 1\* FINAL: Jan 6 | Jan 12 |
| Summer | April 15\* | May 15 |

\*When the deadline falls on a weekend or holiday, applications will be accepted through
the end of the following University business day.

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
\*\*Priority deadline for tuition assistance applications is for applications received
by that first deadline, with the final deadline of closer to the start of the semester.
Awards for applications received after priority deadline will be based on availability
of funds.  

Back to Top

### Tuition Assistance Program for Employees

#### Eligibility

To be eligible for tuition assistance as an employee of WSU, applicants must meet
ALL of the following requirements:

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
- Active appointment status as an Unclassified Professional (UP), Faculty (FA), or University
Support Staff (USS); employees on unpaid leave are not eligible.
- Benefits-eligible (i.e. accrue sick/vacation leave)
- FTE status 0.5 or greater
- Employee must maintain an overall grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 for undergraduate
programs or an overall GPA of 3.0 for graduate programs, which will be reviewed after
final grades are entered for each completed term. Failure to meet this requirement
will make the Employee ineligible for tuition assistance until the Employee’s overall
GPA is greater than 2.0 for undergraduate programs or 3.0 for graduate programs.

#### Award

The maximum award per academic term is limited to the cost of resident tuition plus
associated infrastructure fees up to a maximum of ONE of the following options:

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
- Seven (7) hours of Undergraduate and/or Undergraduate Badge and Certficate programs
- $5,250 max dollar amount per calendar year for Graduate and/or Graduate Badges and
Certificate programs

There is no lifetime award limit for employees. Student fees or costs of books or
housing are not included in tuition assistance award amounts.

Back to Top

### Tuition Assistance Program for Spouses and Dependent Children

#### Eligibility

To be eligible for tuition assistance as the dependent child of an employee of WSU,
applicants (i.e., the student taking courses) must meet ALL of the following requirements
as of the first day of the term for which assistance is requested:

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
- Child, stepchild, or adopted child of the employee
- Under age 26
- Unmarried
- Admitted into any undergraduate or graduate degree-seeking program offered by WSU
- Overall grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 for undergraduate programs or 3.0 for graduate
programs

To be eligible for tuition assistance as the spouse of an employee of WSU, applicants
(i.e., the student taking courses) must meet ALL of the following requirements as
of the first day of the term for which assistance is requested:

- Legal spouse of the employee, as recognized under Kansas state law, including common
law
- Admitted into any undergraduate or graduate degree-seeking program offered by WSU
- Overall grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 for undergraduate programs or 3.0 for graduate
programs

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
In addition, the employee (spouse or parent of the applicant) must meet ALL of the
following requirements as of the first day of the term for which assistance is requested:

- Active appointment status as an Unclassified Professional (UP), University Support
Staff (USS), or member of Faculty (FA)
- Benefits-eligible (i.e. accrue sick/vacation leave)
- FTE status 0.5 or greater

#### Award

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
- The amount of tuition assistance provided for undergraduate courses will be limited
to 50% of the cost of resident tuition, up to a maximum of fifteen (15) credit hours
of courses per semester.
- The amount of tuition assistance provided for graduate courses is limited to 50% of
the cost of the resident tuition up to a maximum of $5,250 in tuition assistance per
calendar year.
- Tuition assistance will be limited to a maximum of sixty (60) cumulative credit hours
in the Spouse and/or Dependent Child’s academic career. Assistance is not available
for any student fees or for the cost of books or housing.
- The award is in additional to any financial aid received and will not exceed the cost
of attendance.

Back to Top

### Additional Program Information

#### Award Amounts

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
Tuition assistance will be paid at the base cost of graduate or undergraduate tuition
rates plus the infrastructure fee. **Students are responsible for any other course fees, including, but not limited to,
fees for online and lab courses or departmental/program fees.**

Any balance owed must be paid by the last day to drop a class at 100% to avoid late
fees. Unpaid fees will result in a financial hold placed on the student’s record which
will prevent viewing grades, transcripts, and future enrollment.

Courses that qualify for the Tuition Assistance Program include all undergraduate,
graduate, badge, and certificate program courses offered for credit by the University.

#### Enrollment

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
Students must register for classes on-line. Tuition assistance will be reflected on
the student's tuition bill only once the student has enrolled in courses. To ensure
proper application of tuition assistance awards, students should be enrolled in their
courses no later than the first day of the academic term.

Students must officially withdraw from a class for payments to be refunded.

#### Academic Eligibility

Employees must maintain an overall grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 for undergraduate
programs or an overall GPA of 3.0 for graduate programs, which will be reviewed after
final grades are entered for each completed term. Failure to meet this requirement
will make the Employee ineligible for tuition assistance until the Employee’s overall
GPA is greater than 2.0 for undergraduate programs or 3.0 for graduate programs.

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
The Spouse or Dependent Child must maintain an overall grade point average (GPA) of
2.0 for undergraduate programs or an overall GPA of 3.0 for graduate programs, which
will be reviewed after final grades are entered for each completed term. Failure to
meet this requirement will make the Spouse or Dependent Child ineligible for tuition
assistance until their overall GPA is restored to 2.0 or greater for undergraduate
programs and 3.0 or greater for graduate programs.

#### Tax Consequences

Employees are responsible for all tax consequences.  Tuition assistance for graduate
courses for an Employee’s spouse and dependents may be included in the Employee’s
gross income as wages and subject to income tax consistent with federal and state
tax laws.

#### Withdrawing from Classes

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
If a course(s) is withdrawn, it must be done before the Full-Refund Deadline for tuition
assistance funds to be applied appropriately. Withdrawing from courses paid for with
tuition assistance received under this policy may affect eligibility for future semesters
unless the recipient has demonstrated that extenuating circumstances caused the late
withdrawal.  A recipient seeking to preserve their eligibility under this policy may
petition the Tuition Refund Board of Appeals by submitting a Petition for Exception to Tuition Refund Policy for Dropping Courses to the Financial Operations and Business Technology Office by mail to Box 38, Wichita,
KS 67260; by email to wsuaccountsreceivable@wichita.edu , by facsimile to 316-978-3107; or by delivery to Jardine Hall, Room 201.

title: Tuition Assistance Program Policies
text:
For dependents and spouses, if a course(s) is withdrawn after the Full-Refund Deadline,
the funds disbursed will be applied to the credit-hour maximum even though the course(s)
have not been completed.

#### Availability of Funds

Tuition Assistance Awards are contingent on available funding.

Back to Top

---

### Who to Contact

**HR Total Rewards Team** **TuitionAssistance@wichita.edu**

title: WSU Academic Policies
text:
# WSU Academic Policies

## Attendance

Students must have satisfactory academic progress (SAP) to maintain financial aid
availability. Link to the Office of Financial Aid to review more information about
this topic.

## Cheating

A standard of academic honesty, fairly applied to all students, is essential to a
learning environment. Students who compromise the integrity of the classroom are subject
to disciplinary action by their instructor, their department, their college and/or
the University. Violations of classroom standards of academic honesty include, but
are not limited to:

title: WSU Academic Policies
text:
- Cheating in any form, whether in formal examinations or elsewhere.
- Using or submitting the work of others as one's own original work without assigning
proper credit to the source.
- Misrepresentation of any work done in or out of the classroom or in preparation for
class.
- Falsification, forgery or alteration of any documents pertaining to academic records.
- Colluding with others in an effort to obtain a grade or credit not truly reflective
of what the student knows or has learned.

title: WSU Academic Policies
text:
Students violating such standards must accept the consequences and appropriately assessed
penalties, which may include reprimand, a failing grade, or suspension or dismissal
from an academic program or the University. Students accused of abridging a standard
of academic honesty will be provided with mechanisms for review and appeal of decisions
regarding allegations of academic misconduct. Read more about Student Academic Honesty
in the WSU Policies and Procedures 2.17 / Student Academic Integrity .

## Campus Violence

title: WSU Academic Policies
text:
Students who want to report concerns about their personal safety, the personal safety
of a fellow student or any concern about a possible act of violence on campus should
notify a faculty member, the Chair of their Department, the Dean of their College,
a member of the Residence Life Staff, the Director of Student Conduct and Community
Standards, the University Behavior Intervention Team, the International Students Office,
the Office of Student Affairs, the Office of Academic Affairs, the University's General
Counsel, the University Police Department or local, state or federal law enforcement
authorities. Read more about WSU’s campus personal safety policy at WSU Policy and Procedures 8.18 / Eschewing Campus/Workplace Violence

## Discrimination

title: WSU Academic Policies
text:
WSU prohibits discrimination in educational programs and activities on the basis of
race, religion, color, national origin, gender, age, sexual orientation, marital status,
political affiliation, status as a veteran, genetic information or disability. Review
the university’s non-discrimination policy in WSU Policies and Procedures 3.06 / Sexual Harassment, Discrimination and Retaliation
for Employees, Students and Visitors .

## Sexual Harassment

title: WSU Academic Policies
text:
Wichita State University is committed to a community in which students, faculty and
staff can work in an atmosphere that is free of sexual harassment. Such behavior is
costly in human terms and it is prohibited by law and by University policy. The University
intends to prevent sexual harassment and to resolve student complaints of sexual harassment
according to the procedures found in WSU Policies and Procedures 3.06 / Sexual Harassment, Discrimination and Retaliation
for Employees, Students and Visitors .

## Retaliation

title: WSU Academic Policies
text:
Any University employee or student who engages in retaliatory conduct against a University
employee or student who has filed a complaint alleging discrimination or otherwise
exercised their rights and privileges against illegal discrimination will be subject
to disciplinary actions pursuant to established University procedures, up to and including
termination of employment or student status. See the procedures found in WSU Policies and Procedures 3.06 / Sexual Harassment, Discrimination and Retaliation
for Employees, Students and Visitors .

## Student Grievances

title: WSU Academic Policies
text:
Federal regulations require an institution of higher education to provide its students
and prospective students with contact information for filing complaints with the institution’s
accreditor and with the institution’s State approval or licensing entity. Review available
remedies and access forms at the Office of Financial Aid website .

## How to Change Apple ID

Instructions on how to change your Apple ID on your device to a different Apple ID.

### How to Sign Out of iCloud on your iPhone

1. Launch **Settings** on you iPhone or iPad.
2. Tap the **Apple ID banner** at the top of the screen.
3. Scroll to the bottom and tab **Sign Out**.
4. Tap **Sign out of iCloud** if you have different accounts for iCloud and the iTunes and App Stores.  Otherwise,
proceed to Step 5.
5. Enter your **password** for you iCloud Apple ID.
6. Tap **Turn Off**
7. **Toggle** the switch on for each data (Contacts and Calendar) that you want to keep on your
iPhone.
8. Tap **Sign Out**.
9. Tap **Sign Out** to confirm that you want to sign out of your iCloud account.

### Sign In on your iPhone, iPad

title: Retiree FAQ - Changing Apple ID

2. Tap **Sign in** to your device.
3. **Enter** your Apple ID and password
4. If prompted, enter the six-digit verification code sent to your trusted device or
phone number and complete sign in.

# ITS Retirement Policies FAQs

## ITS Retirement FAQs

List of Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding what you need to know from Information
Technology Services (ITS) when you retire.

Can I have access to Office 365?

As of May 2023, new Retirees are not eligible for an Office 365 license.

Previous Retirees who have not used or logged into Office 365 for more than 18 months
are not eligible fore reactivation of Office 365.

What do I do with my WSU issued technology devices?

Prior to leaving WSU, please return all WSU provided technology devices to your supervisor
per departmental policy.

*Contact your supervisor for details.*

What happens to my contacts, emails. and calendars from my WSU email account when
I retire?

All contents from the @wichita.edu email address will be disabled when the employee
retires and/or leaves Wichita State.

title: ITS Retirement Policies FAQs
text:
If the retiring employee will need a WSU affiliated email address, they need contact
the Help Desk to request to be transitioned to an @shockers.wichita.edu email address
at retirement.

*As per WSU policy, ITS will **not** be able to transfer contents (including saved emails, contacts, notes, and calendar
events) from @wichita.edu to @shockers.wichita.edu mail accounts.*

*To avoid losing iPhone contacts, **click here for instructions** to guide you through how to save these contacts to your device.*

***Reminder**: Once your @wichita.edu email account is disabled, the @wichita.edu email account
(including emails, contacts, notes, and calendars associated with that email account)
**will be disabled on all your devices** including mobile devices such as cell phones.*

How do I Check Email Online?

Click here for instruction on how to access the @shockers.wichita.edu email online.

title: ITS Retirement Policies FAQs
text:
How do I tranfer Microsoft Teams Ownership?

If you are the owner of a Team in Microsoft Teams, you will need to transfer that
ownership to another WSU employee prior to retirement.

For instructions on how to transfer ownership, click here .

How do I create a Personal Email Account?

If your WSU email address (@wichita.edu) is the only email account that you have,
a personal email account may be required for your mobile devices.

One option would be to create a Gmail account.  Click here for instructions on How to Create Gmail Account .

How do I change my Apple ID on Apple Device?

If your WSU email address (@wichita.edu) is listed as your Apple ID on your Apple
devices, you will need to change it to a person email account.

How do I create a new Apple ID with my person email account?

title: ITS Retirement Policies FAQs
text:
An Apple ID is the account you use to access Apple services like iCloud, the App Store,
the iTunes Store, Apple Music, and more. It includes the email address and password
that you use to sign in, and all the contact, payment, and security details that you'll
use across Apple services.

Click here for instructions on How to Create a New Apple ID .

How do I change my Apple ID to my personal email account?

Click here for instructions on How to Change your Apple ID on your Device to a different Apple ID.

How do I back up iPhone to iCloud?

If you back up your iPhone, iPad, or iPod touch, you’ll have a copy of your information
to use in case your device is ever replaced, lost, or damaged.

Click here for instructions on How to Back up iPhone to iCloud .

How do I restore for iCloud to iPhone?

You can restore your iPhone, iPad, or iPod touch from an iCloud backup

title: ITS Retirement Policies FAQs
text:
Click here to learn how to restore your device from a backup in iCloud or on your computer.

How do I set my WSU Email on a mobile device?

Click here for instructions on How to Setup WSU Email on a Mobile Device

How do I change my password?

Click here for instructions on how to manage or change your WSU ID password.

Can ITS help me setup my home PC?

ITS **cannot** help set up any home devices.

What happens if I come back to WSU?

If you come back to WSU, you will be issued and @wichita.edu address. Emails that
go to your @shockers.wichita.edu will be sent to your @wichita.edu address as so you
will not loose messages. When you leave your role, your mailbox will be empty and
your @shockers.wichita.edu address will still continue to function.

Can I request for extending the availability of my mailbox beyond my retirment time?

title: ITS Retirement Policies FAQs
