title: Catalog (CAT) User Guide
text:
# Catalog (CAT) User Guide

# How to Edit and Approve Catalog (CAT) Pages

This is for reviewers who need to edit and approve the WSU catalog pages during the
annual review process.

## Accessing the Dashboard

Using any web browser except Internet Explorer, go to the CourseLeaf (CAT, CIM, CLSS)
Resources page ( https://wichita.edu/courseleaf ) and click the ***CourseLeaf Dashboard*** button link:

## Your Approval Queue: The Workflow Tab

When the CourseLeaf Dashboard window opens, pages in your queue will not be immediately
visible. This is due to the dashboard defaulting to the ***Items*** tab. You will need to click on the ***Workflow*** tab to view your queue.

title: Catalog (CAT) User Guide
text:
The ***Workflow*** tab will automatically filter for your role. If you have multiple roles in the CourseLeaf
system (CAT, CIM, CLSS), then all of your roles will be selected and any items in
those queues will appear in the list (note the different role names in the Approver
column).

***Please Note:** If there are no items for you to approve, then nothing will appear under the **Workflow** tab.*

To filter only for a specific role, leave the role you want to view alone and click
on the ***X*** by any of the role names in the grey bubbles to remove that role.

To add back any of the roles, search for it under the Role drop-down list, and click
on the role you wish to view. Only roles with something in the queue will appear in
the drop-down.

title: Catalog (CAT) User Guide
text:
Items can also be filtered by type and term. Use the ***Type*** filter to view only programs, courses, catalog pages, or schedule items. Use the
***Term*** filter to view items with a specific effective term.

***Please Note:** Any filters selected are added to the filters already applied.* You will need to click on the ***X*** of any filter you wish to remove. The system will not automatically remove any filters.

## Reviewing Pages

Click on any of the catalog pages to view it.  A preview screen will pop up with the
page:

Red text with a line through it indicates current information that someone is proposing
to have removed or changed on the page.  The green text indicates new information
being proposed.

## Editing Pages

If you need to make edits, click the ***Edit*** button in the top banner. A beige-colored editing toolbar will drop down.

title: Catalog (CAT) User Guide
text:
The ***pencil icons*** on the toolbar represent tabs that have been built for the page. Most likely, the
information you will need to edit can be accessed by clicking the ***Page Body*** pencil icon. If doing that opens an empty window, click cancel to shut the editing
window and click on one of the other pencil icons.

The titles next to each pencil icon correlate with the title on the page tab. The
only exception is the “Overview” tab which always correlates to the Page Body pencil
icon.

To edit the information on the page, click on the pencil icon you need to open the
***Editing Window***. The title of the tab you are editing will appear in the top left corner.

The ***Editing Window*** utilizes many of the same formatting controls you would find on any standard document
editor.

title: Catalog (CAT) User Guide
text:
Once you have finished editing the page, click the ***Save Icon*** first to save your changes and then click the ***green OK button***.

## Tables

If the catalog page has information in a table, the existing table will have a ***blue border*** in the Editing Window. Double clicking anywhere inside the table will open the table
editor.

## Program Information on CAT Pages

If the catalog page you are editing has program information, the text will appear
in a ***grey box***. *This information cannot be edited from the CAT page.* Only the most recently approved version of the program will be displayed. You will
be able to see the date of that last program approval.

title: Catalog (CAT) User Guide
text:
If any program information in the grey box needs to be updated, the program will need
to be edited in CIM Program Management and sent through workflow for approval. If a proposal is already in CIM to update
the program, then once that proposal is fully approved, the CAT page will automatically
be updated with that information. To learn how to edit a program in CIM, visit the
CIM User Guides page .

You do not need to hold program CAT pages to ensure the information gets updated later.
As long as the CIM proposal reaches the end of workflow before the catalog deadline,
the CAT page will be automatically updated. The catalog will also be sent out for
a final review before publication at which point, you can verify that the program
information was properly updated as well. See the Catalog Production Schedule for program change deadlines.

## Approving CAT Pages

title: Catalog (CAT) User Guide
text:
Once you have finished editing and are ready to approve the page, click the green
***Approve*** button in the top right of the page ***Preview Screen***:

If you’d like to confirm that this page has left your queue and has moved on to the
next approval step in workflow, you can refresh the Dashboard, re-select the ***Workflow***tab, and confirm that this page is no longer showing in the ***Pages Pending Approval*** section.

***Please Note:** Refreshing the Dashboard will reset the filters under the **Workflow** tab.*

## Rolling Back CAT Pages

If you need to send the page back to the person that submitted it or anyone in a prior
workflow approval step for edits before approving it, you can click the red ***Rollback*** button:

title: Catalog (CAT) User Guide
text:
A new window will appear on the right side of the page ***Preview Screen*** allowing you to select whom you would like to roll the page back to.  You can select
any previous approver in the workflow or the initiator of the page.  You are also
required to provide a comment/reason for the rollback:

**Please Note:**

- The first person in the rollback list is the ‘initiator’ who submitted the page to
workflow initially. Rolling a page back to this person will roll the page completely
out of workflow and it will need to be resubmitted to workflow once any necessary
edits are made.
- Whomever you choose to roll it back to will need to make the necessary edits and then
all subsequent approvers in the list, who have already approved the page, will have
to reapprove it with these new edits.

## Additional Features in the Preview Screen

### PRINT the Page:

Click on the printer icon:

title: Catalog (CAT) User Guide
text:
### HIDE the Current Information:

Click the drop-down next to the ***Filter by*** field. Select ***Hide Changes*** so the page only shows the proposed information.  This eliminates the current information
in red strikethrough from showing.  The new proposed information will still show but
it won’t be in green.  To view the red/green markup once again, select ***All Changes*** from the same drop-down.

### View Changes by a Specific Person:

Click the drop-down next to the ***Filter by*** field to select someone:

title: Editing a Plan of Study Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
# Editing a Plan of Study Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program

# Editing a Plan of Study Table in a CIM Program

## Accessing the Dashboard

Using any web browser except Internet Explorer, go to the **CourseLeaf (CAT, CIM, CLSS) Resources page** ( https://wichita.edu/courseleaf ) and click the gold ***CourseLeaf Dashboard*** button link:

## Accessing Program Management

Once in the Dashboard, click on the Program Management (CIM) Module Card to be taken
to the Program Management system.

## Editing a Plan of Study Table Steps

### Step 1: Search for the Program to Edit

In the **Program Management** system there are various ways that you can search for the program you want to edit. 
You can type in the program number or use the asterisk as a wildcard to search for
words in the Program Name:

title: Editing a Plan of Study Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
Click on the program that you want to edit to select it.  Then click the green **‘Edit Program’** button:

### Step 2: Opening Plan of Study Table Editor

A new window will open displaying the current values of each field for this program.
Scroll down to the ‘Admissions’ or ‘Requirements’ area that contains the table you
want to edit.  The table is outlined in **blue**.  Double-click anywhere within the blue outline to open the **Plan of Study table editor**. The editor will show all of the courses currently in the table on the right-hand
side.

Use the drop-down areas next to the **‘Year’** and **‘Term’** fields to change to the area you want to edit:

### Step 3: Removing Courses

To **remove** a course from the table, select the course in the right-hand box that you want to
remove and then click on the **left-pointing arrows**:

### Step 4: Adding Courses

title: Editing a Plan of Study Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
There are two ways to add courses to your table:

**Option 1:**  Use the drop-down arrows on the left-hand side of the editor. You can search by
college and subject to find a list of all available courses. Select the course you
wish to add and then click on the right-pointing arrows:

This will move the selected course (SCWK 840M) into the right-hand box.

***Please Note:**  inactivated courses or new courses that haven’t been fully approved in workflow will
not be found in the list of available courses. In order to add these courses to your
table, you must use the **‘Quick Add’** feature illustrated in Option 2 below.*

title: Editing a Plan of Study Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
**Option 2:**  The **‘Quick Add’** field allows you to manually type in the course you want to add without searching
for them. Type in the subject code and number of the course you want to add, and then
click on the **‘Add Course’** button. The subject code must be typed in all caps, and there must be a space before
the number for the system to recognize the course. Do not type in the course title
in the ‘Quick Add’ box.

***Please Note:** If you are adding a new course that is going through workflow for approval, you can
add it to your table with the Quick Add feature. The course will appear as “Course
Not Found” in your table.  However, once the course is fully approved and out of workflow,
the table will automatically fill in the correct information.*

### Step 5: Adding Comments

title: Editing a Plan of Study Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
To add a comment on its own line or header to your course list, use the **‘Add Comment Entry’** button located in the bottom left corner of the table editor.

Comments can also be used to add lines about requirements such as how many electives
to select from a list or a certain type of elective course that students need to select.

With these comments, credit hours can be added by typing in the **‘Hours’** field. These hours will then be added to the **Credit Hour column** of the course table.

### Step 6: Moving Text and Courses

To move text and/or courses around in your table, select the item in the right-hand
box that you want moved and then use the **‘Move Up’** and **‘Move Down’** buttons:

### Step 7: Additional Features

The items on the bottom right side of the table editor are additional features that
you can perform to the course you select in the box above:

title: Editing a Plan of Study Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
**Comment** – add parenthetical text that will appear next to the selected course. (This field
displays differently than when you use the ‘Add Comment Entry’ button located in the
lower left of the table editor window.)

Displays like this in catalog:

**Sequence** – list other courses that must be taken with or in addition to the selected course
(creates an ‘&’ situation: PHYS 313 & PHYS 315)

Displays like this in catalog:

**Or Class** – list alternative course(s) to the selected course (creates an ‘OR’ situation: ARTS
283 OR ARTS 245)

Displays like this in the catalog:

**Hours** – this field will automatically be populated with the credit hours of the selected
course; you can change this number if necessary (i.e. a repeatable course such as
a thesis course needs to be taken multiple times for a total of 8 credit hours)

title: Editing a Plan of Study Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
**Footnote** – if you need to reference a footnote, add the footnote number here

Displays like this in catalog:

**Override Sum** - You can override the sum of the table credit hours by typing in the total required
credit hours.

### Step 8: Finishing Table Edits

When you are done making all of your desired changes, make sure to click on the green
**‘OK’** button to save the changes to the Plan of Study Grid table:

If you need to go back and edit the table, **double click** anywhere inside the inserted table that is outlined in blue.

### Step 9: Submit to Workflow

title: Editing a Plan of Study Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
Continue making any other necessary changes to the program form.  When you are ready
to submit the proposal to the electronic workflow, click the green **'Start Workflow'** button.  If you need to save your work and come back at another time, click on the
gray **'Save Changes'** button and then edit this program again later.

title: Cross-listing Scenarios in CIM - Summarized
text:
# Cross-listing Scenarios in CIM - Summarized

# Cross-Listing Courses in CIM

Cross-listed courses are defined as two or more active courses marked equivalent to
each other in Banner. To be edited using a single curriculum change form in CIM, nearly
all aspects of the courses must be the same – title, description, prerequisites, etc.
If the departments do not agree on these common factors, each course will have to
be maintained using a separate CIM form. Courses can be cross-listed in the schedule
(taught together) and not be cross-listed in CIM.

Each cross-listed pair or group must have a primary course; this is normally the course
subject within the department teaching the course.

**The following describes the actions that would involve cross-listed courses and the
steps for each within the CIM system. These apply to courses that are cross-listed
in CIM.**

title: Cross-listing Scenarios in CIM - Summarized
text:
## Creating two (or more) new courses that will be cross-listed (a SINGLE CIM form):

- Click ***Propose New Course*** and enter the primary course information in the ***Subject*** and ***Course Number*** fields.
- Locate the ***Cross-Listed*** *field further down in the form and **Add*** the secondary course(s) information using the drop-down menus.
- Complete all required fields on the proposal.
- Click ***Start Workflow***.
- Once approved, both/all courses are created in CIM and Banner with identical information.
- For step-by-step instructions, see Creating a New Course and a New Cross-Listed Course .

## Creating two (or more) new courses that will be cross-listed in schedule but are not identical:

title: Cross-listing Scenarios in CIM - Summarized
text:
- Requires two CIM forms.
- Click ***Propose New Course*** for each course separately.
- Note in the ***Describe/Justify*** box of each proposal that the courses are equivalent and will be taught together
but won’t use single CIM form.
- Complete all required fields on each proposal.
- Click ***Start Workflow*** on each.

## Creating a new course(s) to cross-list with existing course:

title: Cross-listing Scenarios in CIM - Summarized
text:
- ***Edit*** existing course (it will be primary to start). **Do not** propose a new course.
- In the proposal of the existing course, locate the ***Cross-List*** *field and **Add*** the information of the new course number(s) using the drop-down menus.
- If new course is to be the primary, click the ***Make Primary*** *link in the **Cross-List***area once the new course is visible there.
- Complete all required fields.
- Click ***Start Workflow***.
- For step-by-step instructions, see Creating a New Cross-listed Course from an Existing Course .

## Removing the cross-list and inactivating one of the courses:

title: Cross-listing Scenarios in CIM - Summarized
text:
- Search for one of the cross-listed courses and select ***Edit***.
- **Ensure** that the course to be inactivated is **NOT** the primary course; if necessary, make it the non-primary course by toggling ***Make Primary*** in the ***Cross-List*** area.
- Once the course to be inactivated is listed in the ***Cross-List*** field, click the ***Remove*** link (this will inactivate the non-primary course).
- Complete all required fields.
- Click ***Start Workflow***.
- For step-by-step instructions, see Inactivating the Primary Cross-Listed Course or Inactivating a Secondary Cross-Listed Course .

## Inactivating both/all courses in a cross-list pair/group:

- Search for primary course.
- Select red Inactivate button.
- Provide effective term and justification.
- Both/all courses will be inactivated.

## Contact Sally Fiscus in the Registrar’s Office To:

title: Cross-listing Scenarios in CIM - Summarized
text:
- Cross-list two or more courses that already exist on the course file.
- Remove cross-listing and keep both courses active,.

## REMEMBER:

Cross-list in CIM means equivalent in Banner and all (with few exceptions) information
about the two courses is the same – one CIM form.

Courses can be equivalent in Banner but not cross-listed in CIM…in this case, each
course would have its own CIM form.

title: Reactivating an Inactive Course in CIM
text:
# Reactivating an Inactive Course in CIM

# Reactivating an Inactive Course

This is for when you want to reactivate a currently inactive course so that it may
be offered on the schedule of courses again.

## Accessing the Dashboard

Using any web browser except Internet Explorer, go to the **CourseLeaf (CAT, CIM, CLSS) Resources page** ( https://wichita.edu/courseleaf ) and click the gold ***CourseLeaf Dashboard*** button link:

**Accessing Course Inventory Management**

Once in the Dashboard, click on the Course Management (CIM) Module Card to be taken
to the Course Inventory Management system.

## Reactivating an Inactive Course Steps

### Step 1: Finding Course to Reactivate

title: Reactivating an Inactive Course in CIM
text:
In the Course Inventory Management system, search for the course you want to reactivate.
In the search field, type in the subject and number of the course (i.e. BADM 201)
or you can search by the course title. You can also use asterisks to search for all
courses that contain specific words in the course code or title.

 
Once you have found the course you wish to reactivate, click on the green ***Reactivate*** button. This will open a separate window for the course reactivation proposal.

### Step 2: Contact and Action Information

Fill out the contact information with the faculty member that can answer questions
about this course.  (Administrative assistants may be the one creating the proposal
but the faculty member that requested this should be listed as the contact person.)

title: Reactivating an Inactive Course in CIM
text:
Check the ***Other***option under applicable actions and type in ***Reactivating course***.  If you are planning on making additional changes to the course (i.e. updating the
course description, title, prerequisites), check those options as well.

**Helpful Information as you move through the form:**

title: Reactivating an Inactive Course in CIM
text:
- Answers provided on this form affect the electronic workflow approval process.  For
example, checking the box for ‘New Course’ starts a different workflow than checking
the box for ‘New Letter under Approved Root Course’.  In addition, the workflow is
constantly changing as you specify/change information.  For example, selecting ‘Yes’
for ‘Does this course have a service-learning component’ adds the Service-Learning
Coordinator to the approval process.
- Now that you are inside the proposal form the blue question marks represent WSU-specific
help:
- If you start a proposal but can’t finish it right now simply scroll to the bottom
of the form and click the ***Save Changes*** button.  When you are ready to return to this proposal you can use the same links
as above to access CIM.  Then, search for the course, select it, and click the ***Edit Course*** button:

title: Reactivating an Inactive Course in CIM
text:
### Step 3: Course Information

**Effective Term** – You will need to select an effective term for this reactivation.

Most of the required fields on the form should already be filled out on the proposal.
**Review all of the information and make any edits as needed.**

The **Justification and Resources** section will not be filled out. And so, you will need to explain why the course is
being reactivated and answer the questions as to how reactivating this course may
affect other departments/colleges, faculty, and/or resources. Also, if any letter(s)
of support are needed, attach them here.

title: Reactivating an Inactive Course in CIM
text:
You will also need to attach an updated syllabus that follows the standard syllabus template .  **Please Note:** The question concerning UG and GR level expectations will only appear on the form
if the course number is 500-699. The Terminal course question will only appear on
the form if the proposed course number is 500+.

### Step 4: Start Workflow

Once you have reviewed, updated, and filled out the entire course proposal form, you
will want to start the proposal through the electronic workflow approval process by

a lettered course) and make it a permanent course.

## Accessing the Dashboard

to the Course Inventory Management system.

## Creating a Permanent Course from an Eperimental Course Steps

### Step 1: Finding Course to Edit

title: Creating a Permanent Course From an Experimental or Special Topics Course in CIM
text:
In the Course Inventory Management system, search for the experimental course you
want to make permanent. In the search field, type in the subject and number of the
course (i.e. AE 460A) or you can search by the course title. You can use asterisks
to search for all courses that contain specific words in the course code or title.

 
Once you have found the course you wish to edit, click on it to select it and then
click on the green **‘Edit Course’** button. This will open a separate window for the course proposal.

### Step 2: Contact and Action Information

Fill out the contact information with the faculty member that can answer questions
about this course.  (Administrative assistants may be the one creating the proposal
but the faculty member that requested this should be listed as the contact person.)

title: Creating a Permanent Course From an Experimental or Special Topics Course in CIM
text:
Check the **‘Experimental course seeking course status’** option AND the **‘Change in course number’** option under applicable actions:

***Please Note:** If the experimental course you are editing is listed on any programs and/or as a
prerequisite for another course, then those programs and/or courses will need to be
updated to reflect the new permanent course number and submitted to workflow as well.*

***Helpful Information as you move through the form:***

title: Creating a Permanent Course From an Experimental or Special Topics Course in CIM
text:
- Answers provided on this form affect the electronic workflow approval process.  For
example, checking the box for ‘New Course’ starts a different workflow than checking
the box for ‘New Letter under Approved Root Course’.  In addition, the workflow is
constantly changing as you specify/change information.  For example, selecting ‘Yes’
for ‘Does this course have a service-learning component’ adds the Service-Learning
Coordinator to the approval process.
- Now that you are inside the proposal form the blue question marks represent WSU-specific
help:
- If you start a proposal but can’t finish it right now simply scroll to the bottom
of the form and click the **‘Save Changes’** button.  When you are ready to return to this proposal you can use the same links
as above to access CIM.  Then, search for the course, select it, and click the **‘Edit Course’** button:

title: Creating a Permanent Course From an Experimental or Special Topics Course in CIM
text:
### Step 3: Course Information

**Effective Term** – Select a term for the change in course numbers.  ***Please Note:** Course changes can only be made for future terms where sections of the course do
not already exist.*

To make the course a permanent course, you will need to enter a new **Course Number**. You cannot simply remove the letter from the number.

If you do not know what course numbers are available, click on the grey **‘Course Numbers in Use’** button after you fill in the **Subject** field.

title: Creating a Permanent Course From an Experimental or Special Topics Course in CIM
text:

title: Creating a Permanent Course From an Experimental or Special Topics Course in CIM
text:

title: Editing a Course List Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
# Editing a Course List Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program

# Editing a Course List Table

## Accessing the Dashboard

Using any web browser except Internet Explorer, go to the **CourseLeaf (CAT, CIM, CLSS) Resources page** ( https://wichita.edu/courseleaf ) and click the gold ***CourseLeaf Dashboard*** button link:

## Accessing Program Management

Once in the Dashboard, click on the Program Management (CIM) Module Card to be taken
to the Program Management system.

## Editing a Course List Table Steps

### Step 1: Search for the Program to Edit

In the **Program Management** system there are various ways that you can search for the program you want to edit. 
You can type in the program number or use the asterisk as a wildcard to search for
words in the Program Name:

title: Editing a Course List Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
Click on the program that you want to edit to select it.  Then click the green **‘Edit Program’** button:

### Step 2: Opening Course List Table Editor

A new window will open displaying the current values of each field for this program.
Scroll down to the ‘Admissions’ or ‘Requirements’ area that contains the table you
want to edit.  The table is outlined in **blue**.  Double-click anywhere within the blue outline to open the **Course List table editor**. The editor will show all of the courses currently in the table on the right-hand
side.

### Step 3: Removing Courses

To **remove** a course from the table, select the course in the right-hand box that you want to
remove and then click on the **left-pointing arrows**:

### Step 4: Adding Courses

There are two ways to add courses to your table:

title: Editing a Course List Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
**Option 1:**  Use the drop-down arrows on the left-hand side of the editor. You can search by
college and subject to find a list of all available courses. Select the course you
wish to add and then click on the right-pointing arrows:

This will move the selected course (PHIL 321) into the right-hand box. You can then
use the ‘**Move Up**’ or ‘**Move Down**’ button to position this course within the other required courses:

***Please Note:**  inactivated courses or new courses that haven’t been fully approved in workflow will
not be found in the list of available courses. In order to add these courses to your
table, you must use the **‘Quick Add’** feature illustrated in Option 2 below.*

title: Editing a Course List Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
**Option 2:**  The **‘Quick Add’** field allows you to manually type in the course you want to add without searching
for them. Type in the subject code and number of the course you want to add, and then
click on the **‘Add Course’** button. The subject code must be typed in all caps, and there must be a space before
the number for the system to recognize the course. Do not type in the course title
in the ‘Quick Add’ box.

***Please Note:** If you are adding a new course that is going through workflow for approval, you can
add it to your table with the Quick Add feature. The course will appear as “Course
Not Found” in your table.  However, once the course is fully approved and out of workflow,
the table will automatically fill in the correct information.*

### Step 5: Adding Comments

title: Editing a Course List Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
To add a comment on its own line or header to your course list, use the **‘Add Comment Entry’** button located in the bottom left corner of the table editor.

Once your comment is showing in the right-hand list of requirements, you can use the
**‘Move Up**’ or ‘**Move Down**’ button to position it where you want and the ‘**Area Header**’ or ‘**Area Subheader**’ checkboxes to format how it is displayed:

Comments can also be used to add lines about requirements such as how many electives
to select from a list or a certain type of elective course that students need to select.

With these comments, credit hours can be added by typing in the ‘Hours’ field. These
hours will then be added to the Credit Hour column of the course table.

### Step 6: Moving Text and Courses

title: Editing a Course List Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
To move text and/or courses around in your table, select the item in the right-hand
box that you want moved and then use the **‘Move Up’** and **‘Move Down’** buttons:

### Step 7: Additional Features

The items on the bottom right side of the table editor are additional features that
you can perform to the course you select in the box above:

**Comment** – add parenthetical text that will appear next to the selected course. (This field
displays differently than when you use the ‘Add Comment Entry’ button located in the
lower left of the table editor window.)

Displays like this in catalog:

**Sequence** – list other courses that must be taken with or in addition to the selected course
(creates an ‘&’ situation: PHYS 313 & PHYS 315)

Displays like this in catalog:

title: Editing a Course List Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
**Cross Reference** – if the selected course is cross-listed with another course, you can list the other
cross-listed course here (i.e. AC 346/CS 346)

Displays like this in the catalog:

**Or Class** – list alternative course(s) to the selected course (creates an ‘OR’ situation: ARTS
283 OR ARTS 245)

Displays like this in the catalog:

**Hours** – this field will automatically be populated with the credit hours of the selected
course; you can change this number if necessary (i.e. a repeatable course such as
a thesis course needs to be taken multiple times for a total of 8 credit hours)

**Footnote** – if you need to reference a footnote, add the footnote number here

Displays like this in catalog:

title: Editing a Course List Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
**Indent** – check this to indent the course/comment in the table; for indented courses, their
credit hours will no longer show in the table (this is typically used when listing
possible elective options students can choose from)

Displays like this in catalog:

### Step 8: Sum Hours

You can choose for your course table to show the total number of credit hours by checking
**‘Sum Hours’** located in the top right corner of the table editor.

Displays like this in catalog:

You can also override the sum by typing in the total required credit hours.

### Step 9: Finishing Table Edits

When you are done making the necessary changes, make sure to click on the green **‘Ok’** button to save the changes to the Course List table:

If you need to go back and edit the table, **double click** anywhere inside the inserted table that is outlined in blue.

### Step 10: Submit to Workflow

title: Editing a Course List Table in Admissions or Requirements Area of a CIM Program
text:
Make any other desired changes to the program and then scroll to the bottom of the
proposal and click on the green **'Start Workflow'** button to submit this proposal to the electronic workflow process. If you need to
save your work and come back at another time, click on the gray **'Save Changes'** button and then edit this program later.

title: Finding a Course Proposal in a CIM Workflow
text:
# Finding a Course Proposal in a CIM Workflow

# Finding a COURSE Proposal in Workflow

Use this guide to learn how to find a specific course proposal in the CIM workflow.

## Accessing the Dashboard

Using any web browser except Internet Explorer, go to the **CourseLeaf (CAT, CIM, CLSS) Resources page** ( https://wichita.edu/courseleaf ) and click the gold ***CourseLeaf Dashboard*** button link:

## Accessing Course Inventory Management

Once in the Dashboard, click on the Course Management (CIM) Module Card to be taken
to the Course Inventory Management system.

## Searching for a Course Proposal

In the Course Inventory Management system, search for the course by putting the course
subject and number in the search field and then clicking the green ‘**Search**’ button:

title: Finding a Course Proposal in a CIM Workflow
text:
The search results appear and the ‘**Workflow**’ column will show the step that this course proposal is currently at in workflow:

If you scroll down, you can see all of the approval steps in workflow that have been
completed (green) and those that are upcoming (gray).  The approval step that this
proposal is currently at in workflow is shown again here in orange:

Below the ‘**In Workflow’** information, you can see the date and time when each completed approval step occurred
by looking at the ‘**Approval Path**’ information.  In this example, you can see that the approval for the **BA UG College Program Committee Chair** was done on December 2, 2025 at 11:22 am by John Perry:

The proposal moved to the **BA Dean** step at the time of this approval.

## Finding Course Proposal You Initiated/Submitted

title: Finding a Course Proposal in a CIM Workflow
text:
If you are the one who initially submitted the course to workflow, you can also track
the progress of the proposal directly from the **Dashboard**.

When in the Dashboard, look at the **Snapshot (aka “thermometer”)** under the **Items tab**. It will initially display items that are the **Done** status.

Clicking on the **Pending** section of the thermometer will change the list to proposals you submitted to workflow.

The **Current User(s)** column shows you at which step of workflow the proposal is.

Clicking on any of the proposals in the list will take you to view the proposal in
**Course Inventory Management**. At that point, you can find all of the additional information described in the previous
section of this guide.

text:
# Creating a New Course and a New Cross-list Course in CIM

# Creating a NEW Course and a NEW Cross-listed Course

cross-listed course that will require two new course numbers to be created.

## Accessing the Dashboard

Using any web browser except Internet Explorer, go to the **CourseLeaf (CAT, CIM, CLSS) Resources page** ( https://wichita.edu/courseleaf ) and click the gold ***CourseLeaf Dashboard*** button link:

## Accessing Course Inventory Management

## Creating a New Course and Cross-Listed Course Steps

### Step 1: Opening New Proposal Form

In the Course Inventory Management system, click on the green **‘Propose New Course’** button:

A new course proposal form will open.

title: Creating a New Course and a New Cross-list Course in CIM
text:
### Step 2: Contact and Action Information

Fill out the contact information with the faculty member that can answer questions
about this course.  (Administrative assistants may be the one creating the proposal
but the faculty member that requested this should be listed as the contact person.)

Check the **‘New course’** and **'Other'** option under applicable actions and fill in the **'Please describe'** box:

***Helpful Information as you move through the form:***

title: Creating a New Course and a New Cross-list Course in CIM
text:
- Answers provided on this form affect the electronic workflow approval process.  For
example, checking the box for ‘New Course’ starts a different workflow than checking
the box for ‘New Letter under Approved Root Course’.  In addition, the workflow is
constantly changing as you specify/change information.  For example, selecting ‘Yes’
for ‘Does this course have a service-learning component’ adds the Service-Learning

- Now that you are inside the proposal form the blue question marks represent WSU-specific
help:
- If you start a proposal but can’t finish it right now simply scroll to the bottom
of the form and click the **‘Save Changes’** button.  When you are ready to return to this proposal you can use the same links
as above to access CIM.  Then, search for the course, select it, and click the **‘Edit Course’** button:

title: Creating a New Course and a New Cross-list Course in CIM
text:
### Step 3: Course Information

**Effective Term** - New courses can be given any effective term that is not a past term. ***Please note:**  If the term selected is over or close to over once the course proposal reaches the
end of workflow, then the effective term will be moved to the next term by the Registrar’s
Office.*

**Course Number** - If you do not know what course numbers are available, click on the grey **‘Course Numbers in Use’** button after you fill in the **Subject**field:

Or fill in the **Course Number** field with the number of the desired course level (1, 2, 3, etc.) and then add x’s
after that. For example, type in 3XX if you are wanting to create a 300-level course.
 ***Please Note:** If you are proposing an Honors course, an ‘H’ will need to be added to the end of
the course number.*

title: Creating a New Course and a New Cross-list Course in CIM
text:
Make sure to fill out all of the required information for the course.  Red fields
are required fields.

You are responsible for filling out the three boxes related to credit hour: **Credit Hour Limit, Lecture Hours** and **Lab Hours**.

**Credit Hour Limit** is the number of hours for which a course can be offered. Please use whole numbers
only (3, not 3.0), unless you are proposing a half credit hour course (.5). If the
course has a credit hour range, enter with dash (1-6).

**Lecture Hours** will be the same as Credit Hour Limit unless the course is Lab only.

If Lecture carries the credit, **Lab Hours** will be 0. If Lab carries the credit, Lecture Hours will be 0.

title: Creating a New Course and a New Cross-list Course in CIM
text:
The **Repeatable for credit** question will automatically be marked as ‘No’.  However, if the new course is repeatable
for credit, toggle this answer over to ‘Yes’.  ***Note:** all courses can be repeated for grade replacement.  This question relates to if this
course be taken more than once for credit.*

If there is a limit to the number of times that the course can be repeated for credit,
check the **Limit**box and fill in the **Limit**field with the total credit hours that a student can earn by repeating the course.

If there is no limit, check the **No Limit** box.

Select all of the appropriate items for **Grading Mode, Planned Delivery Method**, and **Course Format**. More than one answer can be selected for **Planned Delivery Method**. Only select one answer for **Course Format**.

title: Creating a New Course and a New Cross-list Course in CIM
text:
A **Catalog Description** (aka course description) is required for every course. This description must be in
third-person, present tense and no longer than one paragraph. Do not include text
for general education, cross-listing, prerequisites, or corequisites. The system will
add this information to the description when it syncs with Banner based on what you
have in other fields on the form.

If the course requires a **Prerequisite, Prerequisite with Concurrency**, or **Corequisite**, fill out the appropriate box.

If applicable, list any **Restrictions**with the course. Examples of restrictions include: course limited to specific major,
course limited to specific class (freshman, sophomore, etc.), course limited to specific
college, etc.

title: Creating a New Course and a New Cross-list Course in CIM
text:
The questions for **service-learning** and **capstone**will automatically be marked as ‘No’. If the course does contain service-learning
or is a capstone course, toggle the answer over to ‘Yes’. ***Note**: additional fields will open and need to be filled out for the service-learning component.*

### Step 4: Adding a Cross-List Course

To add a **Cross-List** to your course, click on **‘Add’**. A box will open which will allow you to select subject, number, division, and general
education category (if applicable):

For the cross-listed course, you have to enter three pieces of information:

title: Creating a New Course and a New Cross-list Course in CIM
text:
1. Select a Subject for the cross-list from the drop-down box.
2. Enter in the course number in the TBD box. Use the same number as the primary course,
when possible.
3. Select the Division for the cross-list from the drop-down box. The Division may differ
from that of the primary course depending on the Subject of the secondary course.

If the primary course is a General Education course, then go ahead and select the
General Education Category for the cross-list as well. However, if the primary course
is not General Education, then leave the General Education Category on the cross-list
blank.

***Note:** You cannot have the primary course be General Education and the cross-list course
not be General Education and vice versa. Either both courses are General Education
or neither of them are.*

title: Creating a New Course and a New Cross-list Course in CIM
text:
Once you have filled out the necessary information on the window, click on the green
“OK” button. If you want to add more than one cross-list course, follow the same steps
again.

### Step 5: Remaining Course Proposal Information

If this course is meant to replace another, select ‘Yes’.

You will be asked to enter the course that is being replaced and whether or not the
two courses are equivalent. ***Please note:** if the courses are equivalent, then check with the Registrar’s Office about whether
a new course proposal is needed or if an edit to an existing course is preferred.*

In the '**Justification and Resources'** section explain why the course is being created and answer the questions as to how
this course may affect other departments/colleges, faculty, and/or resources. Also,
if any letter(s) of support are needed, attach them here.

title: Creating a New Course and a New Cross-list Course in CIM
text:
A tentative course syllabus that follows the  standard syllabus template  will need to be attached. ***Please Note:** The question below concerning UG and GR level expectations will only appear on the
form if the proposed course number is 500-699. The Terminal course question will only
appear on the form if the proposed course number is 500+.*

The **General Education** question is ‘No’ by default.  If this course is seeking General Education status,
then toggle this answer over to ‘Yes’.

Toggling over to ‘Yes’ will open up several specific General Education questions.
You will need to fill out all of the required text boxes.

### Step 6: Start Workflow

Once you have filled out the entire course proposal form, you will want to start the
proposal through the workflow approval process by clicking the green **‘Start Workflow’** button.

# Creating a New Special Topics Lettered Course in CIM

# Creating a New Special Topic/Lettered Course

This is for when you want to propose a brand new special topic course under an approved
root course.

## Accessing the Dashboard

Using any web browser except Internet Explorer, go to the **CourseLeaf (CAT, CIM, CLSS) Resources page** ( https://wichita.edu/courseleaf ) and click the gold ***CourseLeaf Dashboard*** button link:

## Accessing Course Inventory Management

Once in the Dashboard, click on the ***Course Management (CIM)*** Module Card to be taken to the Course Inventory Management system.

## Creating a New Course and Cross-Listed Course Steps

### Step 1: Opening New Proposal Form

In the Course Inventory Management system, click on the green ***Propose New Course***button:

A new course proposal form will open.

### Step 2: Contact and Action Information

title: Creating a New Special Topics Lettered Course in CIM
text:
Fill out the contact information with the faculty member that can answer questions
about this course.  (Administrative assistants may be the one creating the proposal
but the faculty member that requested this should be listed as the contact person.)

Check the New Letter under Approved Root Course option under applicable actions:

If a Root Course does not yet exist for the Letter course you are wanting to create,
then a Root Course will need to be created in CIM and sent through workflow on a separate
proposal. Follow the same steps as Creating a New Course but select 'NEW Root Course'
instead of 'NEW course'.

**Helpful Information as you move through the form:**

title: Creating a New Special Topics Lettered Course in CIM
text:
- Answers provided on this form affect the electronic workflow approval process.  For
example, checking the box for ‘New Course’ starts a different workflow than checking
the box for ‘New Letter under Approved Root Course’.  In addition, the workflow is
constantly changing as you specify/change information.  For example, selecting ‘Yes’
for ‘Does this course have a service-learning component’ adds the Service-Learning
Coordinator to the approval process.
- Now that you are inside the proposal form the blue question marks represent WSU-specific
help:
- If you start a proposal but can’t finish it right now simply scroll to the bottom
of the form and click the ***Save Changes*** button.  When you are ready to return to this proposal you can use the same links
as above to access CIM.  Then, search for the course, select it, and click the ***Edit Course*** button:

title: Creating a New Special Topics Lettered Course in CIM
text:
### Step 3: Course Information

**Effective Term** - New courses can be given any effective term that is not a past term.***Please note:**  If the term selected is over or close to over once the course proposal reaches the
end of workflow, then the effective term will be moved to the next term by the Registrar’s
Office.*

**Subject** – Select the subject of the new special topic/lettered course.

**Course Number** - All special topic course numbers end in a letter or two letters. Do not use the
letter ‘L’ which is reserved for labs or ‘H’ which is reserved for honors courses. 
Type in the number of the Approved Root Course that the new special topic course will
fall under and then add the next available letter(s).  If you do not know what letters
are available, click on the grey ***Course Numbers in Use*** button after you fill in the ***Subject*** field.

title: Creating a New Special Topics Lettered Course in CIM
text:
Make sure to fill out all of the required information for the course.  Red fields
are required fields.

You are responsible for filling out the three boxes related to credit hour: **Credit Hour Limit, Lecture Hours** and **Lab Hours**.

**Credit Hour Limit** is the number of hours for which a course can be offered. Please use whole numbers
only (3, not 3.0), unless you are proposing a half credit hour course (.5). If the
course has a credit hour range, enter with dash (1-6).

**Lecture Hours** will be the same as Credit Hour Limit unless the course is Lab only.

If Lecture carries the credit, **Lab Hours** will be 0. If Lab carries the credit, Lecture Hours will be 0.

title: Creating a New Special Topics Lettered Course in CIM
text:
The **Repeatable for credit** question will automatically be marked as ‘No’.  However, if the new course is repeatable
for credit, toggle this answer over to ‘Yes’.  ***Note:** all courses can be repeated for grade replacement.  This question relates to if this
course be taken more than once for credit.*

If there is a limit to the number of times that the course can be repeated for credit,
check the **Limit**box and fill in the **Limit**field with the total credit hours that a student can earn by repeating the course.

If there is no limit, check the **No Limit** box.

Select all of the appropriate items for **Grading Mode, Planned Delivery Method**, and **Course Format**. More than one answer can be selected for **Planned Delivery Method**. Only select one answer for **Course Format**.

title: Creating a New Special Topics Lettered Course in CIM
text:
A **Catalog Description** (aka course description) is required for every course. This description must be in
third-person, present tense and no longer than one paragraph. Do not include text
for general education, cross-listing, prerequisites, or corequisites. The system will
add this information to the description when it syncs with Banner based on what you
have in other fields on the form.

If the course requires a **Prerequisite, Prerequisite with Concurrency**, or **Corequisite**, fill out the appropriate box.

If applicable, list any **Restrictions**with the course. Examples of restrictions include: course limited to specific major,
course limited to specific class (freshman, sophomore, etc.), course limited to specific
college, etc.

title: Creating a New Special Topics Lettered Course in CIM
text:
The questions for **service-learning** and **capstone**will automatically be marked as ‘No’. If the course does contain service-learning
or is a capstone course, toggle the answer over to ‘Yes’. **Note**: additional fields will open and need to be filled out for the service-learning component.

To add a **Cross-List** to your course, click on ***Add***. A box will open which will allow you to select subject, number, division, and general
education category (if applicable):

If this course is meant to replace another, select ‘Yes’.

You will be asked to enter the course that is being replaced and whether or not the
two courses are equivalent. ***Please note:** if the courses are equivalent, then check with the Registrar’s Office about whether
a new course proposal is needed or if an edit to an existing course is preferred.*

title: Creating a New Special Topics Lettered Course in CIM
text:
In the ***Justification and Resources*** section explain why the course is being created and answer the questions as to how
this course may affect other departments/colleges, faculty, and/or resources. Also,
if any letter(s) of support are needed, attach them here.

A tentative course syllabus that follows the  standard syllabus template  will need to be attached. ***Please Note:** The question below concerning UG and GR level expectations will only appear on the
form if the proposed course number is 500-699. The Terminal course question will only
appear on the form if the proposed course number is 500+.*

The **General Education** question is ‘No’ by default.  If this course is seeking General Education status,
then toggle this answer over to ‘Yes’.

title: Creating a New Special Topics Lettered Course in CIM
text:
Toggling over to ‘Yes’ will open up several specific General Education questions.
You will need to fill out all of the required text boxes.

### Step 4: Start Workflow

Once you have filled out the entire course proposal form, you will want to start the
proposal through the workflow approval process by clicking the green ***Start Workflow*** button.

title: Inactivating a Course in CIM
text:
# Inactivating a Course in CIM

# Inactivating a Course

This is for when you want to inactivate an existing course or a cross-listed pair
or group. Inactivated courses can be reactivated later. ***Please note:** If the course you select to inactivate is cross-listed with other courses, all courses
in the cross-listed pair or group will be inactivated. If the course being inactivated
is listed as a prerequisite of another course and/or listed on a program, then the
other course and/or program will need to be edited as well.*

## Accessing the Dashboard

Using any web browser except Internet Explorer, go to the **CourseLeaf (CAT, CIM, CLSS) Resources page** ( https://wichita.edu/courseleaf ) and click the gold ***CourseLeaf Dashboard*** button link:

## Accessing Course Inventory Management

title: Inactivating a Course in CIM
text:
Once in the Dashboard, click on the Course Management (CIM) Module Card to be taken
to the Course Inventory Management system.

## Inactivating a Course Steps

### Step 1: Finding Course to Inactivate

In the Course Inventory Management system, search for the course you want to inactivate.
In the search field, type in the subject and number of the course (i.e. HIST 101)
or you can search for all courses within a subject.  You can also use asterisks to
search for all courses that contain specific words in the course code or title.

 
Once you have found the course you wish to inactivate, click on it to select it and
then click on the red **‘Inactivate’** button. This will open a separate window for the inactivation proposal.

### Step 2: Effective Term

title: Inactivating a Course in CIM
text:
In the **‘These changes are effective’** field select the term that you want to inactivate the course. ***Please Note:** Courses cannot be inactivated during a term that there are active sections for that
course.*

### Step 3: Justification

In the **‘Justification for this request’** field explain why the course is being inactivated. If you have supporting documents
for the inactivation of the course, you can attach them to the proposal as well.

### Step 4: Start Workflow

Once you have filled out the inactivation proposal form, you will want to start the
proposal through the electronic workflow approval process by clicking the green **‘Start Workflow’** button.

title: Inactivating a Cross-listed Pair or Group of Courses in CIM
text:
# Inactivating a Cross-listed Pair or Group of Courses in CIM

# Inactivating a Cross-Listed Pair or Group of Courses

This is for when you want to inactivate all courses in a cross-listed pair or group.
 Inactivated courses can be reactivated later. ***Please Note:** If the course being inactivated is listed as a prerequisite of another course and/or
listed on a program, then the other course and/or program will need to be edited as
well.*

**IMPORTANT: Cross-listed Courses**

title: Inactivating a Cross-listed Pair or Group of Courses in CIM
text:
- Cross-listed courses are maintained on one CIM form. Changes made on the one proposal
form affect all of the cross-listed courses in the pair or group.
- Each cross-list pair or group has one primary course and one or more secondary courses.
Normally, the primary course is the course within the department teaching the course.
- The *primary course* will be the main course on the CIM form. On the search screen, if you scroll down
to preview the course information you will see that the Subject, Department, Unabbreviated
Course Title, etc. all relate to the primary course.
- The *secondary course(s)* is/are listed on the search screen as **‘Also listed as’**.
- Searching for either the primary or secondary course(s) will result in the same proposal.

## Accessing the Dashboard

title: Inactivating a Cross-listed Pair or Group of Courses in CIM
text:
Using any web browser except Internet Explorer, go to the **CourseLeaf (CAT, CIM, CLSS) Resources page** ( https://wichita.edu/courseleaf ) and click the gold ***CourseLeaf Dashboard*** button link:

## Accessing Course Inventory Management

Once in the Dashboard, click on the Course Management (CIM) Module Card to be taken
to the Course Inventory Management system.

## Inactivating a Cross-Listed Pair Steps

### Step 1: Finding Course to Inactivate

In the Course Inventory Management system, search for either the primary or secondary
cross-listed course in the pair or group you want to inactivate. In the search field,
type in the subject and number of the course (i.e. POLS 121H) or you can search by
the course title. You can use asterisks to search for all courses that contain specific
words in the course code or title.

title: Inactivating a Cross-listed Pair or Group of Courses in CIM
text:
Once you have found one of the courses in the cross-listed pair or group that you
wish to inactivate, click on it to select it and then click on the red **‘Inactivate’** button. This will open a separate window for the inactivation proposal.

### Step 2: Effective Term

In the **‘These changes are effective’** field select the term that you want to inactivate the course. ***Please Note:** Courses cannot be inactivated during a term that there are active sections for that
course.*

***Note:** Only the primary cross-listed course is shown on the proposal but ALL secondary cross-listed
courses will also be inactivated by this one proposal.*

### Step 3: Justification

In the **‘Justification for this request’** field explain why the courses are being inactivated. If you have supporting documents
for the inactivation of the courses, you can attach them to the proposal as well.

title: Inactivating a Cross-listed Pair or Group of Courses in CIM
text:
### Step 4: Start Workflow

Once you have filled out the inactivation proposal form, you will want to start the
proposal through the electronic workflow approval process by clicking the green **‘Start Workflow’** button.

title: General Education Learning Outcomes
text:
# General Education Learning Outcomes

# General Education Learning Outcomes

Copy the sample table below and paste it into your syllabus <tell them where to place
it>. Edit the Assignments/Activities column to identify which components in your class
achieve each of the learning outcomes in your syllabus. Edit the remaining columns<headings?>
to match your course content then check the boxes for which outcomes these assignments
address. **Attach your completed syllabus to the CIM proposal.**

title: General Education Learning Outcomes
text:
***Note:** Learning outcomes focus on student behavior and use simple, specific action verbs
to describe what students are expected to demonstrate. Measurable learning outcomes
are required in all types of courses. Bloom’s taxonomy provides a strong framework
for writing learning outcomes with action verbs that are measurable.*  Example: https://www.utica.edu/academic/Assessment/new/Blooms%20Taxonomy%20-%20Best.pdf 

## General Education Basic Skills Learning Outcomes

*Upon successful completion of this course, students should be able to:*

1. Have acquired knowledge in the arts, humanities, natural and social sciences
2. Think critically and independently
3. Write and speak effectively
4. Employ analytical reasoning and problem-solving techniques

## Disciplinary Learning Outcomes

These outcomes are developed by the instructor based on the unique disciplinary content
of the course.

title: General Education Learning Outcomes
text:
*Upon successful completion of this course, students should be able to:*

1. First outcome
2. Second outcome, etc.

title: Approving Proposals in CAT, CIM or CLSS
text:
# Approving Proposals in CAT, CIM or CLSS

# How to Edit or Approve Proposals in CAT, CIM or CLSS

This is for workflow approvers who need to review and approve proposals for courses,
programs, schedules or miscellaneous admin requests in their queue.

## Accessing the Dashboard

Using any web browser except Internet Explorer, go to the CourseLeaf (CAT, CIM, CLSS)
Resources page ( https://wichita.edu/courseleaf ) and click the ***CourseLeaf Dashboard*** button link:

## Your Approval Queue: The Workflow Tab

When the CourseLeaf Dashboard window opens, proposals in your queue will not be immediately
visible. This is due to the page defaulting to the ***Items*** tab. You will need to click on the ***Workflow*** tab to view your queue.

title: Approving Proposals in CAT, CIM or CLSS
text:
The ***Workflow*** tab will automatically filter for your role. If you have multiple roles in the CourseLeaf
system (CAT, CIM, CLSS), then all of your roles will be selected and any items in
those queues will appear in the list (note the different role names in the Approver
column).

***Please Note:** If there are no items for you to approve, then nothing will appear under the **Workflow** tab.*

To filter only for a specific role, leave the role you want to view alone and click
on the ***X*** by any of the role names in the grey bubbles to remove that role.

To add back any of the roles, search for it under the Role drop-down list, and click
on the role you wish to view. Only roles with something in the queue will appear in
the drop-down.

title: Approving Proposals in CAT, CIM or CLSS
text:
Proposals can also be filtered by type and term. Use the ***Type*** filter to view only programs, courses, catalog pages, or schedule items. Use the
***Term*** filter to view items with a specific effective term.

***Please Note:** Any filters selected are added to the filters already applied.* You will need to click on the ***X*** of any filter you wish to remove. The system will not automatically remove any filters.

## Reviewing Proposals

Click on any of the proposals to view it.  A preview screen will pop up with the entire
proposal:

Red text with a line through it indicates current information that someone is proposing
to have removed or changed with this proposal.  The green text indicates new information
being proposed with this proposal.

The ***Justification and Resources*** section describes in full the changes being requested:

title: Approving Proposals in CAT, CIM or CLSS
text:
At the very bottom of the proposal, be sure to read any ***Reviewer Comments*** left by previous approvers:

## Editing Proposals

Before approving the proposal, click the ***Edit*** button in the top of the ***Preview Screen***:

This will open the edit form of the proposal in a new window. Review the full proposal,
make any necessary changes and, if necessary, fill in the ***Reviewer Comments*** field at the bottom of the form. Be sure to click the ***Save Changes*** button at the bottom when finished:

The edit window will close, and you will be back at the ***Preview Screen*** on the Dashboard.

## Approving Proposals

If you are ready to approve this proposal, click the green ***Approve*** button in the top right of the proposal ***Preview Screen***:

title: Approving Proposals in CAT, CIM or CLSS
text:
If you’d like to confirm that this proposal has left your queue and has moved on to
the next approval step in workflow, you can refresh the Dashboard, re-select the ***Workflow***tab, and confirm that this proposal is no longer showing in the ***Pages Pending Approval*** section.

***Please Note:** Refreshing the Dashboard will reset the filters under the **Workflow** tab.*

## Rolling Back Proposals

If you need to send the proposal back to the person that submitted it or anyone in
a prior workflow approval step for edits before approving it, you can click the red
***Rollback*** button:

title: Approving Proposals in CAT, CIM or CLSS
text:
A new window will appear on the right side of the proposal ***Preview Screen*** allowing you to select whom you would like to roll the proposal back to.  You can
select any previous approver in the workflow or the initiator of the proposal.  You
are also required to provide a comment/reason for the rollback:

**Please Note:**

title: Approving Proposals in CAT, CIM or CLSS
text:
- The first person in the rollback list is the ‘initiator’ who submitted the proposal
to workflow initially. Rolling a proposal back to this person will roll the proposal
completely out of workflow and it will need to be resubmitted to workflow once any
necessary edits are made.
- Whomever you choose to roll it back to will need to make the necessary edits and then
all subsequent approvers in the list, who have already approved the proposal, will
have to reapprove it with these new edits.
- The comment you enter will stay with this proposal in history forever in the ***Reviewer Comments*** section at the bottom of the proposal and will be viewable by everyone.

## Additional Features in the Preview Screen

### PRINT the Proposal:

Click on the printer icon:

### HIDE the Current Information:

title: Approving Proposals in CAT, CIM or CLSS
text:
Click the drop-down next to the ***Filter by*** field. Select ***Hide Changes*** so the proposal only shows the proposed information.  This eliminates the current
information in red strikethrough from showing.  The new proposed information will
still show but it won’t be in green.  To view the red/green markup once again, select
***All Changes*** from the same drop-down.

### View Changes by a Specific Person:

Click the drop-down next to the ***Filter by*** field to select someone:

### Export the Proposal:

You can export the proposal in either PDF or Word format by clicking on the corresponding
button.  The PDF format is suggested.

title: Inactivating a Secondary Course in a Cross-listed Pair or Group in CIM
text:
# Inactivating a Secondary Course in a Cross-listed Pair or Group in CIM

# Inactivating a Secondary Cross-Listed Course

This is for when you want to inactivate a secondary course in a cross-listed pair
or group but leave the primary course active.

**IMPORTANT: Cross-listed Courses**

title: Inactivating a Secondary Course in a Cross-listed Pair or Group in CIM
text:
- Cross-listed courses are maintained on one CIM form. Changes made on the one proposal
form affect all of the cross-listed courses in the pair or group.
- Each cross-list pair or group has one primary course and one or more secondary courses.
Normally, the primary course is the course within the department teaching the course.
- The *primary course* will be the main course on the CIM form. On the search screen, if you scroll down
to preview the course information you will see that the Subject, Department, Unabbreviated
Course Title, etc. all relate to the primary course.
- The *secondary course(s)* is/are listed on the search screen as **‘Also listed as’**.
- Searching for either the primary or secondary course(s) will result in the same proposal.

## Accessing the Dashboard

title: Inactivating a Secondary Course in a Cross-listed Pair or Group in CIM
text:
Using any web browser except Internet Explorer, go to the **CourseLeaf (CAT, CIM, CLSS) Resources page** ( https://wichita.edu/courseleaf ) and click the gold ***CourseLeaf Dashboard*** button link:

## Accessing Course Inventory Management

Once in the Dashboard, click on the Course Management (CIM) Module Card to be taken
to the Course Inventory Management system.

## Inactivating a Secondary Cross-Listed Course Steps

### Step 1: Finding Course to Inactivate

In the Course Inventory Management system, search for the course you want to inactivate.
In the search field, type in the subject and number of the course (i.e. CJ 324 or
SOC 323) or you can search by the course title.  ***Please Note:** When searching for cross-listed courses, you can search for either the primary or
secondary course and the same CIM form will appear.*

title: Inactivating a Secondary Course in a Cross-listed Pair or Group in CIM
text:
Once you have found the CIM form with the course that you wish to inactivate, click
on it to select it and then click on the green **'Edit Course'** button. This will open a separate window for the course proposal.

### Step 2: Contact and Action Information

Fill out the contact information with the faculty member that can answer questions
about this course.  (Administrative assistants may be the one creating the proposal
but the faculty member that requested this should be listed as the contact person.)

Check the **‘Other’** option under applicable actions and type in something like ‘inactivating cross-listed
course, CJ 324’.

### Step 3: Effective Term

You will need to select an effective term for this inactivation. ***Please Note:** You cannot inactivate a course which has active sections. So, you will need to select
a future term where sections of the course do not exist.*

title: Inactivating a Secondary Course in a Cross-listed Pair or Group in CIM
text:
### Step 4: Removing/Inactivating Secondary Course

Note that the information in the Subject, Department, Unabbreviated Course Title,
etc. fields relate to the *primary course*. Scroll down the form to find the **‘Cross-Listed’** area which is located just above the **Justification and Resources** section.

To inactivate the secondary course, click on the red **‘Remove’** link next to the course in the **Cross-listed area**:

### Step 5: Remaining Sections of Proposal

Most of the required fields on the form should already be filled out on the proposal.
**Review all the information and make any edits as needed.**

title: Inactivating a Secondary Course in a Cross-listed Pair or Group in CIM
text:
The **Justification and Resources** section will not be filled out. And so, you will need to explain why you are inactivating
the secondary course and answer the questions as to how this may affect other departments/colleges,
faculty, and/or resources. Also, if any letter(s) of support are needed, attach them
here.

A course syllabus that follows the standard syllabus template will need to be attached. ***Please Note:** The question below concerning UG and GR level expectations will only appear on the
form if the proposed course number is 500-699. The Terminal course question will only
appear on the form if the proposed course number is 500+.*

### Step 7: Start Workflow

Once you have reviewed, updated, and filled out the entire course proposal form, you
will want to start the proposal through the electronic workflow approval process by
clicking the green **‘Start Workflow’** button.
